The board also amended the bylaws' Independent Director independence criteria, effective at Nasdaq trading commencement. No price, stake or transaction terms are involved; this is a listing-venue migration, not a corporate event, with no arbitrage angle.

ELVN.brief: Enliven Therapeutics filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement for a public offering of 8,933,334 common shares and pre-funded warrants for 1,733,333 shares at $37.50/$37.499 per unit. The total proceeds are ~$376 million before expenses. Shares are offered via underwriters including Jefferies and Goldman Sachs, with a 30-day greenshoe for up to 1,600,000 additional shares. This capital raise is a primary share issuance—a capital return event. The offering closes June 15, 2026. Watch for potential dilution and market reaction; no risk-arb angle as this is a straight equity financing.

ODD.brief: ODDITY Tech filed a Form 6-K furnishing its second-quarter 2026 earnings press release, headlined by capital-return actions and an operating update. The company repurchased ~5.6 million Class A ordinary shares for ~$80 million in Q2 2026 under a $200 million buyback plan authorized March 2026, and retired $50 million principal of zero-coupon 2030 exchangeable notes. Year-to-date repurchases total ~11.7 million shares for ~$163 million, cutting shares outstanding ~20%; ~$87 million remains authorized. Q2 net revenue was $181 million, down ~25% year-over-year; cash and investments were $561 million. Watch buyback execution pace and IL MAKIAGE advertising-algorithm normalization.

BNY.company: Bank of New York Mellon Corp
BNY.brief: The Bank of New York Mellon Corp filed an 8-K announcing a 19% increase in its quarterly cash dividend from $0.53 to $0.63 per share, expected to commence in Q3 2026 pending board approval. The filing also notes that the company's Stress Capital Buffer remains at the 2.5% floor following the 2026 Fed stress test, and that it continues to be authorized for share repurchases under an existing program announced in April 2026. Repurchases may occur via open market, private transactions, or structured programs. No advisor or recommendation is noted. This is a shareholder return event, not a merger or acquisition. Watch for dividend declaration and actual buyback execution.

FBLA.brief: FB Bancorp, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a third stock repurchase program authorizing up to 1,606,837 shares, or 10% of outstanding common stock. The program will be conducted on the open market, potentially via a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan, with no set price or premium. The board has not named an advisor. This follows completion of two prior programs repurchasing 1,983,750 and 1,785,375 shares respectively. The repurchase is discretionary and can be suspended at any time. Watch for execution pace and market conditions; no risk-arb angle as it is a pure capital return initiative.

IBCP.brief: Independent Bank Corp (IBCP) filed an 8-K reporting that HCB Financial Corp shareholders approved the merger agreement dated March 18, 2026, in which IBCP will acquire HCB. The all-stock deal is expected to close July 1, 2026, pending customary conditions. No per-share price, premium, or advisors were disclosed. The filing notes Rule 425 communications. Watch for regulatory approvals and the closing mechanics; the narrow spread to close suggests low risk-arb opportunity.

MVIS.brief: MicroVision filed an 8-K reporting receipt on August 26, 2026 of a Nasdaq Listing Qualifications notice confirming regained compliance with Listing Rule 5550(a)(2), the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement, and closing the matter. Noncompliance had been noticed January 12, 2026. The press release, dated August 31, 2026, quotes CEO Glen DeVos. The notice resolves a delisting overhang rather than a transaction; no price, stake, premium, advisor, or regulatory clock is stated. Watch for renewed sub-$1 trading that could restart a 180-day compliance clock and any reverse-split commentary.

MPWR.brief: Monolithic Power Systems filed an 8-K reporting its 2026 annual meeting voting results and declared a regular quarterly cash dividend of $2.00 per share. The dividend will be paid on July 15, 2026, to shareholders of record as of June 30, 2026. This is a routine capital return event with no premium, merger, or activist involvement. The company is returning capital to shareholders in the ordinary course. No special situation or extraordinary corporate event is present. Watch for any future changes in dividend policy or special dividends.

TYL.brief: Tyler Technologies filed an 8-K on September 15, 2026, disclosing entry into a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan with a brokerage firm to repurchase up to $260.0 million of common stock. Repurchases may begin September 16, 2026, and end October 29, 2026. The plan sits under board authorizations of $1.0 billion (February 3, 2026) and an added $1.5 billion (July 24, 2026), leaving $1.416 billion available. No price per share, premium, or advisor is stated; funding comes from cash and credit facility borrowings. Watch execution pace and any acceleration signals.

ADSK.brief: Autodesk filed an 8-K on August 3, 2026, disclosing completion of its acquisition of MaintainX Inc. The deal was executed pursuant to the Agreement and Plan of Merger dated May 28, 2026, among Autodesk, its wholly-owned subsidiary Matterhorn Acquisition Corp., MaintainX, and Shareholder Representative Services LLC as securityholders' agent. Terms such as price per share, total value, premium, and advisors were not disclosed. The merger structure involved a Delaware subsidiary merging with MaintainX. This filing is a closing notice. What to watch: integration execution and any earnout or stock consideration mechanics, though no further details were provided.

ENSG.brief: Ensign Group filed an 8-K disclosing a $60 million increase to its existing $40 million stock repurchase program, bringing total authorization to $100 million. The program allows open-market or privately negotiated repurchases under Rule 10b-18 and 10b5-1 plans. No price per share, premium, or expiration date was specified; repurchases are discretionary based on market conditions and liquidity. The board approved the increase on June 12, 2026, with no advisor named. The filing is a capital-return event, signaling management's view of undervaluation. Watch for actual buyback pace and potential EPS accretion as risk-arb angles.

FOXA.brief: Fox Corporation filed an 8-K reporting completion on November 6, 2026 of its previously announced acquisition of Roku, Inc. under a June 14, 2026 merger agreement using a two-step reverse triangular structure (Falcon Merger Sub 1 into Roku, then into Falcon Merger Sub 2, renamed Roku, LLC). Concurrently Fox amended and restated its term loan with Morgan Stanley as administrative agent, doubling commitments from $1.0 billion to $2.0 billion and permitting full cash netting. The filing also covers officer departures/appointments and Regulation FD disclosure. Watch integration execution, financing costs and any purchase-price or consideration details disclosed in exhibits.

IIPR.brief: Innovative Industrial Properties Inc., through its operating partnership, issued $402.5 million aggregate principal amount of 6.00% exchangeable senior notes due 2029 in a private placement under Rule 144A. The offering included full exercise of a $52.5 million greenshoe option. The notes are senior unsecured obligations guaranteed by the company, ranking equal with other unsecured debt. Proceeds may be used for general corporate purposes including capital returns. Interest is payable semiannually. Watch for future use of proceeds—if directed toward share buybacks or dividends, this would be a classic capital-return event.

KIM.brief: Kimco Realty OP, LLC filed an 8-K on June 15, 2026, solely to disclose the entry into a material definitive agreement for a preferred stock issuance. The filing details the terms of depositary shares representing 7.250% Class N Cumulative Convertible Perpetual Preferred Stock, along with Class L and Class M Cumulative Redeemable Preferred Stock. No specific price per share, premium, or conversion terms are provided in the excerpt. The agreement creates a direct financial obligation and an unregistered sale of equity securities. This is a routine capital-raising transaction through preferred equity, not a special situation. No advisors or board recommendations are noted, and the focus is on the operational funding of the REIT. Monitor for future pricing and conversion details.

NGS.brief: Natural Gas Services Group Inc. filed an 8-K reporting its acquisition of 100% of Flatrock Compression Holdings LLC. The consideration includes 241,803 shares of common stock plus $110 million in cash, subject to adjustments for cash, debt, net working capital, and transaction expenses. Sellers also receive contingent royalty payments under a separate Royalty Agreement. A $2.25 million cash escrow secures post-closing adjustments. The transaction closed simultaneously with execution on June 12, 2026. The representations and warranties do not survive closing; recourse is via representation and warranty insurance. No break fee or premium disclosed. Watch for integration execution and royalty payment triggers.

NWSA.brief: News Corporation filed an 8-K (Items 8.01/9.01) on November 5, 2026, disclosing daily ASX-transparency notices tied to its existing stock repurchase program, under which it may acquire up to $1 billion in aggregate of Class A (NWSA) and Class B (NWS) common stock from time to time. The filing covers no new authorization or price terms and names no advisor; exhibits 99.1/99.2 are the ASX disclosures. Mechanics are open-market buybacks subject to market conditions and securities laws, flagged with standard forward-looking-statement caveats. Watch pace of executions versus the $1 billion authorization and any signal on buyback cadence.

NMRA.brief: Neumora Therapeutics filed an Item 3.01 8-K on October 26, 2026, disclosing a written notice from Nasdaq that the company is out of compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement under Listing Rule 5450(a)(1) for the Nasdaq Global Select Market. The company has 180 calendar days, until April 26, 2027, to regain compliance, requiring a closing bid of at least $1.00 for ten consecutive business days. Absent a cure, Neumora could apply to transfer to the Nasdaq Capital Market for additional time, subject to market-value and initial-listing standards plus an application fee. Management said it will monitor the bid and consider options including a reverse stock split. Watch remediation timing and any reverse-split announcement, which could introduce trading and structural risk for holders.

BANR.brief: Banner Corporation filed an 8-K announcing the closing of its merger with Pacific Financial Corporation, effective September 1, 2026. Under the Merger Agreement dated April 30, 2026, each Pacific Financial share converted into 0.2633 Banner shares, with Banner issuing about 2,654,563 shares. Bank of the Pacific also merged into Banner Bank, with Denise Portmann becoming EVP. No price per share or premium was disclosed. The transaction represents a completed stock-for-stock acquisition; risk-arb angle is moot post-closing, but integration execution and share issuance effects warrant monitoring.

AZO.brief: AutoZone filed an 8-K announcing its Board authorized an additional $1.5 billion in share repurchases under its ongoing buyback program, bringing total authorizations to $42.2 billion since 1998. No price per share or specific premium is given, as this is an open-market authorization. The program is discretionary and will be funded from free cash flow while maintaining credit ratings. No board recommendation, advisor, or regulatory clock applies. Watch for execution pace and potential impact on EPS, though no risk-arb angle exists as this is not a tender offer.

CCNE.brief: CNB Financial Corporation filed an 8-K on June 16, 2026 announcing the completion of a partial redemption of $50 million of its 3.25% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Subordinated Notes due 2031. The redemption occurred on June 15, 2026 at par plus accrued interest, leaving $35 million outstanding. This is a capital structure action reducing debt and future interest expense, with no premium or accretion. No board recommendation, advisor, or regulatory timeline is mentioned. Watch for potential further redemptions or balance sheet repositioning; the risk-arb angle is negligible as this is a unilateral issuer action.

CNTN.brief: Canton Strategic Holdings, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a share repurchase program approved by its board on June 11, 2026, authorizing up to $50 million of common stock repurchases. Repurchases may occur via open market or privately-negotiated transactions under Rule 10b-18. The company entered into a non-exclusive repurchase agreement with Virtu Americas LLC on June 12, 2026, paying $0.02/share commission. The program’s timing and amount depend on capital resources, market conditions, and securities law limits. Watch for execution pace and impact on share price.

MXCT.brief: MaxCyte, Inc. reported in an 8-K filed June 16, 2026, that it received notice from Nasdaq on June 10, 2026, confirming the company regained compliance with the minimum bid price rule (Listing Rule 5450(a)(1)). The closing bid price remained at or above $1.00 for 10 consecutive business days from May 27 to June 9, 2026. The delisting matter is now closed. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or deal terms were disclosed. No activist or new campaign is involved. Investors should monitor stock price maintenance above $1.00 to avoid future non-compliance.

NN.brief: Nasdaq Stock Market LLC filed Form 25-NSE to delist warrants of NextNav Inc. (CIK 0001865631) under 17 CFR 240.12d2-2(a)(1). The delisting is effective June 26, 2026, removing the warrants from Nasdaq listing. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or transaction structure was disclosed. The filing is a standard administrative action for security removal. What to watch: whether the warrants will trade over-the-counter or if a separate corporate event (e.g., merger) triggered the delisting; risk-arb angle is minimal as no tender or exchange offer is involved.

RXT.brief: Rackspace Technology filed an 8-K disclosing a workforce realignment plan approved by its Executive Committee on June 10, 2026. The plan eliminates approximately 15% of the global workforce, targeting legacy Public Cloud delivery functions to redeploy resources toward enterprise AI. One-time charges of $14-$19 million are expected in 2026, with annualized run-rate savings of $75-$85 million. Notice was given on or about June 10; additional exits occur over six months. The company may implement further operational optimization measures. Watch actual savings relative to estimates, reinvestment pace into AI, and any future restructuring announcements.

DKS.brief: DICK'S Sporting Goods filed an S-4/A registration statement for an exchange offer to swap up to $381,932,000 of its 4.000% Senior Notes due 2029. The company is offering to exchange any and all outstanding notes issued September 11, 2025 for registered notes with substantially identical terms. The exchange is intended to satisfy registration rights obligations. There is no board recommendation, advisor, premium, or change in economic terms. The exchange is not conditioned on a minimum tender. The deal mechanics involve a like-for-like principal exchange with no cash consideration. No regulatory clock applies beyond SEC effectiveness. What to watch: execution risk is minimal; the arbitrage angle is absent as this is a registration rights exchange with no price dislocation.

ELTX.brief: Elicio Therapeutics filed an 8-K (Item 8.01, Other Events) on June 17, 2026, attaching a press release that reports preliminary clinical observations from its Phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P study. The release highlights three metastatic pancreatic cancer patients who achieved complete radiographic and metabolic responses after receiving ELI-002 7P followed by nivolumab-based therapy. This is a clinical development update with no deal terms, transaction, or special-situation corporate event. The filing discloses no financial terms, board recommendation, or imminent structural change. The company plans a Phase 1 study in first-line metastatic KRAS-mutant pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, subject to funding. The press release serves as the sole exhibit. No special-situation categorization applies; the filing is a routine clinical update.

GENC.brief: Gencor Industries filed an 8-K (Item 3.01) disclosing it received a NYSE American notice on May 19, 2026, for failing to timely file its Q1 2026 10-Q by the May 18, 2026 extension deadline, triggering a six-month cure period. On June 12, 2026, the company filed the delinquent 10-Q within that period. On June 15, 2026, NYSE confirmed compliance was regained and removed the company from its late filers list. No board action, advisor, or premium was involved. Risk-arb watch: this delisting risk is now resolved, removing a potential overhang on the stock.

HLIT.brief: Harmonic Inc. filed an 8-K announcing the completion of the sale of its Video Business to Leone Media Inc. (d/b/a MediaKind) for $145 million in cash. The purchase price is subject to customary working capital, cash, indebtedness, and selling expense adjustments. The Asset Purchase Agreement, dated March 20, 2026, includes a three-year non-compete and reciprocal indemnification. Neven Haltmayer, SVP and GM of the Video Business, resigned upon closing. No board recommendation or advisor is named. Pro forma financials were omitted as the business was previously reported as discontinued operations. What to watch: integration execution by MediaKind and Harmonic's post-divestiture strategy; risk-arb is limited as the deal is closed.

MAC.brief: Macerich filed an 8-K on June 29, 2026, announcing the full exercise of the underwriters' 30-day option to purchase an additional 2,100,000 shares of common stock at $23.12325 per share, under an underwriting agreement dated June 15, 2026. The company entered into additional forward sale agreements with forward purchasers to borrow and sell the option shares. Closing occurred June 26, 2026. Proceeds depend on future physical settlement of the forward agreements, expected by June 16, 2027. The company may elect cash or net share settlement. This is a capital-raising equity forward transaction, not a special situation.

NEO.brief: NeoGenomics, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a civil settlement with the DOJ on behalf of OIG-HHS regarding an internal investigation into compliance of consulting agreements with federal healthcare laws. The settlement requires a payment of $9,813,260, which is below the previously accrued reserve of $11.2 million. The filing is a regulatory disclosure of a legal resolution, not a special situation such as an acquisition, divestiture, or activist campaign. The settlement does not involve a change in control, restructuring, or capital return.

RIGL.brief: Rigel Pharmaceuticals filed an 8-K to report completion of an exclusive license agreement with Arvinas, Inc., Arvinas Operations, Inc., Arvinas Estrogen Receptor, Inc. and Pfizer Inc. as licensors. Under the deal, Rigel obtained exclusive global rights to develop, manufacture and commercialize VEPPANU (vepdegestrant) and related products. Rigel paid a one-time upfront payment of $70.0 million. The closing followed early termination of the HSR waiting period and satisfaction of other conditions. This is an asset acquisition via exclusive license. Watch for milestone or royalty terms, regulatory progress, and potential competitive dynamics in the targeted therapeutic area.

SPFI.brief: South Plains Financial, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the termination of its Board Representation Agreement with shareholder Henry TAW LP, effective June 17, 2026. The agreement had granted the shareholder the right to designate one board nominee. At origination in 2019, the shareholder held about 16% of outstanding shares; its stake has since fallen below 10%. The board believes termination aligns with the company's maturation as a widely-held public entity. Richard D. Campbell, the designated representative, will remain on the board through his current term and is expected to be renominated. This is a governance change, not a special situation event.

HAPN.brief: LendingClub Corp voluntarily delisted its common stock from the NYSE, filing Form 25 on June 18, 2026, under Rule 12d2-2(c). No tender offer or acquisition; the issuer itself initiated removal. No price, premium, or consideration terms given. The board did not name an advisor; the filing cites compliance with exchange rules. The delisting became effective upon filing. With no overhang or ownership changes, this is a purely administrative event. Watch for any subsequent SEC deregistration under Rule 12g-4 or potential going-private transaction; risk-arb is inapplicable.

ALIT.brief: Alight, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a reverse stock split and related charter amendments approved by stockholders at its June 10, 2026 annual meeting. The reverse stock split is 1-for-20 for Class A common stock, Class B non-voting common stock, and Class V common stock, effective June 29, 2026. A corresponding 1-for-20 reverse unit split of Alight Units in a subsidiary was also executed. The charter amendments also included board declassification and officer exculpation under DGCL Section 102(b)(7). This is an ordinary corporate action with no special situation dynamics; no deal consideration, premium, or stakeholder contest is involved. Watch for any subsequent stock price adjustment to the reverse split.

BCO.brief: Brink's filed an 8-K reporting a press release that the UK CMA accepted in principle its proposed remedy for the pending acquisition of NCR Atleos (NATL). The remedy is the divestiture of NoteMachine TestLink UK to address UK-specific competition concerns and avoid a CMA Phase 2 referral. The sale process, announced September 30, 2026, is progressing with multiple prospective buyers. Brink's expects the acquisition to close early in the first quarter of 2027. The filing is a regulatory milestone, not new deal terms; no price, premium, or break fee is stated. Watch for a definitive buyer, divestiture agreement, and any Phase 2 referral risk if the remedy is not concluded.

BAND.brief: Bandwidth Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the repurchase of approximately $20.8 million aggregate principal amount of its 0.50% Convertible Senior Notes due 2028 in open-market transactions at a discount to par, paying cash. This leaves about $6.7 million outstanding from an initial $250 million issuance. The company has capped call transactions in place expected to remain effective despite the repurchases. The repurchases reduce debt and potential dilution. What to watch: the impact on diluted share count and any further opportunistic repurchases given the small remaining balance.

CMTV.brief: Community Bancorp /VT filed an 8-K on June 17, 2026 announcing its Board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.25 per share, payable August 1, 2026 to holders of record July 15, 2026. The filing under Item 8.01 (Other Events) includes a press release as Exhibit 99.1. There are no deal terms, premium, or transaction mechanics; this is a routine dividend declaration with no change to corporate structure or capital return program. As a standard dividend announcement, it does not meet special-situation criteria.

ECHO.brief: EchoStar subsidiary DISH DBS emerged from prepackaged Chapter 11 on October 1, 2026, after the Bankruptcy Court confirmed its standalone plan on September 29; the DISH Wireless plan was bifurcated. Per the March 19, 2026 RSA, debt restructuring plus full repayment of the 7.75% 2026 notes and partial early repayment of the 5.25% secured notes cut DISH DBS debt by roughly $4.35 billion. DISH DBS, guarantors, Wilmington Savings Fund Society as successor trustee and U.S. Bank as collateral agent executed a secured notes supplemental indenture. Watch residual DISH Wireless proceedings, EchoStar guarantees and any intercompany or collateral leakage.

ESOA.brief: Energy Services of America filed an 8-K announcing an Asset Purchase Agreement with FAMCO, Inc., a West Virginia water and sewer utility contractor. Its new subsidiary, FAMCO Acquisition, Inc., will buy substantially all operating assets for a $6.95M base price. At closing, three-eighths is cash, one-half is ESOA common stock issued soon after closing, and one-eighth is withheld for a post-closing true-up. Closing is anticipated on or about October 9, 2026, subject to conditions. No board recommendation, advisor, break fee, or regulatory clock disclosed; watch closing mechanics and earn-out adjustments.

ENPH.brief: Enphase Energy filed an 8-K disclosing a Tax Credit Transfer Agreement to sell up to $150 million of Section 45X advanced manufacturing production tax credits to a leading financial institution for up to $139.5 million, payable in four installments through 2027. The agreement involves standard conditions precedent, covenants, indemnification, and termination provisions. This transaction monetizes tax credits generated from eligible component production in the US. As a non-deal special situation, it falls under 'Other' categories like tax credit sales. Watch for payment milestones and the company's ability to generate sufficient credits to fulfill the agreement.

OMER.brief: Omeros Corporation filed an 8-K reporting the repurchase and retirement of $30.5 million aggregate principal amount of its 9.50% Convertible Senior Notes due 2029 through privately negotiated agreements. The latest repurchase of approximately $14.5 million principal was completed on July 20, 2026, for $29.0 million total including accrued interest. Combined with a prior $16.0 million repurchase, $40.3 million in notes remain outstanding. The company directly reduced debt, with no board recommendation or advisors named. The transaction reduces future interest obligations and overhang. Watch for further opportunistic debt reduction or potential equity conversion dynamics.

TRAK.brief: ReposiTrak, Inc. filed an 8-K to report its acquisition of 4,709,837 shares of SPAR Group, Inc. common stock from William Bartels and WHB Services, Inc. Incentive Savings Plan and Trust for aggregate contingent consideration of approximately $3.3 million, comprising a $100,000 previously paid deposit, $139,883 and $485,118 cash payments, and a $2,571,885 unsecured promissory note bearing 6% interest, maturing July 1, 2030, with annual $725,000 principal installments. No board recommendation or advisors named. The note is prepayable without penalty, with customary default provisions. Watch for regulatory clearances and SPAR Group's response; risk-arb focus on note servicing and share delivery timing.

SRBK.brief: SR Bancorp, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on June 18, 2026, announcing its Board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.06 per share, a $0.01 or 20% increase from the prior dividend. The dividend will be paid on July 15, 2026 to shareholders of record as of June 30, 2026. As the issuer, the company highlights its earnings strength and commitment to shareholder value. No other special-situation mechanics (e.g., tender, restructuring, acquisition) are present. This is a routine dividend increase disclosure, thus classified under Capital Returns.

CERS.brief: Cerus Corporation filed a Form 8-K on June 8, 2026, reporting entry into a Second Amended and Restated Credit, Security and Guaranty Agreement (Term Loan) and a Second Amended and Restated Credit, Security and Guaranty Agreement (Revolving Loan) on June 5, 2026. These agreements amend and restate existing credit facilities with MidCap Financial Trust and MidCap Funding IV Trust. The Term Loan Credit Agreement provides a secured term loan facility of up to $65.0 million, with an initial $35.0 million draw to refinance existing term loans. Additional tranches up to $30.0 million are available for working capital and general corporate purposes. Interest is Term SOFR plus 5.50% (1.00% floor). Interest-only payments apply for 48 months then 12 months of amortization. No early termination fee after one year. This is a routine refinancing and credit facility amendment, not a special situation such as an acquisition, divestiture, or activist campaign.

CELC.brief: Celcuity Inc. filed a Form 8-K on September 30, 2026, furnishing a press release under Items 7.01 and 8.01 announcing that REVTORPYK (gedatolisib), its PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway inhibitor, is now commercially available in the United States for HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer without a detected PIK3CA mutation following progression on at least one line of endocrine therapy. The filing contains no transactional, ownership, or pricing terms; it is a routine commercial-launch and Regulation FD disclosure, not a merger, tender, spin-off, or activist event. No board recommendation, advisor, or deal mechanics are implicated; there is no risk-arb angle.

HUBB.brief: Hubbell Incorporated filed an 8-K announcing completion of its acquisition of NSI Electrical Buyer, Inc. (NSI Industries) for $3.0 billion in cash. The purchase was funded via a $900 million unsecured term loan, $1.9 billion in senior notes, and commercial paper. The target provides electrical fittings and wire management products for industrial, infrastructure, and commercial markets. All issued and outstanding shares were acquired from seller NSI Buyer, LP. Terms include customary cash, debt, working capital, and expense adjustments. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or break fee stated. The deal closed on June 9, 2026, with no further regulatory hurdles; watch integration progress and debt servicing.

INCY.brief: Incyte filed an 8-K under Items 8.01 and 9.01 announcing the completion of its acquisition of Vega Therapeutics, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Star Therapeutics LLC. The deal closed on July 6, 2026, with terms not disclosed. The acquisition adds VGA039, an anti-Protein S monoclonal antibody in Phase 3 for von Willebrand disease, to Incyte's hematology pipeline. No price, premium, board recommendation, advisors, or breakup fee were stated. The filing confirms consummation, not a new announcement. Watch for Phase 3 data readouts and potential label expansion, as VGA039 could be first-to-market for VWD prophylaxis. No risk-arb spread since terms are undisclosed.

AVO.brief: Mission Produce filed an 8-K furnishing an Investor Day press release and updated presentation (Items 7.01/8.01/9.01). The Item 8.01 disclosure confirms activity under the previously announced June 8, 2026 $100 million stock repurchase authorization, with 290,994 shares bought back fiscal Q4 to date at an average price of $12.94. Management unveiled five-year targets of mid-single-digit organic sales growth, 300 basis points of margin expansion, and a 2035 ambition to double sales and triple Adjusted EBITDA. No deal terms or advisors were disclosed; watch execution against buyback pace.

PDYN.brief: Palladyne AI Corp. filed an 8-K on June 8, 2026, announcing an MOU and posting a press release and investor presentation for an investor call on June 9, 2026. Reg FD disclosure suggests potential strategic initiatives, but no specific terms (price, premium, stake %) or definitive agreement were provided. The board recommendation and advisors were not named. The filing may indicate a strategic review or partnership exploration, but details are absent. Watch for updates from the investor call or subsequent filings for clarity on the MOU's implications.

SIG.brief: Signet Jewelers filed an 8-K under Item 8.01 disclosing an accelerated share repurchase (ASR) agreement, a US-style buyback mechanism, with JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. on September 10, 2026. Signet paid $125 million on September 11, 2026 and received an initial delivery of roughly 1,023,000 common shares. Final share count is based on daily volume-weighted average prices less a discount, with settlement expected between September 25 and December 2, 2026. About $575 million remains authorized under the 2017 program. Watch settlement adjustments, delivery direction risk, and buyback support for the stock.

SENS.brief: The filing is an 8-K reporting the closing of previously disclosed local asset purchases by Senseonics Holdings (acquirer) from Ascensia Diabetes Care Holdings (seller) of certain European Eversense CGM assets in Italy, Germany, Spain and Sweden, under a master asset purchase agreement dated Dec 31, 2025. No financial terms, price, or premium are disclosed. The closings occurred on June 1 and June 8, 2026, with an effective accounting date of June 1. The transaction appears to be a bolt-on asset acquisition, not a transformative M&A event. Watch for potential operational integration updates.

VRRM.brief: Verra Mobility Corporation filed an 8-K reporting that its Board formed a Transformation Committee on June 5, 2026, to oversee a transformation initiative. The committee will support management's review of business and financial strategies, cost optimization, growth opportunities, capital allocation, portfolio composition, financing, and capital expenditure plans, and make recommendations to the Board. The committee comprises Raj Ratnakar (chair), Douglas Davis, and John Rexford. No specific terms, premium, or advisor are disclosed. This is an early-stage strategic review. Watch for further updates on potential divestitures, restructuring, or capital allocation changes; no immediate risk-arb angle.

ATYR.brief: aTyr Pharma filed an 8-K reporting a mutual termination agreement with Kyorin Pharmaceutical, effective July 30, 2026, ending their collaboration and license agreement for efzofitimod in Japan. Kyorin had previously given 90-day notice of termination without cause on May 12, 2026; the Termination Agreement accelerated the end date and covered wind-down activities. All rights to develop and commercialize efzofitimod globally revert to aTyr, which now holds worldwide rights. No financial terms, payments, or change-of-control involve; this is purely a contract termination restoring rights. Watch for potential new partnerships or a global commercialization strategy for efzofitimod.

AX.brief: Axos Financial subsidiary Axos Bank closed its purchase of roughly $1.9 billion of Capital One individual retirement account deposits tied to savings and CD accounts. The parties signed a Purchase and Assumption Agreement on April 22, 2026, and the deal closed September 21, 2026. The bank paid cash for the aggregate deposit balance less a negotiated premium. No board recommendation or advisor is named, and no shareholder vote was required. The deposit transfer is a business-line asset purchase rather than a whole-company merger, so no target equity remains outstanding. Watch the negotiated premium and retention of the acquired IRA deposits.

BNAI.brief: Brand Engagement Network filed an 8-K (Item 8.01) updating expected cost reductions tied to integrating Cataneo GmbH, acquired June 30, 2026. Post-closing organizational actions (Phase II and III), authorized by the CEO in the ordinary course, carry one-time exit costs estimated near $177,000, mostly severance and notice pay, largely payable in the first half of 2027. Combined annualized savings across Phases I–III are now projected at roughly $1.919 million, mostly realized in 2027. No board recommendation, advisor, or price terms disclosed; watch severance timing and integration execution risk.

EVTC.brief: EVERTEC, Inc. filed an 8-K on August 4, 2026, reporting Q2 2026 results and announcing a Board-approved increase to its share repurchase authorization. The authorization was raised to permit up to an aggregate $150 million in future repurchases, with approximately $83 million previously remaining. The program allows open-market buys, accelerated share repurchases, Rule 10b5-1 plans, or privately negotiated transactions, expiring December 31, 2027. The company also raised its full-year 2026 outlook and signed strategic agreements with Transbank and Clip. This is a capital return event; watch for repurchase cadence and balance-sheet impact.

SLNH.brief: Soluna Holdings, Inc filed an 8-K reporting entry into a joint venture agreement for Project Kati 2, a multi-phase data center development in Texas. Soluna's subsidiary contributed property, a purchase agreement, and ~$3.5M in expenses, with a further ~$19M capital commitment and up to $2M for expenses. After recovering contributions and a 14% IRR plus $100K/MW, distributions are 50/50 with Metrobloks. This is a strategic operating JV, not a special situation. Watch for development milestones and capital calls.

SMCI.brief: Super Micro Computer, Inc. filed a 424B5 preliminary prospectus supplement for a $1.25B common stock offering (price to be determined; June 9, 2026 close $40.64). Concurrently, it is offering 75M depositary shares representing mandatory convertible preferred stock and plans a $2B ATM program. No board recommendation or advisor named. Proceeds will fund component purchases to fulfill ~$39B in AI server orders and for general corporate purposes. Closings are not conditioned on each other. Watch for pricing, overallotment option exercise, and impact from the concurrent financings on stock price.

CE.brief: New York Stock Exchange filed Form 25-NSE to delist the 4.777% Senior Notes Due 2026 guaranteed by Celanese Corp. The entire class of securities was called for redemption on June 25, 2026, with sufficient funds deposited and made available to holders. The delisting will be effective at the opening of business on July 6, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The filing is a routine administrative notice following full redemption; no structural or contest dynamics apply. The risk-arb angle is nil — all securities have been retired and paid.

JJSF.brief: J&J Snack Foods filed an 8-K regarding Amendment No. 2 to its credit agreement, extending the revolving facility maturity to 2031, increasing capacity by up to $200M (or EBITDA-based amount), and raising leverage ratio covenants. No acquisition, divestiture, or special situation event is announced; this is a routine credit facility amendment. The filing includes departure of a named officer (item 5.02), but no forced departure details are provided, and terms/advisor are absent. Watch for future acquisition use of the expanded facility.

MH.brief: McGraw Hill, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing its board approved a $50.0 million common stock repurchase plan on June 2, 2026, disclosed alongside fiscal Q4 and full-year results ended March 31, 2026. The buyback authorizes repurchases from time to time with no specific price, premium, or expiration terms set forth. The board authorized the plan; no external advisors or transaction mechanics are detailed. As a capital return to shareholders via open-market repurchases, this is a discretionary capital-allocation action. Watch for periodic repurchase disclosures and any impact on share float or EPS accretion.

PNRG.brief: PrimeEnergy Resources Corp filed an 8-K (Items 5.07, 8.01) on June 11, 2026, reporting annual meeting voting results and a board-authorized share repurchase program. The board authorized repurchase of up to 300,000 shares via open-market or privately negotiated transactions, at management's discretion, subject to market conditions and cash availability. No premium, expiration, or material terms were disclosed beyond authorization. The repurchase is a capital-return signal, reducing float and returning cash to shareholders. Watch for actual execution pace and any subsequent tender offers, as the open-market nature limits typical risk-arb precision.

STTK.brief: Shattuck Labs filed an 8-K disclosing an underwritten public offering of 10,879,376 shares at $4.00/share plus pre-funded warrants for 7,870,624 shares at $3.9999/share, with a full underwriter option for 2,812,500 additional shares exercised. Proceeds go to the issuer. No premium, recommendation, or advisor named; the offering was conducted under an effective shelf registration. The warrants are exercisable immediately with a 4.99%-19.99% beneficial ownership blocker. Expected close is June 11, 2026. Watch for dilution impact and potential share price drift post-closing.

VENU.brief: Venu Holding Corp filed an 8-K reporting the sale of approximately 9.5 acres of land underlying its Ford Amphitheater to O'Neil Roth Ford, LLC for $49.7 million, plus an adjacent 1.1-acre undeveloped parcel for $10.00. The buyer is co-owned by a shareholder and the CEO/Chairman, making it a related-party transaction. The sale is part of a sale-leaseback strategy to generate liquidity, with the purchase price set at an independent appraisal. No specific premium, close date beyond closing, or board recommendation is detailed. Watch for the leaseback terms and any related-party governance scrutiny.

WDC.brief: Western Digital filed an 8-K reporting privately negotiated exchange agreements with holders of its 3.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2028. Holders agreed to exchange approximately $191.0 million aggregate principal for about $192.7 million cash (principal plus accrued interest) plus common stock equal to remaining conversion value based on the August 26, 2026 VWAP. Exempt under Section 4(a)(2). Expected close on or after September 2, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor named. This is a liability-management transaction, essentially an issuer tender of convertible notes. Watch for settlement terms, potential dilution from stock issuance, and accounting impact on debt extinguishment.

XERS.brief: Xeris Biopharma filed an 8-K reporting privately negotiated exchange agreements with noteholders to exchange ~$23M (69%) of its 8.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2028 for cash (principal amount) plus common stock valued using a 21-day VWAP. $10.5M of notes will remain outstanding. Closing expected ~July 15, 2026. The exchange reduces debt overhang and is a form of capital return via liability management; shares issued will be unregistered under Section 4(a)(2). Watch for the VWAP calculation and remaining noteholder dynamics.

BFLY.brief: The New York Stock Exchange filed Form 25-NSE to delist the warrants of Butterfly Network, Inc., each exercisable for one share of Class A common stock at $11.50/share, due to abnormally low selling prices under Section 802.01D of the Listed Company Manual. Trading was suspended on January 14, 2026, and the company did not appeal, making delisting effective February 13, 2026. This is a regulatory removal, not a merger; the common stock remains listed. The delisting eliminates warrant overhang and liquidity. Watch for any potential impact on common shares or alternative venue trading.

CARE.brief: Carter Bankshares, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing the completed sale of its membership interest in Bearing Insurance Group, LLC to an unaffiliated third party, effective May 1, 2026. The estimated pre-tax gain is approximately $35.8 million, to be recognized in Q2 2026. No specific price per share, premium, or break fee was disclosed. The board did not issue a recommendation; the transaction closed on announcement. The filing provides no structural mechanics beyond the gain estimate. The closed nature means no regulatory clock remains; watch for subsequent earnings reports to confirm actual gain and potential redeployment of proceeds.

FRME.brief: First Merchants Corporation filed an 8-K disclosing board approval of a stock repurchase program for up to 3,125,000 shares (~5% of outstanding) with a $100M aggregate cap. Repurchases may occur via open market, private transactions, or Rule 10b5-1 plans at management's discretion, with no obligation to buy. The program replaces a March 2025 plan. No premium, price terms, or advisors are named. The mechanics allow flexible execution under Rule 10b-18. Watch share buyback pace and market conditions; risk-arb angle is minimal as this is a discretionary capital return, not a fixed tender.

LAZ.brief: Lazard, Inc. filed an 8-K to disclose its agreement to acquire all issued shares of Campbell Lutyens Holdings Limited, a private capital advisor. Total consideration is up to $660 million: $460 million initial (primarily in Lazard common stock at $46.50/share), $115 million deferred at two-year anniversary, and up to $85 million earn-out based on 2030 revenue targets. The transaction is expected to close with 100% ownership. Board supports the deal. Risk-arb focus: stock election mechanics, regulatory clearances, and earn-out achievability.

PB.brief: Prosperity Bancshares filed an 8-K announcing completion of its acquisition of Stellar Bancorp effective July 1, 2026. Each Stellar share was converted into 0.3803 Prosperity shares plus $11.36 cash, implying a total per-share consideration valued using a $71.44 reference price for Prosperity stock. Stellar stock options were cashed out based on the per-share merger consideration value. The merger was structured as a tax-free reorganization with Prosperity as the surviving entity, followed by a bank merger into Prosperity Bank. The deal closed with no disclosed regulatory hurdles; future updates may address integration milestones and accretion.

RICK.brief: RCI Hospitality Holdings disclosed on Form 8-K that it received a Nasdaq notice on May 20, 2026 for noncompliance with Listing Rule 5250(c)(1) due to failure to file its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026. The company has until July 20, 2026 to file or submit a compliance plan; Nasdaq may grant up to 180 days from the due date (November 16, 2026) to regain compliance. The notice has no immediate effect on the listing of RICK on the Nasdaq Global Market. Watch for the filing of the 10-Q or acceptance of a compliance plan; risk-arb impact is minimal as this is a procedural delisting notice.

QUBT.brief: Quantum Computing Inc. (QUBT) filed an 8-K reporting its acquisition of NHanced Semiconductors, Inc. via a Stock Purchase Agreement. Aggregate consideration comprises $68.1M cash (subject to adjustments) plus ~$5.0M in QUBT stock, with $20.0M of the cash held in escrow contingent on NHanced's 2027-2028 revenue thresholds. Additional earnout of up to $72.0M based on revenue and EBITDA targets is payable in cash or stock. No price per share or premium was disclosed. The board recommended the transaction; advisors are not named. Watch for QUBT's dilution and integration risk; earnout mechanics and potential stock issuance create complexity.

ATEN.brief: A10 Networks filed an 8-K on November 5, 2026, reporting Q3 results (quarter ended September 30, 2026) via press release and posted website slides under Items 2.02/7.01, alongside an Item 8.01 announcement that its Board of Directors approved a quarterly dividend of $0.06 per share. The dividend is payable December 1, 2026 to holders of record November 16, 2026, subject to possible prior revocation. No advisor or recommendation beyond Board approval is named. The Board retains discretion to adjust or withdraw future dividends as it reviews capital allocation; watch payout sustainability and any shift toward larger capital-return actions.

TECH.brief: Bio-Techne filed an 8-K updating its pending merger with Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany and EMD Holdings NewCo, Inc., under which Merger Sub will merge into Bio-Techne, leaving it a wholly-owned Merck subsidiary. The merger agreement was signed June 25, 2026; a definitive proxy was filed August 20, 2026, with the special meeting set for September 23, 2026. A Minnesota suit, Garfield v. Baumgartner, plus demand letters challenge proxy disclosures and seek to enjoin the vote; Bio-Techne calls claims meritless but is voluntarily supplementing disclosures. Watch vote timing, injunction risk, and any revised deal terms.

RAL.brief: Ralliant Corp filed an 8-K on May 12, 2026, disclosing entry into an accelerated share repurchase (ASR) program to repurchase $100 million of its common stock under a pre-existing Board-authorized buyback. The repurchase price is based on the average daily Rule 10b-18 volume-weighted average price during the program term, with settlement expected by end of Q2 2026. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The ASR is a cash-settled structure reducing share count. Watch for final settlement shares repurchased and any impact on EPS; no arbitrage angle exists as this is an issuer capital return.

TENB.brief: Tenable Holdings, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on September 15, 2026, announcing the closing of its private offering of $800 million aggregate principal amount of 0.25% Convertible Senior Notes due 2031, including the full exercise of the $75 million initial purchasers' over-allotment option. The Notes are senior unsecured obligations issued under an indenture with U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association, and bear interest at 0.25% per year, payable semiannually starting March 15, 2027. The offering represents a capital markets transaction rather than a special situation, though the issuance of convertible notes carries potential equity dilution implications. Holders may convert under specified conditions, including a 150% stock price trigger over a 30-day trading period or upon certain corporate events. Investors should watch for the use of proceeds and any related capped call or conversion rate mechanics disclosed in the full filing, as these will affect the effective conversion premium and dilution profile. The conversion price, initial conversion rate, and any associated hedge transactions were not specified in the excerpt.

GENI.brief: Genius Sports Ltd filed a Form 6-K reporting the consummation of its acquisition of Zeal Ltd (Legend) via its wholly-owned subsidiary Lion Bidco (Guernsey) Limited. The transaction closed on April 30, 2026, with consideration comprising $800 million in cash (subject to customary adjustments) and 10,088,781 ordinary shares of Genius (issued at a volume-weighted average share price). The Seller Parties are subject to a six-month lock-up on the stock consideration. Additional earn-out consideration may be payable in cash or shares at Genius's election. The acquisition was financed with a new $825 million term loan and $220 million revolving credit facility, secured by substantially all assets. The filing confirms an earn-out and orderly sell-down structure; the regulatory clock has expired as the deal is closed. Watch for integration risk and earn-out triggers.

WMS.brief: Advanced Drainage Systems filed an 8-K disclosing an October 1, 2026 Securities Purchase Agreement under which ADS and subsidiary ADS Investment LLC will acquire all equity interests of StormTrap Investments, L.L.C. from StormTrap Investors, L.L.C. and other sellers for approximately $530 million, or about $450 million adjusted for the present value of expected tax benefits, subject to purchase price adjustments. The purchase is funded with cash on hand and existing credit facility borrowings. Closing remains subject to customary conditions, including antitrust approvals; the Company obtained representations and warranties insurance. Watch regulatory clearance timing and integration execution.

LBRX.brief: LB Pharmaceuticals Inc filed an 8-K on July 28, 2026, announcing a private placement of 3,577,560 common shares and 715,513 pre-funded warrants at $34.94 per share-equivalent, raising gross proceeds of approximately $150 million. The warrants are immediately exercisable at $0.0001, subject to beneficial ownership caps of 4.99% or 9.99%. The offering is expected to close on July 30, 2026, and proceeds will be used for company purposes. This is a routine capital raise, not a special situation.

MCFT.brief: MasterCraft Boat Holdings filed an 8-K to report its acquisition of Marine Products Corporation via a two-step merger. Under the terms, Marine Products shareholders received 0.232 MasterCraft shares plus $2.43 cash per share, implying a mixed cash-and-stock consideration. The exact price per share and premium are not stated in this excerpt. The board of both companies approved the transaction; no advisors are named. The deal closed on May 15, 2026, the filing date. Watch for post-close integration updates and potential dissenting shareholder litigation.

NBHC.brief: National Bank Holdings Corp filed an 8-K on October 1, 2026, disclosing that on September 30, 2026 its board approved an additional share repurchase authorization of up to $40.1 million of Class A common stock, supplementing $59.9 million remaining under the existing authorization for aggregate authority of $100.0 million. Separately, Item 2.06 disclosed expected material credit impairments on $65.0 million of commercial loans, primarily franchise and healthcare, estimated to be charged down to $18.2 million, producing roughly $46.8 million of charge-offs, $38–40 million of quarterly provision, a $4.0 million FinTech investment impairment, and a $32–34 million after-tax hit ($0.72–$0.76 per diluted share). No expiration date; buybacks may use open-market, negotiated, or 10b5-1 transactions. Watch credit deterioration versus capital return pace and any revised provisioning guidance.

IIIV.brief: i3 Verticals, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing its board approved a new $100 million share repurchase program for its Class A common stock, replacing a prior program that was fully expended. Repurchases may be made in open market, privately negotiated transactions, or under Rule 10b5-1 plans through May 11, 2027, subject to market conditions, liquidity, contractual restrictions, and securities law compliance. The program is discretionary and may be suspended or terminated at any time. Watch for actual repurchase activity and impact on diluted share count; no premium or fixed price is specified.

EXE.brief: Expand Energy Corporation filed an 8-K reporting the completed acquisition of Twin Eagle Holdings N.A., LLC on September 16, 2026, marking the close of a previously announced transaction. Concurrently, the company disclosed that Dan Turco ceased serving as Executive Vice President Marketing and Commercial effective at closing, transitioning to Executive Vice President of Commercial Activities focusing on LNG and gas marketing integration. No purchase price, per-share terms, premium, advisor, or break fee were disclosed in the excerpt. Deal terms and financial impact remain unavailable, so the risk-arb angle centers on integration execution and any undisclosed consideration details.

LMND.brief: NYSE American LLC filed a Form 25-NSE on February 9, 2026, to delist Lemonade, Inc.'s warrants (ticker: LMND) from the exchange, effective February 20, 2026. The delisting follows the warrants' conversion into other securities via operation of law, with trading suspended on February 6, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The warrants now only represent the right to receive an immediate cash payment per Rule 12d2-2(a)(3). The delisting removes the warrants' public market, creating a mandatory cash-out event for holders. Watch for the final cash payment terms and any residual claims; risk-arb focuses on valuation versus the cash-out price.

NTB.company: Bank of N.T. Butterfield & Son Ltd

AMC.brief: AMC priced $2.0 billion of 8.875% first lien notes due 2031 and $850 million of first lien term loans at SOFR+4.50% with 1.50% OID, alongside a previously announced $1.12 billion second lien term loan facility. Proceeds, plus cash, fund a tender offer for AMC's 7.500% senior secured notes due 2029, a conditional full redemption of Muvico 1.5L notes due 2029, and repayment of existing term loans. Deals close on or around October 5, 2026, with guarantees from Muvico, Odeon Cinemas Group, and subsidiaries. Watch tender participation and close conditions.

RIG.brief: Transocean filed an 8-K updating its pending acquisition of Valaris Limited under a February 9, 2026 Business Combination Agreement, exchanging 15.235 Transocean shares per Valaris share. On October 13, 2026, Brazilian competition authority CADE cleared the deal without restrictions; publication in Brazil's Official Journal on October 15-16, 2026 triggers a fifteen-day waiting period before finality, after which all regulatory approval conditions are satisfied. Closing is expected in Q4 2026, subject to remaining conditions. Watch publication timing, finality, any last regulatory conditions and arbitrage spread around the fixed exchange ratio.

AEE.brief: Ameren Corp filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement for an at-the-market equity offering of up to $2,266,700,000 of common stock under its existing $5.0 billion sales agreement. The offering uses sales agents and forward sale agreements with multiple banks, where proceeds are received upon physical settlement, with potential cash or net share settlement. This is a capital-raising transaction by the issuer, with proceeds likely used for general corporate purposes. No premium, board recommendation, or advisors specified. Watch for dilution and settlement mechanics.

FTV.brief: The New York Stock Exchange LLC filed a Form 25-NSE to delist Fortive Corp's 3.700% Notes due 2026 under Rule 12d2-2(a)(2). The securities were redeemed or paid at maturity on February 13, 2026, with trading suspended same day. Delisting becomes effective at the opening on February 24, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor was named. This is a routine notification of maturity, not a merger or take-private. The notes are fully collateralized by the issuer's obligation to pay. No overhang, ownership split, or regulatory clock applies. What to watch: confirm the full redemption price; risk-arb angle is negligible as this is a scheduled maturity event.

NRIM.brief: Northrim BanCorp filed an amended Form S-4 on September 15, 2026 registering shares for its acquisition of PBCO Financial Corporation under a July 22, 2026 merger agreement. The registration statement covers Northrim common stock to be issued to PBCO shareholders via merger sub Whitewater Sub, Inc. No exchange ratio, price per share, or premium is disclosed in this excerpt. The deal represents Northrim's first out-of-state branch expansion, extending its community banking franchise. Named advisors are Accretive Legal and Hunton Andrews Kurth. The transaction remains preliminary and subject to shareholder votes and regulatory approvals; deal terms and timeline require further disclosure review for risk-arb assessment.

CBZ.brief: NYSE filed Form 25-NSE on 2026-11-02 to delist CBIZ, Inc. common stock under Rule 12d2-2(a)(3), after the merger with Viking MergerCo, Inc., a direct wholly owned subsidiary of Viking ParentCo, Inc., an affiliate of Grant Thornton Advisors LLC, became effective that same day. Each CBIZ share converted into USD 55.00 cash, without interest, less applicable fees and taxes; the whole class now evidences only the right to an immediate cash payment. Trading was suspended November 2, 2026, with removal from listing and registration effective at the opening of business on November 13, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor is identified; residual risk is deal-close administrative mechanics.

TRST.brief: TrustCo Bank Corp NY filed an 8-K announcing its Board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.40 per share, a 5.3% increase over the prior dividend, equating to $1.60 annualized. The dividend is payable October 1, 2026, to shareholders of record September 4, 2026. CEO Robert J. McCormick emphasized the dividend increase alongside a robust share repurchase program, citing solid earnings and strong capital. This routine dividend declaration reflects ongoing capital returns. Watch for future repurchase activity or capital deployment updates as management balances buybacks with dividend growth.

TNK.brief: This is a Form 6-K filed by Teekay Tankers Ltd. reporting its second quarter 2026 earnings. The filing discloses GAAP net income of $225.9M ($6.49/share) and adjusted net income of $193.6M ($5.56/share). It notes fleet renewal transactions: acquisition of two Suezmax newbuilding contracts for $190M total and sale of two vessels for $138M total proceeds. The company declared a $0.25/share cash dividend. The filing is a routine periodic earnings report, not triggering a special situation category, as it merely summarizes operational and financial results with no transformative corporate event.

GVA.brief: Granite Construction closed a private offering of $600M 6.375% senior notes due 2034, generating ~$590M net proceeds. The proceeds, plus cash on hand and capped call payments, will redeem all outstanding 3.75% convertible notes due 2028, repay credit facility borrowings, and for general corporate purposes. The notes are senior unsecured and guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries that are borrowers under the credit facility. The filing primarily describes a refinancing and debt restructuring rather than a pure capital return, but the redemption of convertible notes with cash qualifies as a capital return to prior noteholders. Watch for interest rate environment shifts and credit rating impact.

MSGK.brief: Madison Square Garden Sports Corp. filed an 8-K/A (Amendment No. 1) amending Item 8.01 of its September 30, 2026 report concerning the tax-free distribution of MSGS Spinco, Inc. common stock to stockholders; post-distribution the registrant renames to MSG Knickerbockers Corp. and trades as MSGK. The amendment updates disclosure of overlapping executive officers and directors across the registrant, Spinco, MSG Entertainment, Sphere Entertainment and AMC Global Media, including James Dolan as Executive Chairman/CEO of the registrant and Spinco. No price, ratio, record or distribution dates, or advisor are disclosed. Watch for Form 10 registration effectiveness and NYSE when-issued trading as the arbitrage timeline signals.

FIVN.brief: Five9 filed an 8-K on November 5, 2026, disclosing a definitive merger agreement to acquire privately held Level AI (Ujwal, Inc.), a Delaware corporation, via reverse triangular merger through wholly owned subsidiary Lander Merger Sub. Aggregate consideration is $325.0 million in cash for Level AI's outstanding stock, options and warrants, subject to customary cash, debt, transaction-expense and net working-capital adjustments. No board recommendation or financial advisor is named, and no premium applies given the private target. Termination rights include an outside date of February 5, 2027; neither party owes a termination fee. Watch regulatory clearance and closing-condition satisfaction; no public arbitrage spread exists.

GPN.brief: Global Payments Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing an accelerated share repurchase (ASR) program to repurchase $500 million of its common stock, part of a previously announced board-approved repurchase plan. Approximately 5.74 million shares will be received on May 8, 2026, with final settlement expected by June 30, 2026. The total shares repurchased will be based on the average daily VWAP during the repurchase period, less a discount and subject to adjustments. This is a capital return event via an ASR, not a tender offer. Watch for the final share count and impact on EPS.

PLGO.brief: Pelagos Insurance Capital (NYSE: PLGO), a Bermuda foreign private issuer, filed a Form 6-K disclosing board approval of a replenished common share repurchase authorization totaling $400.0 million. The board also raised the quarterly dividend to $0.22 per share, payable December 23, 2026, to holders of record December 11, 2026. No advisors or board recommendation language beyond board approval was named. Repurchases may occur via Rule 10b-18 open-market purchases, accelerated share repurchases, privately negotiated transactions, or Rule 10b5-1 plans, at company discretion. Watch buyback execution pace, dividend sustainability, and capital deployment versus growth.

LNC.brief: Lincoln National Corporation filed Amendment No. 1 to its issuer tender offer statement (Schedule TO-I) on September 9, 2026, reporting final results of two concurrent cash offers to purchase up to $500,000,000 aggregate liquidation preference of its outstanding depositary shares representing fractional interests in its 9.250% Fixed Rate Reset Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock, Series C, and its 9.000% Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock, Series D. The offers expired at 5:00 p.m. New York City time on September 8, 2026, subject to priority terms. The filing confirms expiration and results; no per-share price, premium, board recommendation, or advisor was disclosed. No regulatory clock or break fee applies. Watch for acceptance and proration details, since offers were capped and oversubscription could scale back tenders.

MS.brief: Morgan Stanley filed an 8-K to announce a quarterly common stock dividend increase to $1.15 per share from $1.00, a 15% rise. The dividend applies to the common stock and will commence with the declaration expected in the quarter ending September 30, 2026. The board authorized the increase, reflecting strong capital position. Terms include per-share amount only; no premium, advisors, or structural conditions. This is a routine capital return action not linked to any other event. Watch for sustained earnings coverage and payout ratio evolution.

AMCX.brief: AMC Global Media Inc. filed an 8-K on September 4, 2026, disclosing a settlement agreement with Robert Kirkman and other plaintiffs resolving 2022 breach-of-contract claims tied to The Walking Dead and Fear The Walking Dead. Total consideration is $120 million: $85 million cash due by September 18, 2026, plus $35 million by January 31, 2027, treated as an advance against future Modified Adjusted Gross Receipts participation. No board recommendation or advisor named. AMC takes an approximately $85 million charge in Q3 2026 and lowered 2026 free cash flow guidance to about $150 million from $220 million.

ROCK.brief: Gibraltar Industries filed an 8-K disclosing that subsidiary D.S.B. Holding Corp. agreed to sell all capital stock of The D.S. Brown Company to GCP Applied Technologies Inc., an affiliate of Saint-Gobain, for $208.0 million cash, subject to working capital, debt, cash and transaction-expense adjustments. The October 14, 2026 Securities Purchase Agreement requires HSR antitrust clearance, no injunction and customary closing conditions; no Gibraltar stockholder vote is needed. Closing is expected before year-end 2026, with an outside date of January 31, 2027 and up to five 30-day automatic extensions. Watch HSR timing and regulatory risk.

KDP.brief: Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. filed an 8-K under Item 8.01 reporting that its wholly-owned subsidiaries DPS Holdings Inc. and Mott's LLP, with other affiliates, completed previously announced transactions with FHU US Holdings, LLC (Chobani) on September 28, 2026. The company redeemed all indirect equity interests in Chobani for $800 million aggregate consideration — $400 million cash plus a $400 million Chobani promissory note maturing December 26, 2026 — and sold certain assets, including leasehold interests in two Allentown, Pennsylvania facilities, for $125 million cash. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The short-dated note carries counterparty credit exposure; watch repayment by the December maturity and any related gain or loss disclosure.

MLM.brief: Martin Marietta Materials filed an 8-K announcing the consummation of its acquisition of Lhoist North America (LNA) from Belgium-based LNA Holding. Consideration was approximately $7 billion in cash plus 10,953,543 newly issued Martin Marietta shares valued at $6.5 billion (based on a 15-day VWAP), as set in the Securities Sale Agreement dated June 27, 2026. At closing, Martin Marietta entered a shareholders agreement with LNA Holding, including a lock-up on the Consideration Shares (50% released at 12 months, 50% at 24 months) and a board seat designation. The transaction closed on August 21, 2026; watch for post-closing integration and lock-up expirations.

MAX.brief: MediaAlpha filed an 8-K on September 9, 2026, disclosing an Assignment, Assumption and Termination Agreement with Parallaxes Mars entities (PLX) to buy back PLX's interest in its Tax Receivables Agreement for $12.0 million cash, a 47% discount ($10.7 million) to the $22.7 million estimated June 30, 2026 value of that interest. The board, majority independent and disinterested, approved under related-person procedures. Post-transaction TRA liability is about $32 million; the deal is not a change of control or early termination. Funded from subsidiary cash via a pro rata QLH distribution to members, including executives. Watch related-party optics and remaining counterparty payments.

AMGN.brief: Nasdaq Stock Market LLC filed Form 25-NSE to delist Amgen Inc.'s 2.000% Senior Notes due 2026 under Rule 12d2-2(a)(2). The delisting is effective as of February 24, 2026, and reflects the securities' maturity. No premium, stock consideration, or board involvement applies. This is a routine administrative removal of matured notes, not a merger or tender. The filing has no regulatory clock or risk-arb implications; the notes will cease trading on Nasdaq. What to watch: any residual claims or conversion rights tied to the matured notes.

EXPD.brief: Expeditors International filed an 8-K on May 5, 2026, announcing a semi-annual cash dividend of $0.81 per share declared May 4, 2026, payable June 15, 2026 to holders of record June 1, 2026. This represents a 5% increase from prior dividends. The company also highlighted a new $3 billion share repurchase program authorized in February 2026 and cumulative returns of nearly $2 billion to shareholders since 2024. No board recommendation or advisor was named. The filing is a routine dividend declaration and ongoing buyback program disclosure. What to watch: no risk-arb angle; this is a steady capital return policy.

UTL.brief: Unitil Corp filed an 8-K reporting Amendment No. 4 to its Purchase and Sale Agreement with Aquarion Water Authority, changing the acquisition scope from three subsidiaries (AWC-MA, AWC-NH, Abenaki) to only AWC-NH and Abenaki, effectively narrowing the deal. The prior amendments extended the termination date to June 30, 2026. No financial terms, price/share, premium, or board recommendation were disclosed in this excerpt. The filing includes an Operating and Transition Services Agreement. Watch for regulatory approvals and any further adjustments as the revised transaction proceeds toward close.

VLY.brief: Valley National Bancorp filed Amendment No. 1 to its Form S-4 registration statement on 2026-10-30 covering its proposed acquisition of Providence Financial Corporation; Providence will merge with and into Valley, making Valley the surviving entity. The filing is a proxy statement/prospectus soliciting Providence shareholder approval and registers Valley common stock to be issued as merger consideration. The excerpt discloses no exchange ratio, price per share, implied value, premium or outside date; consideration is stock. Valley's board has not yet been described as recommending the deal in the excerpt; no financial advisor is named. The transaction is structured as a stock-for-stock bank merger requiring Providence shareholder vote and regulatory approvals. Watch for definitive exchange ratio and termination fees in later amendments.

ALOY.brief: Realloys Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a Securities Purchase Agreement entered into on June 24, 2026, to sell ~7.02M shares at $14.25/share to accredited investors in a private placement raising ~$100M gross. Clear Street LLC acted as placement agent. The deal includes customary reps/warranties and a 45-day lock-up on further equity issuance. Net proceeds are for general corporate and working capital. Close expected June 26, 2026, subject to conditions. A registration rights agreement covering resale was also signed. This is a capital-raising event (PIPE-like), not a transformative M&A or activist campaign, but fits 'Capital Returns' as a direct equity issuance for corporate purposes.

CWT.brief: California Water Service Group filed an 8-K under Item 8.01 to announce its board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.3350 per common share, payable May 22, 2026, to holders of record May 11, 2026. This marks the 325th consecutive quarterly dividend. No special-situation event such as an acquisition, divestiture, activist campaign, strategic review, tender offer, going-private, capital return, spin-off, rights offering, restructuring, liquidation, delisting, issuer tender, deal termination, SPAC, or management change is present. The filing is a routine dividend declaration, not a special situation.

LFST.brief: LifeStance Health Group filed an 8-K on September 11, 2026, disclosing a September 9 Underwriting Agreement among the Company, Barclays Capital Inc., and selling stockholders for a 22.25 million-share secondary offering of LifeStance common stock. All shares were sold by selling stockholders, and LifeStance concurrently repurchased 2,000,000 shares from the underwriter at the same price paid to the sellers, with no underwriting compensation on those repurchased shares. No price per share, premium, expected close, or board recommendation was stated in the excerpt. Closing occurred September 11. The structural overhang from selling holders is offset by the company's buyback; watch for pricing detail and any remaining lock-ups.

TTD.brief: Trade Desk, Inc. disclosed in an 8-K filed 2026-03-25 that it fell out of compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rules 5605(c)(2)(A) and 5605(d)(2)(A) after the resignations of directors Alexander Kayyal (3/19) and Kathryn Falberg (3/23). The audit and compensation committees lost minimum independent director counts. Nasdaq granted a cure period through 9/21/2026. The board appointed Andrew Vollero as Class II director and to the audit committee effective 4/3/2026, partially addressing the vacancies. No shareholder vote, premium, or price is involved. Watch for appointment of additional independent directors to regain compliance by the deadline; delisting risk remains if uncured.

XYL.brief: Xylem Inc. filed an 8-K on September 29, 2026, disclosing completion of a $1.5 billion public offering of senior notes in three tranches ($500 million each: 5.250% due 2029, 5.450% due 2032, 5.850% due 2037). Net proceeds, combined with cash on hand, will finance all or a portion of the purchase price for the previously announced acquisition of the Cornell Pump and Roper Pump businesses. The notes are senior unsecured obligations. A special mandatory redemption at 101% applies if the equity purchase agreement terminates or the acquisition does not close by August 10, 2027. Watch deal-close timing and leverage impact.

FSBW.brief: FS Bancorp, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing its board authorized a share repurchase program of up to $5.0 million of its common stock. The program runs for 12 months until August 24, 2027, commencing no sooner than the second trading day after the announcement. Repurchases may occur in open market or private transactions, or via a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan, at management's discretion, subject to market conditions and other factors. The company may suspend or terminate the program at any time. No specific price per share or premium was stated. What to watch: pace of repurchases and impact on EPS and capital ratios.

GRND.brief: Grindr Inc. filed an 8-K on September 30, 2026, disclosing a Securities Purchase Agreement for its wholly owned subsidiary to acquire all outstanding shares of PurposeMed Inc., parent of telehealth brand Freddie, for a $250 million base price. Consideration comprises $190 million cash and $60 million in 3,851,684 Grindr shares valued at $15.58 each (15-day VWAP through September 29, 2026), plus up to $70 million cash earnout tied to FY2027 targets. Shares are locked up 12 months post-closing. Buyer-side rep and warranty insurance limits recourse. No board recommendation or advisor named. Watch regulatory approvals, integration, and earnout achievement risk against Grindr's equity overhang.

INTU.brief: Intuit Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a restructuring plan to simplify its organizational structure, reducing its workforce by ~17% and considering site closures. The company expects $300-$340 million in charges, primarily for severance and benefits, mostly in Q4 fiscal 2026 ending July 31, 2026, with actions substantially completed by Q1 fiscal 2027 ending October 31, 2026. The board approved a cash dividend. This is a cost-cutting restructuring, not a sale or acquisition. Watch for execution risk and further charges.

URBN.brief: This 8-K Item 8.01 filing reports Urban Outfitters, Inc.'s earnings release for the quarter ended April 30, 2026, disclosing record net sales of $1.48 billion (up 11.4%) and net income of $115.7 million ($1.30 EPS). No strategic event or transaction is announced; it is a routine earnings disclosure without any special-situation elements such as M&A, activism, or restructuring. The filing is purely informational and does not trigger corporate action.

EFC.brief: Ellington Financial Inc. filed an 8-K on October 7, 2026 disclosing that its Board of Directors declared a monthly common dividend of $0.13 per share, payable November 30, 2026 to holders of record as of October 30, 2026. The filing, under Items 8.01 and 9.01, furnishes the related press release as Exhibit 99.1. No advisors, premium, strategic rationale, or structural mechanics beyond the dividend timetable are stated. The event is routine capital-return activity for the mortgage REIT; watch for consistency of the monthly payout with distributable earnings and book value trends.

MCHB.brief: Mechanics Bancorp filed an 8-K on September 16, 2026, disclosing that its wholly owned subsidiary, Mechanics Bank, completed the sale of approximately $417 million of remaining performing indirect auto loans to Bank of America's trading desk. The price was near book value, with a cutoff date of August 31, 2026; Mechanics Bank retains roughly $13 million of runoff auto loans. Westlake Portfolio Management continues servicing loans for both parties. Management framed the deal as balance-sheet optimization and capital reallocation. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or close date was disclosed, as this was an asset sale rather than a whole-company transaction.

ROAD.brief: Construction Partners filed an 8-K on Aug 10, 2026, disclosing that the death of independent director Michael H. McKay reduced its Audit Committee to two members, triggering non-compliance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5605(c)(2)(A), which requires a minimum of three independent directors. The company will rely on the cure period, which runs until the earlier of its next annual meeting or July 22, 2027, to regain compliance. Separately, on Aug 6, 2026, the company issued 619,000 unregistered restricted Class B shares with time-based vesting, exempt under Section 4(a)(2) and Regulation D. Shares vest fully on Sept 30, 2030. A press release honoring McKay was furnished under Item 7.01. Watch for audit committee appointee timing; unrelated to any M&A.

THFF.brief: First Financial Corporation (FFC), the Terre Haute, Indiana bank holding company, filed a preliminary Form S-4 proxy statement/prospectus on October 30, 2026 to register shares for its merger with First Illinois Corporation, announced under an agreement and plan of merger dated August 26, 2026. Consideration is FFC common stock, making this a stock-for-stock bank combination; the filing is preliminary and does not yet disclose exchange ratio, per-share value, premium or implied deal value.
