The combined holding company would hold roughly $7.0 billion in total assets and operate about 90 branches across key Indiana markets. Neither a board recommendation nor a financial advisor is named in the excerpt; the registration statement has not yet been declared effective. What to watch: the eventual exchange ratio and collar, shareholder votes, and Indiana/federal bank regulatory approvals governing the closing clock.

GYRE.brief: Gyre Therapeutics filed an 8-K reporting completion of its acquisition of Cullgen Inc. via a merger, with Cullgen surviving as a wholly owned subsidiary. The all-stock transaction valued Cullgen at approximately $300 million. At closing, shares of Cullgen capital stock were converted into shares of Gyre’s Series B Convertible Preferred Stock or common stock based on an exchange ratio of 0.4753. The merger is intended to qualify as a tax-free reorganization under Section 368(a). No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or break fee was disclosed. The deal closed on May 4, 2026. Watch for integration execution and potential dilution from the preferred stock terms.

ABUS.brief: Arbutus Biopharma filed Amendment No. 2 to its issuer tender offer Schedule TO (the US equivalent of a Canadian issuer bid) on October 1, 2026, reporting final results after the offer expired at 5:00 p.m. New York City time on September 29, 2026. The company offered to purchase common shares for an aggregate price of up to US$5.00–US$5.75 per share in cash, without interest, for an aggregate purchase price not exceeding US$230 million. The offer commenced August 24, 2026. No premium, board recommendation, advisor, break fee, or ownership split was disclosed in the excerpt. What to watch: final share count accepted and proration mechanics, given the capped aggregate value and price range.

MNSB.brief: MainStreet Bancshares, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing open-market share repurchases of 207,000 common shares at an average price of $24.09/share since Q2 start. The stock is slightly below tangible book value of $25.63 as of March 31, 2025. The repurchases are conducted under Rule 10b-18 with no obligation to continue, and the program can be suspended or discontinued at any time. This is a routine capital return disclosure rather than a transformative special situation. No material event risk or arbitrage angle; watch for ongoing buyback pace as a signal of management's view on valuation.

VNOM.brief: Viper Energy filed a prospectus supplement to its automatic shelf registration statement on Form S-3 for the sale of up to 3,691,796 shares of Class A common stock by a selling stockholder. The filing includes an opinion of Latham & Watkins LLP on the legality of the securities. No terms such as price per share or premium are disclosed; the registrant is the issuer facilitating a secondary sale. This is a routine shelf takedown, not a transformative special situation. The event is a capital markets transaction with no advisory, board recommendation, or structural complexity beyond equity distribution. Watch for selling shareholder identity and potential market overhang.

T.brief: The New York Stock Exchange filed a Form 25-NSE to delist AT&T Inc.'s 1.800% Global Notes due 2026, which matured and were paid in full on September 5, 2026. The Exchange notified the SEC of its intent to remove the securities from listing and registration at the opening of business on September 21, 2026, under Rule 12d2-2(a)(2). Trading was suspended on September 8, 2026. This is a routine administrative delisting following debt maturity, not a corporate action involving equity. No board recommendation or advisor is involved. Watch for the formal delisting effective date; no risk-arb implications as the notes are fully retired.

VICI.brief: VICI Properties filed an S-4/A registering shares to be issued in connection with its acquisition of Golden Entertainment, Inc. VICI will issue VICI common stock to holders of Golden common stock as merger consideration. The board of Golden has recommended the transaction; no advisor named in the excerpt. The merger will be effected under Minnesota law; VICI common stock is to be listed on NYSE. The transaction is subject to regulatory approval and Golden stockholder vote. What to watch: execution risk from regulatory clearance and stockholder approval; risk-arb spread will depend on VICI share price volatility.

PMTS.brief: CPI Card Group Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a partial redemption of its 10.000% senior secured notes due 2029. On July 2, 2026, the Company issued a notice to redeem $26.5 million of the $265.0 million aggregate principal, at a redemption price of 103.000% of par plus accrued interest, with redemption effective July 15, 2026. This is a routine debt management action, not a special situation. No board recommendation or advisors are named. Watch for any impact on leverage ratios or future refinancing steps.

PAYC.brief: Paycom Software filed an 8-K announcing a $0.375/share quarterly cash dividend and a new $2.0 billion stock repurchase plan with no expiration date. The dividend will be paid June 8, 2026 to holders of record May 26, 2026. Repurchases may be executed via open-market, privately negotiated, or Rule 10b5-1 programs at the board's discretion. No break fee or premium applies; this is a pure capital-return initiative. The company may use cash or its credit facility to fund repurchases. Watch for execution pace and any suspension triggers based on market conditions; no risk-arb angle as there is no M&A.

ATAI.brief: AtaiBeckley Inc. filed a Form 15-12G on September 21, 2026, terminating registration of its common stock under Section 12(g) and suspending Section 13 and 15(d) reporting obligations, with one holder of record. The filing follows the July 15, 2026 Agreement and Plan of Merger among AtaiBeckley, Eli Lilly and Company, and Lilly's indirect subsidiary Albali Acquisition Corporation. Merger Sub merged into AtaiBeckley on September 11, 2026, leaving the company a wholly owned Lilly subsidiary. No deal price, premium, advisor, or break fee was disclosed. The deregistration eliminates public reporting; watch for any residual shareholder consideration mechanics.

BYND.brief: Beyond Meat, Inc. filed a Form 8-K disclosing privately negotiated exchange agreements to retire approximately $15.0 million principal amount of its outstanding 0% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 at a purchase price of 96% of face value. In exchange, the Company will issue shares of its common stock based on a VWAP calculation over three trading days beginning September 23, 2026, with a floor price of $7.4009 per share. An initial 1,097,444 shares will be issued, with up to 848,265 additional true-up shares possible at final settlement on or about September 28, 2026. The transaction reduces debt and is structured as a private exchange, with no board recommendation or advisor named. Watch for dilution impact, final VWAP settlement, and potential open-market selling pressure from noteholders receiving shares.

NRDY.brief: Nerdy Inc. filed an 8-K reporting it received a NYSE notice on September 1, 2026, that it regained compliance with Section 802.01C minimum share price listing standard. The company's Class A common stock average closing price for the 30 trading days ended August 31, 2026, exceeded the $1.00 minimum. No transaction, terms, advisors, or structural changes are involved. This is a compliance milestone, not a special-situation corporate event. What to watch: continued compliance with other NYSE standards to avoid future delisting risk.

SLDB.brief: Solid Biosciences filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement to register an at-the-market (ATM) offering of up to $200 million of common stock through Jefferies as sales agent. This replaces a prior ATM with $6,447 unsold, and adds $199,993,553 in new capacity. Jefferies earns up to 3.0% commission. No specific price, shares, or timing were set. The filing is routine capital-raising, not a special situation. What to watch: market overhang from potential sales under this ATM facility.

KRRO.brief: Korro Bio filed an 8-K disclosing receipt on November 3, 2026 of Novo Nordisk's written notice terminating for convenience the September 13, 2024 research collaboration and license agreement, as amended November 11, 2025. Termination is effective February 1, 2027 after the contractual 90-day notice. Korro had received a $10.0 million upfront payment plus R&D cost reimbursement; no milestones were earned. Novo Nordisk never nominated a second target and did not exercise substitution rights during the 12-month hold. Post-termination, licenses revert, IP ownership is retained by each party, and Novo reimburses wind-down costs. Watch for pipeline/runway implications and any re-partnering or strategic review signals.

MZTI.brief: The Marzetti Company filed an 8-K reporting the closing of a $200 million term loan to partially fund its $400 million acquisition of Bachan's, Inc., a Japanese barbecue sauce brand, with the balance from cash on hand. The term loan, drawn on April 29, 2026, matures April 29, 2031, with a springing maturity date of March 6, 2029 under certain conditions; quarterly principal payments of $2.5 million begin after the first full calendar quarter. The acquisition closed on the same date. Watch for integration updates and margin impact; no arb angle as deal is cash and closed.

SLM.brief: SLM Corp filed a prospectus supplement (424B5) for a registered offering of $500M aggregate principal amount of 6.495% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Senior Notes due 2032. The notes bear initial fixed interest at 6.495% through May 15, 2031, then float at Compounded SOFR plus 271 bps. Price to public is 100%, underwriting discount 1%, net proceeds $495M. The notes are unsecured senior obligations, unlisted, and structurally subordinated to subsidiary liabilities. Joint book-running managers are J.P. Morgan and Barclays. This is a plain-vanilla debt issuance, not a special situation.

SYBT.brief: Stock Yards Bancorp filed an 8-K announcing the completion of its acquisition of Field Main Bancorp, Inc. and its subsidiary bank, Field Main Bank, Inc. (collectively Field Main). The filing confirms the appointment of Scott P. Davis, Field Main's CEO, to the Board effective May 1, 2026, as previously announced. The press release attached as Exhibit 99.1 highlights the merger completion. No financial terms (price per share, premium, consideration) or advisors are disclosed in this excerpt. The acquisition appears to be a strategic bolt-on for Stock Yards Bancorp. Watch for integration updates and potential synergies in future filings; risk-arb is moot as deal closed.

AEVA.brief: Nasdaq filed Form 25-NSE to delist Aeva Technologies, Inc.'s warrants (under Rule 12d2-2(a)(2)), effective March 11, 2026. No stake, price, or premium stated. The board recommendation is not mentioned; no advisor named. Removal follows failure to maintain listing standards. Delisting is mechanical, with no cash consideration or overhang. Watch for potential trading halt and any subsequent exchange or shareholder action.

JOBY.brief: NYSE filed Form 25-NSE to delist Joby Aviation's redeemable warrants (exercisable for common at $11.50) after the instruments were substituted by operation of law, representing solely the right to receive an immediate cash payment, per Rule 12d2-2(a)(3). Trading suspended August 10, 2026; delisting effective at the opening of business August 21, 2026. No board action, advisor, or premium specified. The warrants' substitution likely follows a forced exercise or redemption; common shares remain listed. Watch for cash payment terms per warrant and residual warrant overhang; risk-arb centers on expected redemption proceeds versus prior warrant trading levels.

AVAH.brief: Aveanna Healthcare Holdings Inc. filed an 8-K on June 2, 2026, announcing the completion of its acquisition of Family First Holding, LLC (Family First Homecare) via its wholly-owned subsidiary Pediatric Services of America, LLC. The cash purchase price was $175.5 million, subject to customary working capital adjustments, and was funded with cash on hand. The deal, originally disclosed in a March 12, 2026 8-K, expands Aveanna's pediatric home care footprint across seven states. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The press release updates FY2026 guidance to include the acquired operations. Watch for integration updates and future earnings impact.

TBCH.brief: Turtle Beach Corp filed an 8-K on April 30, 2026, announcing entry into a $85 million term loan facility with Blue Torch Finance, LLC and a separate ABL revolving credit facility. Proceeds refinance existing debt, fund general corporate purposes, and pay fees. The term loan matures April 30, 2029, with SOFR+6.75%-7.50% interest, quarterly amortization of 1.25%, and prepayment penalties. It is secured by substantially all assets and includes financial covenants. This is a routine debt refinancing, not a special situation.

CAR.brief: Avis Budget Group filed an 8-K on October 5, 2026 reporting receipt of a $650 million cash settlement from Pentwater Capital Management and affiliates under a June 19, 2026 Settlement and Release Agreement resolving the company's Section 16(b) short-swing profits lawsuit. The court approved the payment, which will be recorded in Q4 financials. Avis expects to use part of the proceeds to repay the remaining $350 million principal of its 5.750% Senior Notes due 2027 before year-end. The filing states nothing constitutes a redemption notice; watch redemption mechanics and any residual use of proceeds.

DC.brief: NYSE American LLC filed Form 25-NSE to delist Dakota Gold Corp.'s warrants (exercisable for common shares at $2.08) effective March 27, 2026. The delisting follows the warrants' conversion into other securities or an immediate cash payment under Rule 12d2-2(a)(3). Trading was suspended March 13. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The action is mechanical—warrants no longer represent independent value. Key watchpoint: whether holders receive cash or replacement securities and the timeline for any residual payments.

UUUU.brief: Energy Fuels filed an 8-K updating its pending acquisition of VAC Group B.V. and Ara VAC TOPCO US LLC from Ara Partners, a deal originally signed June 23, 2026, alongside completion of its ASM scheme acquisition on August 28, 2026. The filing discloses a Merger Agreement Amendment, supplemental VAC and ASM business disclosures, VAC historical financials, and unaudited pro forma combined financials. It also notes the planned departure of Energy Fuels' Chief Legal Officer and EVP, Global Government Relations. No revised price, stake, premium, or closing date is stated; consummation remains subject to customary conditions. Watch for the Item 2.01 closing 8-K and any deal-term changes embedded in the amendment.

EXLS.brief: ExlService Holdings, through its indirect subsidiary Clairvoyant AI, entered a securities purchase agreement to acquire 100% of iMerit for $170M upfront cash (subject to adjustments) plus up to $140M in cash incentives/earnouts over two years. The transaction is expected to close Q3 2026, pending antitrust clearance and customary conditions. The acquirer plans to fund with cash on hand and credit facility. Board approval is implied; no advisor named. Watch for regulatory timing and earnout milestone definitions as risk-arb drivers.

FFAI.brief: Faraday Future filed an 8-K disclosing a November 4, 2026 Purchase Agreement under which Executive Chairman Jiawei Wang bought one share of newly designated Series A Preferred Stock for $100, closing same day. The share carries super-voting rights contractually bound to mirror common and Series B/Series C votes on the Reverse Stock Split Proposal, but only once a one-third quorum of those classes is present; absent quorum the share stays unvoted. Mechanics create a quorum/pass gate for the reverse split rather than a conventional special situation; watch meeting turnout and whether the arrangement is challenged as entrenchment.

NXXT.brief: NextNRG, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing a Nov 2, 2026 Debt Exchange Agreement between the Company, its subsidiary NextNRG Holding Corp., and CEO/director/principal stockholder Michael D. Farkas; the transaction closed November 3, 2026. Farkas exchanged $7,000,000 of obligations—$3,629,924 note principal, $2,749,169 accrued interest, and $620,907 guarantee fees—for 7,000 newly designated Series D Convertible Voting Preferred shares at $1,000 stated value each, with no cash paid. Exchanged amounts and related liens and guaranties were cancelled; excluded obligations remain outstanding. This is a related-party balance-sheet recapitalization by an insider, not a third-party special situation; watch Series C protective provisions limiting cash repayment of remaining insider debt and potential dilution from preferred conversion.

RMBI.brief: Richmond Mutual Bancorporation filed an 8-K announcing the completion of its merger with The Farmers Bancorp, Frankfort, Indiana, effective July 1, 2026. Under the agreement dated November 11, 2025, each Farmers share was exchanged for 3.40 shares of Richmond common stock, resulting in Richmond issuing 6,254,357 shares. The merger was structured as a stock-for-stock transaction with cash for fractional shares. Richmond survived as the parent, and First Bank Richmond was renamed First Bank Midwest. The transaction received SEC effectiveness on April 3, 2026. No break fee or premium percentage was disclosed. Regulatory clocks have passed. Watch for post-merger integration updates and potential dilution impact on RMBI shares.

CLSK.brief: CleanSpark's indirect subsidiary CSDC Finance I, LLC completed a previously announced private offering of 7.875% senior secured notes due 2031, raising $2,276.0 million at 98.500% of par plus accrued interest. Proceeds fund the Sandersville, Georgia data center, reimburse prior equity contributions, and fund debt service reserves. Notes are guaranteed by CSRE Properties Sandersville and secured by collateral under a U.S. Bank indenture, with semi-annual amortization tied to a target project debt service coverage ratio. Interest pays April 1 and October 1; maturity October 1, 2031. Watch collateral coverage and project execution risk.

HUBG.brief: Hub Group filed an 8-K on September 17, 2026 disclosing receipt of a Nasdaq Staff Delisting Determination dated September 16, 2026, tied to non-compliance with Listing Rule 5250(c)(1). The company failed to file its Form 10-K for fiscal 2025 and Forms 10-Q for Q1 and Q2 2026 by September 14, 2026, the end of a previously granted 180-day extension. The determination has no immediate trading effect; Hub must request a Nasdaq Hearings Panel hearing by September 23, 2026. A timely request stays suspension 15 days, with a possible extended stay. Watch appeal timing, stay grant, and periodic filing remediation.

GNW.brief: Genworth Financial filed a definitive proxy statement (DEFC14A) for its 2026 annual meeting, addressing a contested solicitation. No specific terms were provided regarding stake, price, or premium. The board's recommendation is anticipated but not detailed in the excerpt. The filing includes disclosures on capital generation from Enact ($98 million dividends, $309 million share repurchases) and a $350 million share repurchase program, with $856 million repurchased since May 2022. Mechanics involve a shareholder vote on director elections and other proposals. Regulatory clock aligns with typical proxy timeline. What to watch: outcome of contested election and any activist influence on capital allocation.

SLQT.brief: On March 19, 2026, SelectQuote received a NYSE notice for non-compliance with Section 802.01C due to its average closing price falling below $1.00 over 30 consecutive trading days. The company intends to notify the NYSE of its plan to cure the deficiency within a six-month cure period. Compliance may be regained if, on the last trading day of any calendar month during the cure period, the closing price is at least $1.00 and the 30-day average is also at least $1.00. The stock remains listed during this period. Watch for potential reverse stock split or other remedial actions.

MBC.brief: MasterBrand, Inc. filed an 8-K to report the closing of its acquisition of American Woodmark Corporation via a merger. At closing, each American Woodmark share was exchanged for 5.150 shares of MasterBrand common stock (stock consideration). No cash or premium percentage was explicitly stated. Equity awards were converted based on the same exchange ratio. The board of each company approved the deal; no advisors named. The merger was effective May 28, 2026, and MasterBrand is the surviving public company. The market should monitor post-close integration and any stock price adjustments reflecting the exchange ratio.

BMY.brief: Bristol-Myers Squibb filed Form 15 to terminate the registration of its $2 Convertible Preferred Stock and 43 other classes of debt securities under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act, effective March 27, 2026. The filing states there are zero holders of record for the affected securities, meeting the threshold to suspend reporting obligations. No board recommendation, advisor, or financial terms were disclosed. This deregistration reduces ongoing SEC compliance costs but does not affect the company's common stock or contingent value rights. The move is procedural following prior redemptions or conversions. Watch for any remaining litigation or contingent value right triggers.

IMMR.brief: Immersion Corp disclosed on March 27, 2026, via Form 8-K, that it received a Nasdaq Staff Determination Letter for failure to timely file its Form 10-Q for the January 2026 quarter, adding to previously unfiled 10-Qs for July and October 2025. The company held a Hearings Panel meeting on March 26, 2026, requesting additional time to regain compliance. Immersion has since filed its annual report and July 2025 10-Q. No specific deal terms, premium, or consideration were mentioned. Investors should monitor the Hearing Panel's decision and the timing of the remaining filings.

APO.brief: Apollo Global Management filed Form 15-12G to terminate registration of its 6.75% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock under Section 12(g), effective August 11, 2026. The filing certifies zero holders of record, relying on Rule 12g-4(a)(1) (fewer than 300 holders). Common stock and 7.625% junior subordinated notes remain registered. The move likely follows the preferred's conversion or redemption, reducing reporting burden. Risk-arb angle: no deal terms; watch for any residual preferred trading or conversion mechanics.

BRBS.brief: HomeTrust Bancshares filed a definitive joint proxy statement/prospectus (DEFM14A) seeking shareholder approval of its acquisition of Blue Ridge Bankshares via a two-step merger announced August 16, 2026. Blue Ridge holders receive a fixed 0.086 HomeTrust shares per share, valued at approximately $4.30 based on HomeTrust's $49.98 close on August 14, 2026, and approximately $4.05 at the $47.14 price on October 27, 2026. The transaction is structured as a stock-for-stock merger intended to qualify as a Section 368(a) reorganization, tax-free except for fractional-share cash. HomeTrust expects to issue roughly 8.31 million shares, leaving former Blue Ridge holders with about 35% and existing HomeTrust holders 65% of the combined company; Blue Ridge Bank, N.A. will merge into HomeTrust Bank. Risk-arb focus: the fixed exchange ratio exposes Blue Ridge holders to HomeTrust price movement before closing, and both shareholder votes plus remaining regulatory approvals must clear.

JBSS.brief: John B. Sanfilippo & Son, Inc. (JBSS) filed an 8-K announcing a special cash dividend of $1.05 per share and a regular annual cash dividend of $0.95 per share on both Common and Class A Common stock. The aggregate payment will return approximately $23.6 million to stockholders. Dividends are payable September 9, 2026, to holders of record August 17, 2026. The special dividend is a one-time capital return event. The annual dividend represents a $0.05 increase year-over-year. The filing does not mention any advisor or board recommendation beyond the dividend declaration. No structural complexities or regulatory clock are noted. What to watch: future capital allocation policies and whether special dividends become recurring.

CDRE.brief: Cadre Holdings, Inc. filed Amendment No. 1 to its Form S-4 registration statement, updating the preliminary prospectus for the issuance of up to 7,500,000 shares of common stock to be used as consideration in future acquisitions of assets, businesses, or securities. No specific acquisition terms, counterparties, or pricing are disclosed; terms will be negotiated case-by-case. The amendment also updates the filing fee table and includes KPMG LLP's consent as auditor. The registration statement is not yet effective, and shares may be issued from time to time after effectiveness. The structure creates potential overhang from shares issued as acquisition currency; watch for future deals and dilution impact on existing holders.

BTSG.brief: BrightSpring Health Services, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting an underwriting agreement dated June 3, 2026 for a secondary offering of 14,999,771 shares of common stock at $58.75 per share by selling stockholders, including KKR Phoenix Aggregator L.P. and management stockholders. The company did not receive proceeds except from stock option exercises, and repurchased 1,026,465 shares from the underwriter. The offering was made under an existing Form S-3ASR. While the share repurchase is a capital return element, the filing primarily discloses a secondary sale by existing holders, not a transformative special situation. Watch for any further KKR stake reduction or insider selling; no risk-arb angle applicable.

ORMP.brief: Oramed Pharmaceuticals filed an 8-K reporting two events. First, board approved amendments to its bylaws regarding record dates and written consent procedures. Second, the company agreed with Scilex Holding to extend maturity of senior secured promissory notes (Tranche A ~$29.5M, Tranche B ~$6.7M) plus a $1M cash extension fee payable by Scilex. No special-situation deal terms such as price, premium, or change of control are involved. This is a routine operational and debt extension filing.

NCNO.brief: nCino, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting Q2 FY2027 results and announcing a board-authorized stock repurchase program of up to $100 million of common stock. Repurchases may occur via open market, block trades, private negotiations, accelerated stock repurchase, or Rule 10b5-1 plans. The program has no time limit, does not obligate repurchases, and can be modified or suspended at board discretion. This is a capital return event, not a tender offer, with no fixed price per share or premium.

EMAT.brief: Evolution Metals & Technologies Corp. filed an 8-K on September 17, 2026 disclosing a Securities Purchase Agreement with YA II PN, LTD. (Yorkville) for convertible debentures totaling $30,927,835. The first $22,000,000 debenture was issued immediately, with $2,000,000 and $6,927,835 tranches tied to registration statement filing and effectiveness. Purchase price is 97% of principal; conversion price is the lower of $5.02 or 95% of the 5-day VWAP, subject to a floor and a 4.99% beneficial ownership cap. This is a private placement financing, not a special situation.

MOV.brief: Movado Group filed an 8-K disclosing a definitive agreement, effective October 5, 2026, to sell a 95% interest in its EBEL watch brand to a strategic buyer group led by Montres Journe SA, with Chanel and industry veteran Pierre Jacques participating; Jacques will serve as EBEL CEO. Consideration totals approximately $66.5 million, subject to customary closing adjustments, with Movado retaining a 5% minority interest. Closing is expected in Q4 fiscal 2026, contingent on customary conditions including a pre-closing reorganization. The sale sharpens Movado's focus on core accessible-luxury and fashion watch and jewelry brands; watch closing mechanics and any purchase-price adjustment true-up.

ARAI.brief: Arrive AI Inc. disclosed a Nasdaq notification on July 21, 2026 that it fails to meet the minimum Market Value of Publicly Held Shares (MVPHS) of $15mm for continued listing under Rule 5450(b)(2)(C), having fallen short for 32 consecutive business days through July 20. No immediate impact on trading under symbol ARAI. The company has 180 days (until January 19, 2027) to regain compliance by maintaining MVPHS ≥$15mm for at least 10 consecutive business days, or it may apply to transfer to the Nasdaq Capital Market. Stock continues trading; watch for compliance updates or a potential reverse stock split to boost MVPHS.

DCOM.brief: Dime Commercial Bancshares filed an 8-K disclosing an October 19, 2026 Agreement and Plan of Merger under which ES Bancshares (parent of Empire State Bank) will merge into Dime, followed by the bank subsidiary merger into Dime Commercial Bank. Consideration is a mixed cash/stock election: $30.0 million aggregate cash pool funded at $30.0M divided by half the outstanding ES shares, with the balance in Dime stock at an Exchange Ratio. Both boards unanimously approved. Terms beyond the cash pool—exchange ratio value, premium, and close date—are absent from the excerpt. Watch regulatory approvals, election proration, and shareholder votes.

INGN.brief: Inogen filed an 8-K reporting completion on November 2, 2026 of its previously announced sale of its U.S. oxygen rental business to Rotech Healthcare, under an Asset Purchase Agreement dated September 29, 2026. Aggregate purchase price is estimated at up to approximately $24.8 million, based on transferred inventory and patient records, subject to post-closing reconciliation and payable in six installments. Transferred assets are specified on-rent and on-hand inventory plus related patient records. The same filing discloses a CEO transition, naming COO Andy Reding President and CEO effective October 30, 2026, and includes third-quarter results. Watch installment collection risk and residual value of retained operations.

GNE.brief: Genie Energy Ltd. received an NYSE noncompliance notice on April 1, 2026, for failing to timely file its Form 10-K for FY2025 due to a restatement of audited financials for FY2023 and FY2024. Per NYSE Section 802.01E, the company has six months to file a remediation plan and regain compliance; trading continues under symbol GNE during this period. The board has not issued a formal recommendation. The delayed filing stems from a restatement effort rather than operational distress. Risk-arb watch: monitor filing timeline, NYSE acceptance of the plan, and any related financing or restructuring events.

AGX.brief: Argan, Inc. filed an 8-K on September 9, 2026, announcing that its board declared a 40% increase in the quarterly cash dividend, from $0.50 to $0.70 per common share, or $2.80 annualized. The dividend is payable October 30, 2026, to holders of record October 22, 2026. No advisor was named. This marks the fourth consecutive annual increase, supported by power-generation demand from datacenters and electrification. Watch for sustainability of free cash flow and payout coverage versus project timing and backlog conversion.

INSW.brief: International Seaways (parent) filed an 8-K disclosing Exchange and Support Agreements and a Transaction Agreement with Bruton Limited, a Bermuda company whose NDRs trade in Norway. Holders representing ~50.5% of Bruton common agreed to exchange each Bruton share for 0.05190 INSW shares privately, expected to close on or about October 20, 2026; Merger Sub then merges into Bruton, making Bruton an indirect wholly owned subsidiary. Terms are stock-for-stock with cash in lieu of fractional shares; no price, premium, or advisor stated. The lock-up support secures merger approval. What to watch: Bruton shareholder vote and remaining minority roll-up.

SMG.brief: Scotts Miracle-Gro filed an 8-K reporting that on September 11, 2026 it redeemed all $250.0 million principal of its 5.250% Senior Notes due 2026 at par plus accrued interest, terminating that material indenture and extinguishing noteholder rights except payment. The company simultaneously announced completion of capital allocation initiatives, achievement of its $275 million free cash flow target and reaffirmed fiscal 2026 guidance. No board recommendation, advisor, premium or change-of-control element appears. The debt retirement removes a fixed charge and mirrors a US issuer tender/redemption; watch for follow-on refinancing, leverage trajectory and any incremental buyback or dividend commentary.

ETON.brief: Eton Pharmaceuticals filed an 8-K disclosing an October 13, 2026 license agreement with Aquestive Therapeutics granting exclusive U.S. commercialization rights to LIBERVANT (diazepam) buccal film for seizure clusters. Eton paid a $10.0 million upfront fee plus up to $47.5 million in regulatory/commercial milestones ($10M first sale, $2.5M ages 6-11 approval, up to $35M sales-based) and mid-teens royalties; Aquestive supplies exclusively for 20 years. The product holds tentative FDA approval. No board recommendation or advisor named. Watch launch timing, full-approval conversion and sales-milestone risk.

GCBC.brief: Greene County Bancorp, Inc. filed an 8-K on September 15, 2026 reporting the redemption of $10.0 million aggregate principal of its 3.00% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Subordinated Notes due September 15, 2031. The redemption price equaled 100% of principal plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, the redemption date; $20.0 million remains outstanding. The company funded the redemption with cash on hand. No board recommendation or advisor was disclosed. The partial note retirement reduces regulatory capital and interest expense; watch for future capital actions or further note repurchases.

AVEX.brief: AEVEX Corp. filed an 8-K on September 8, 2026 announcing completion of its acquisition of Maritime Applied Physics, LLC (d/b/a/formerly Maritime Applied Physics Corporation) from Black Sea Technologies, LLC for a total enterprise value of $600 million, subject to customary adjustments. Consideration consisted of 12,727,273 Class A shares valued at $350 million plus cash for the balance, with a $5 million working-capital adjustment escrow and up to $50 million in earnout contingent on AVEX trading at or above $28.00 and the target achieving specified GARC/CHASER revenue and gross profit targets through December 31, 2027. No advisor or board recommendation was named in the excerpt.

RCUS.brief: Arcus Biosciences filed an 8-K under Item 8.01 to disclose the discontinuation of the Phase 3 STAR-121 study due to futility (domvanalimab plus zimberelimab and chemotherapy), as recommended by the IDMC; and that Gilead will not make an option continuation payment, ending its option rights to additional early-stage programs (CCR6, CD89, CD40L) after July 14, 2026. Gilead retains limited options to AB801, AB598, AB102, and a TNF small-molecule inhibitor. Arcus retains full rights to casdatifan except those licensed to Taiho. No financial terms, deal mechanics, or board recommendation were provided. Watch for any restructuring of the Gilead collaboration or potential impact on Arcus's pipeline valuation.

NTST.brief: NETSTREIT Corp. filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement establishing a new $400M ATM equity offering program, replacing a prior $300M program. The company enters into a sales agreement with multiple agents and forward sellers, allowing for sales of common stock from time to time. As of the filing, $256.1M in shares have been sold under the prior program, and 12.8M shares remain unsettled under forward sale agreements maturing September 2026 through March 2027. This is a routine capital-raising transaction, not a special situation.

ATEX.brief: Anterix Inc. filed an 8-K on September 18, 2026 disclosing that its board authorized a new share repurchase program on September 16, 2026, effective September 22, 2026, after the prior program expires September 21, 2026. The company may buy up to $250,000,000 of common stock through September 22, 2029 via open market or privately negotiated transactions, including Rule 10b5-1 plans. Timing and amount remain discretionary; the program can be suspended or modified. Watch buyback pace versus free cash flow and Spectrum Enterprises monetization proceeds.

DX.brief: Dynex Capital filed an 8-K after pricing an underwritten public offering of 4,800,000 shares of 9.375% Series D Fixed-Rate Cumulative Redeemable Preferred Stock at a $25.00 liquidation preference, with a 30-day option for up to 720,000 additional shares. An underwriting agreement dated September 22, 2026 was signed with Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan, RBC, UBS, Wells Fargo, Citigroup, Goldman Sachs and KBW as representatives. Articles of Amendment effective September 29, 2026 designated 5,520,000 authorized preferred shares; quarterly cumulative dividends are payable January, April, July and October 15. Watch preferred overhang and dividend coverage.

DFIN.brief: Donnelley Financial Solutions filed an 8-K reporting that its Board authorized a new $150 million share repurchase program, replacing a prior program with ~$15 million remaining. Repurchases may occur on the open market or in private transactions through December 31, 2027, and may be executed under a Rule 10b5-1 plan. No price/share, premium, or advisor is stated. The repurchase is an ordinary capital return event, not a tender offer. Watch for the pace of buybacks and possible suspension if market conditions change.

ONTO.brief: Onto Innovation Inc. filed an 8-K announcing plans for a private offering of $1.1B aggregate principal amount of convertible senior notes due 2031, under Rule 144A. The proceeds will be used for share repurchases and capped call transactions. No specific price per share, premium, or board recommendation was disclosed. The offering is subject to market conditions. The mechanics include a convertible issuance alongside hedging via capped calls to reduce dilution. Watch: pricing terms, conversion premium, and overall capital return impact to equity value.

WVE.brief: Wave Life Sciences Ltd. filed Form 15-12G to terminate its SEC registration and suspend reporting obligations under the 1934 Act, citing Rule 12g-4(a)(1). The filing reports one holder of record of its ordinary shares as of the certification date, reflecting a likely strategic transaction or going-private event. Filed August 7, 2026, effective August 10, the delisting removes public disclosure requirements. Watch for confirmation of the underlying transaction, such as an acquisition or merger, and potential liquidity or governance implications for remaining holders.

BZAI.brief: Blaize Holdings, Inc. filed a Form 8-K on September 28, 2026, disclosing receipt of a Nasdaq Listing Qualifications letter dated the same day. The company is not in compliance with the minimum closing bid price requirement under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5450(a)(1), as its common stock closed below $1.00 per share for 30 consecutive business days. The company has 180 calendar days, until March 29, 2027, to regain compliance. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The stock continues trading on the Nasdaq Global Market under BZAI. The overhang poses delisting risk; watch for a reverse split or other curative action.

DDOG.brief: Datadog filed an 8-K reporting shareholder approval and completion of a redomiciliation from Delaware to Nevada via a plan of conversion, effective April 21, 2026. The reorganization did not change business, management, assets, or stock terms. No price, premium, or deal value is involved. New indemnification agreements were entered with officers and directors. This is a jurisdictional reincorporation, not a special-situation transaction, so the filing is classified as Other.

NHC.brief: National Healthcare Corp. (NHC) filed an 8-K reporting completion of its $560 million cash acquisition of 35 skilled nursing and independent living facilities from National Health Investors (NHI) on July 1, 2026. The purchase was funded by borrowings under a credit facility from Bank of America and cash on hand. NHC previously leased these properties. The credit agreement was amended to increase the revolver from $50M to $75M. No premium percentage, board recommendation, or advisor was disclosed. The transaction eliminates the master lease structure, converting NHC from tenant to owner-operator. Watch for integration execution and potential deleveraging actions.

NP.brief: Neptune Insurance Holdings Inc. filed an 8-K on April 22, 2026, announcing a $100 million stock repurchase program approved by its Board on April 21, 2026. The program authorizes open-market or private repurchases of Class A common stock, funded by cash from operations or its revolving credit facility. No specific price per share, premium, or expiration date is given; repurchases will comply with Rule 10b-18 and may involve Rule 10b5-1 plans. The program can be suspended at any time. Watch for actual buyback execution pace and impact on share count.

PBFS.brief: Pioneer Bancorp, Inc. filed a Form 8-K announcing the acquisition of The College Advisor of New York, a college admissions advisory firm. The registrant, Pioneer, acted as the acquirer. Terms such as price per share, valuation, or premium were not disclosed. Dr. Dean Skarlis, founder of the target, will head Pioneer's new College Advising Division as Vice President. No board recommendation or financial advisors were named. The transaction diversifies Pioneer beyond core banking into education advisory services, integrating college planning with financial strategy. Watch for integration execution and potential impact on Pioneer's earnings, though financial materiality remains unclear.

NOW.brief: ServiceNow Inc. filed an 8-K reporting its entry into a $4 billion unsecured term loan credit agreement on April 17, 2026, to finance a portion of the cash consideration for its acquisition of Armis Security Ltd. The term loan matures on October 16, 2026, with interest at alternate base rate or term SOFR plus a margin based on credit ratings, and includes customary covenants and a potential six-month extension at lender discretion. JPMorgan Chase acted as administrative agent. The acquisition terms (price, premium, target advisors) and board recommendation were not disclosed. Watch for regulatory clearance and financing risk given short maturity.

TH.brief: Target Hospitality filed an 8-K detailing a September 8, 2026 underwriting agreement tied to a secondary offering by Arrow Holdings and MFA Global (TDR Capital-controlled), covering 14,000,000 shares at $18.50, plus a 2,100,000-share greenshoe, with no company proceeds. Concurrently, Target will repurchase roughly $30 million of shares at the same price, funded with cash and ABL borrowings, held as treasury. Morgan Stanley, Deutsche Bank and J.P. Morgan are representatives. Watch deal pricing pressure, lockup signals and whether the buyback absorbs enough supply to limit overhang.

CATY.brief: CATHAY GENERAL BANCORP filed an 8-K on April 23, 2026, announcing a new $150 million share repurchase program adopted by its board. The program allows open-market or private repurchases at management's discretion, potentially via a Rule 10b5-1 plan, with no fixed expiration. With ~67 million shares outstanding, the authorization represents ~$2.24/share. The board may suspend or modify the program at any time. What to watch: actual execution pace and any impact on capital ratios or EPS; risk-arb: none, as no M&A catalyst is present.

FFBC.brief: First Financial Bancorp filed Amendment No. 1 to its Form S-4 registration statement (the US equivalent of a scheme/prospectus document) on September 23, 2026, registering shares for its acquisition of Finward Bancorp under a July 21, 2026 merger agreement. Finward will merge into First Financial, then Finward's subsidiary Peoples Bank will merge into First Financial Bank. The proxy statement/prospectus is preliminary and subject to completion; no stake percentage, price per share, implied value, premium, board recommendation mechanics, or advisor is stated in the excerpt. The filing registers First Financial common stock as consideration, confirming a stock-based deal. What to watch: shareholder vote timing, regulatory approvals, and final exchange ratio disclosure.

GLIBK.brief: GCI Liberty, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing entry into a Securities Purchase Agreement on April 21, 2026, whereby its wholly owned subsidiary GCI Holdings, LLC will acquire all equity interests in Q Gateway Intermediate Holdings, LLC (Quintillion) from Q Gateway Ultimate Holdings, LLC. Total consideration includes $310M cash at closing (subject to working capital adjustments), up to $50M in reimbursed capex within 30 days post-close, and earn-out payments for 2027/2028/2030 gross revenues payable in 2028/2029/2031. GCI may satisfy the 2030 earn-out in Series C stock valued by VWAP. Closing is subject to customary conditions and regulatory approvals. Watch for antitrust review timeline; earn-out structure adds revenue-linked upside.

GPRE.brief: Green Plains Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a routine amendment to its existing senior secured sustainability-linked revolving credit facility. The Second Revolver Amendment extends the termination date from March 25, 2027 to September 25, 2027 and reduces the facility commitment from $350 million to $300 million. No new borrowing, special distribution, or extraordinary corporate event is disclosed. This is a standard credit facility modification, not a special situation.

HAFC.brief: Hanmi Financial Corp. filed an 8-K on April 23, 2026, announcing a $0.28 per share quarterly cash dividend declared by its Board of Directors, payable May 20, 2026, to holders of record May 4, 2026. The dividend is part of a capital return program; the press release also references a share repurchase program. No offer, tender, or structural change is involved; the filing is a routine dividend declaration with a note on buybacks. The action returns capital to shareholders without altering the corporate structure. Watch for any changes in payout policy or repurchase activity as signals.

PHM.brief: PulteGroup filed an 8-K disclosing Q1 2026 earnings and a $1.5 billion increase in its existing share repurchase program, effective April 22, 2026. The company reported net income of $347 million ($1.79 per share) and had already repurchased $308 million of common shares in the quarter. The board approved the authorization increase, but no specific price, premium, or expiration date was provided. The mechanics are a standard open-market buyback, which reduces share count and supports EPS. Watch for future buyback execution pace and any leverage impact; risk-arb is not applicable as this is purely a capital allocation event.

USGO.brief: U.S. GoldMining Inc. filed an 8-K on November 3, 2026 disclosing that its board, on the recommendation of the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, unanimously appointed John DeLucchi on November 2, 2026 to fill an existing board vacancy and named him Audit Committee Chair. The move cures a Nasdaq Listing Rule 5605 audit-committee deficiency triggered by Aleksandra Bukacheva's prior resignation, notice of which the company received August 27, 2026. DeLucchi, 63, is a former PwC Canada partner and ex-Madison Group CEO; no related-party transactions or side arrangements were disclosed, and he receives a US$10,000 annual cash retainer. Watch Nasdaq confirmation of regained compliance.

WABC.brief: Westamerica Bancorporation filed an 8-K announcing a board-approved increase in its stock repurchase plan authorization by 2,000,000 shares, bringing total remaining authorization to 2,785,023 shares (11.8% of shares outstanding as of March 31, 2026). Repurchases may occur on the open market or in privately negotiated transactions through December 31, 2026. Chair/CEO David Payne cited financial strength and capital-management goals. No price or premium terms are stated. The program is accretive to EPS but execution depends on market conditions. Watch the pace of buybacks relative to authorization as a signal of management's capital-return appetite.

ZSQR.brief: Z Squared Inc. (Nasdaq: ZSQR) filed an 8-K reporting completion on September 8, 2026 of its acquisition of 100% of the membership interests of Paradox Data, LLC from Paradox Infrastructure LLC under a July 31, 2026 Membership Interest Purchase Agreement. Consideration was 5,000 shares of newly designated Series A Convertible Preferred Stock with $5,000,000 aggregate stated value. Concurrently the target, as landlord, leased the El Dorado, Arkansas bitcoin mining premises back to seller at $1.00 annual base rent, with Z Squared capping its relocation liability at $500,000. Watch preferred conversion terms, overhang, and power-transition risk.

JEF.brief: Jefferies Financial Group Inc. filed an 8-K announcing the pricing of a public offering of $1.1 billion aggregate principal amount of 5.125% Senior Notes due 2031, with an effective yield of 5.304% and maturity on April 28, 2031. The offering is expected to settle on April 28, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. Net proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes. Jefferies LLC acted as sole global coordinator and joint book-runner. This is a routine debt capital markets transaction and does not constitute a special situation event; therefore, no deal terms are applicable.

UHT.brief: Universal Health Realty Income Trust filed an 8-K on April 21, 2026, to report entering into a First Amendment to its Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement. The amendment adds a $50 million incremental term loan facility, adjusts the minimum tangible net worth requirement to $100 million, and removes the 0.10% Term SOFR Adjustment. A new subsidiary was added as a guarantor. The term loan matures on September 30, 2028, with interest based on SOFR or Base Rate plus a leverage-based margin. This is a routine debt financing modification, not a special situation. Watch for ongoing leverage ratio compliance and any future capital structure changes.

FBK.brief: FB Financial Corp filed an 8-K announcing its board renewed a stock repurchase plan authorizing up to $175 million of common stock repurchases, running until June 30, 2027, replacing a prior authorization. Repurchases may be executed via open market or private transactions under Rule 10b-18, with timing and amount subject to market conditions, regulatory constraints, and alternative capital uses. No specific price, premium, or advisor was disclosed. The plan reflects disciplined capital management and can be suspended anytime. Watch for execution pace and potential buyback impact on share price given the open-ended mechanics.

RNGR.brief: Ranger Energy Services filed an 8-K on October 9, 2026, reporting completion on October 8, 2026 of its previously announced acquisition of STEP Energy Services' U.S. coiled tubing, fluid and nitrogen pumping, and related well services assets under an Asset Purchase Agreement dated August 31, 2026. Aggregate consideration was approximately $27.5 million, comprising $22.5 million cash plus 307,503 Class A shares valued at $5.0 million based on the trailing 30-trading-day VWAP, subject to customary post-closing adjustments. Cash was funded via the Wells Fargo revolving credit facility. No board recommendation or advisor was disclosed. Watch integration execution, earn-out-free asset deal structure, and delayed financial statement filings due within 71 days.

VELO.brief: Velo3D filed an 8-K reporting a firm commitment underwritten registered direct offering of 3,571,428 shares at $14.00/share, expected gross proceeds of $50 million, closing April 28, 2026. Cantor Fitzgerald is sole underwriter, receiving a 6.0% discount. Shares are sold under an effective shelf registration statement. Lock-up of 60 days applies to directors, officers, and certain stockholders. This is a capital raise, not a tender offer; categorized as Issuer Tenders only per the schema's label for an issuer sale. Watch for market reception and potential dilution.

WSBF.brief: Waterstone Financial, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing its Board authorized an additional 2,000,000 share repurchase under its existing program, increasing total availability to 2,148,285 shares (~11.9% of outstanding). No price, premium, or date specified. The open-market/block/private repurchases may occur under a Rule 10b5-1 plan; shares become authorized but unissued. Timing depends on market conditions and liquidity. Watch for buyback execution pace and potential EPS accretion.

FLXS.brief: Flexsteel Industries filed an 8-K reporting a privately-negotiated stock repurchase agreement with director F. Brooks Bertsch and family entities. The company repurchased 1,279,870 shares (≈24% of outstanding) at $47.00/share, a 2.5% discount to the April 24 close, for total ~$60.2 million. A special committee of independent directors recommended, and the board (with Bertsch recused) approved the deal. The repurchase closed on April 28, 2026, funded via cash and credit facility. The transaction is supplemental to an existing buyback program. Bertsch resigned as director concurrently. Watch for potential overhang reduction and future capital allocation decisions; no arbitrage angle as price was at a discount.

GILD.brief: Gilead Sciences filed an 8-K announcing completion of its acquisition of Arcellx, Inc. via a tender offer and merger. The consideration was $115.00 per share in cash plus one CVR (earn-out of $5.00 per CVR payable in 2030 if Arcellx's anito-cel product cumulative worldwide sales exceed $6.0B by December 31, 2029). The tender offer expired on April 27, 2026, with the merger effective April 28, 2026. No board recommendation or advisors are noted. The CVR includes a risk-arb angle as payout depends on commercial milestones; watch for future sales disclosures.

UMBF.brief: UMB Financial Corp filed an 8-K on April 28, 2026, announcing a $0.43 quarterly common dividend and a Series B preferred dividend of $193.75 per share ($0.484375 per depositary share). The board also authorized repurchase of up to two million common shares through the board meeting following the 2027 annual meeting. No price, premium, or advisor details are provided. These capital return actions are routine shareholder distributions. What to watch: actual share repurchase pace and any future capital management updates.

AFRI.brief: Forafric Global PLC filed a Form 6-K on October 7, 2026, disclosing a letter of intent to acquire 100% of AL NASR Industries Systems, a recently formed Moroccan defense platform holding minority stakes in two licensed defense manufacturing ventures. No price per share, total consideration or premium was disclosed; expected closing is Q4 2026, subject to due diligence, definitive agreements, board approval based on final terms, and regulatory approvals. AL NASR is controlled by Forafric's ultimate beneficial owner, making this a related-party transaction. Watch related-party valuation fairness, Moroccan Law 10-20 licensing scrutiny, and whether a definitive deal or financing materializes.

EIG.brief: Employers Holdings, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting Q1 2026 results, declaring a regular quarterly dividend of $0.34 per share payable May 27, 2026 to holders of record May 13, 2026, and authorizing a new $125 million share repurchase program (2026 Program) effective May 4, 2026 through December 31, 2027, replacing a fully utilized prior program. Repurchases may occur in open market or private transactions under Rules 10b5-1 and 10b-18. The dividend increase and buyback authorization signal a capital return to shareholders. Watch execution pace and any future program extensions.

QUIK.brief: QuickLogic filed an 8-K on April 29, 2026, reporting entry into a $10.0 million secured revolving credit facility with Sunflower Bank, N.A., maturing April 24, 2029. Interest is the greater of 5.50% or Prime plus 0.50%, secured by substantially all assets, with a $30,000 annual fee. Proceeds are for working capital and general corporate purposes. Covenants include a 7-month liquidity requirement and limitations on debt, liens, investments, and acquisitions. This is a routine credit facility, not a special situation.

YSS.brief: York Space Systems Inc. filed an 8-K to report entry into a definitive merger agreement to acquire All.Space Holdings, Inc. for $355 million in a combination of cash and stock. At closing, York will pay approximately $155 million in cash and issue up to 5.9 million shares of its common stock, with customary adjustments for cash, debt, transaction expenses, and working capital. An adjustment escrow ($5M), reorganization indemnification escrow ($1.5M), special indemnification escrow (BGP 750k converted to USD), and an expense reserve ($1M) are established. The acquisition will be effected through a series of contributions making All.Space an indirect wholly owned subsidiary. No board recommendation or advisor is named in the filing. Watch for shareholder approvals, regulatory clearances, and potential competing bids as closing conditions.

ACR.brief: ACRES Commercial Realty Corp. filed an 8-K on August 6, 2026, reporting entry into and termination of material definitive agreements, completion of an acquisition/disposition, creation of a direct financial obligation, unregistered sales of equity securities, and officer departures. The excerpt details a First Amendment to a Loan and Servicing Agreement, increasing term loan commitments to $185 million with scheduled principal payments through July 2033. No specific special-situation event such as a merger, tender offer, or strategic review is concretely described in the excerpt; the items suggest multiple transactions but lack explicit deal terms, pricing, or board recommendations.

BDC.brief: Belden Inc. filed an 8-K to report the completion of its acquisition of Vistance Networks’ RUCKUS reporting segment (the "RUCKUS Acquisition") on July 1, 2026, pursuant to a Purchase Agreement dated April 29, 2026. To fund the transaction, Belden entered into a $1,850 million senior secured term loan credit facility maturing July 1, 2033, bearing interest at term SOFR + 2.25% or base rate + 1.25% p.a., with customary covenants. No per-share price, premium, or valuation details were disclosed. The Transaction is closed. What to watch: post-acquisition integration and debt-service metrics.

BLDR.brief: Builders FirstSource filed an 8-K reporting Q1 2026 results (net sales $3.3B, down 10.1%; net loss $47.4M) and announced a $500M share repurchase authorization. The buyback is a capital-return event, not a formal tender offer; the board authorized it without stated expiration. No price per share, premium, or advisor was specified. The program will be funded from operations, allowing open-market purchases at management's discretion. Watch for actual repurchase cadence and potential EPS accretion; the risk-arb angle is limited as this is an open-market program, not a tender.

ESTA.brief: Establishment Labs Holdings Inc. filed an 8-K reporting entry into an amended Credit Agreement on April 30, 2026, with Oaktree Fund Administration as administrative agent. The agreement provides up to $300 million in term loans in two tranches: a $265 million Tranche E advanced at closing and an up to $35 million Tranche F subject to mutual consent. Proceeds primarily repay $259 million of prior indebtedness and for working capital. Loans mature April 30, 2031, bear interest at 8.75% per annum, with a PIK toggle on the first anniversary. This refinancing is a routine credit facility amendment, not a special-situation event. There are no deal terms to report.

ILMN.brief: Illumina filed an 8-K to disclose a settlement reached August 21, 2025, in Icahn Partners LP v. DeSouza (Del. Ch.), a stockholder derivative suit over the GRAIL acquisition. The Release Agreement provides for mutual releases and no payments, with dismissal with prejudice as to plaintiffs only, subject to court approval. A dismissal hearing is scheduled November 2, 2026. No deal terms apply. The event is a litigation settlement, not a strategic or capital markets transaction. Watch for court approval and potential objector challenges.

INSG.brief: Inseego closed its purchase of Nokia Solutions and Networks Oy's fixed wireless access business, paying 1,163,693 Inseego shares, warrants on 521,139 shares, and assumed liabilities; Nokia simultaneously invested $10M cash for 775,795 shares plus warrants on 290,569 shares, giving Nokia roughly 11% of Inseego pre-warrant exercise. Warrant strike was reset to $4.26, the 30-trading-day VWAP through September 25, 2026. An amendment adds a $10M Nokia cash payment by October 15, 2026, funding device-OS interoperability engineering. Terms rest entirely on stock and cash, with no stated premium. Watch Nokia's ~11% stake, warrant overhang, and integration execution.

KAI.brief: Kadant Inc. filed an 8-K announcing its subsidiary Kadant Holdings GmbH completed the acquisition of voestalpine BÜHLER Profil GmbH & Co KG and voestalpine BÜHLER Profil VerwaltungsGmbH (now renamed Kadant Profil) for approximately €157.0 million in cash, subject to customary adjustments. The acquisition was primarily financed via borrowings under Kadant's revolving credit facility. Kadant Profil will be integrated into Kadant's Industrial Processing reporting segment. No board recommendation or advisor was disclosed. The purchase price implies a straightforward cash deal with no premium stated. The 8-K does not provide a timeline for purchase accounting or synergies. Watch for future earnings integration updates; no risk-arb angle as deal is closed.

MARA.brief: MARA Holdings' subsidiary Volt Texas amended its July 2, 2026 membership interest purchase agreement with HIF USA for MAT 1177 LLC, which holds Texas land and rights to 2,000 MW of power capacity. The September 21, 2026 first amendment posted a $100 million security deposit with the electric utility, restructured milestone payments tied to regulatory approvals into two installments, and revised project milestones. Consideration remains post-closing milestone-based, with no per-share price stated. Watch Texas regulatory audit outcomes, milestone timing, and whether MARA draws the refundable deposit, affecting deal economics.

NREF.brief: NexPoint Real Estate Finance entered into a $375M senior secured term loan with Mizuho Capital Markets, drawing $310M on April 29, 2026, to refinance $185.2M of its 5.75% senior unsecured notes due May 1, 2026. The facility matures May 1, 2029, with two six-month extension options, and bears interest at SOFR+4.0% (2.0% floor). Concurrently, a Total Return Swap with Mizuho reduces net interest cost to SOFR+2.45%. The filing is a financing transaction, not a special situation, as it involves ordinary debt refinancing and derivative hedging without change-of-control, activist, or strategic review elements.

ORKA.brief: Oruka Therapeutics filed an 8-K reporting preliminary cash of ~$496M as of March 31, 2026 (Item 2.02) and entry into an underwriting agreement on April 28, 2026 for a primary public offering of 9,660,000 shares at $72.50/share, with a 30-day greenshoe option for up to 1,449,000 additional shares (Item 8.01). Underwriters include Leerink, TD Securities, Goldman Sachs, Stifel, and Guggenheim. No special-situation M&A, activism, restructuring, or other event; it is a routine equity capital raise disclosed via 8-K. Watch for closing and share dilution.

PRGO.brief: Perrigo Company plc filed an 8-K announcing the completion of the sale of its Dermacosmetics Business to an affiliate of Karo Healthcare AB, managed by KKR. The transaction closed on April 30, 2026, with a cash payment of €305.6 million, including net working capital adjustments, and up to €27.0 million in contingent consideration over three years. The board recommended the sale, though no specific advisors were named. The deal was executed via a Master Sale and Purchase Agreement with Kairos Bidco AB. Watch for further updates on the contingent earn-out and potential use of proceeds by Perrigo.

OPTX.brief: Syntec Optics Holdings, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing an underwritten public offering of 2,857,142 shares at $7.00 per share, with a 30-day option for additional 428,571 shares. Gross proceeds ~$20M; net proceeds intended for acquisitions, working capital, debt repayment; includes customary lock-ups and a 90-day issuance standstill. This is a capital raise, not a transformative special situation. [Non-US filing not applicable.] Watch for closing on April 30, 2026.

SNDR.brief: Schneider National filed an 8-K announcing a quarterly cash dividend of $0.10 per share on Class A and B common stock, approved by its Board on April 29, 2026. The dividend is payable to holders of record as of June 12, 2026, and expected to be paid on July 10, 2026. This is a routine capital return event, not a special situation. No premium, price per share, or deal structure is involved. The filing is a standard dividend declaration with no strategic or structural complexity. Watch for consistent dividend policy as a signal of shareholder return commitment.

TIPT.brief: Tiptree Inc. filed an 8-K reporting its entry into a Stock Purchase Agreement on July 28, 2026, to acquire all equity interests of Universal Shield Insurance Group, Inc. (USIG) from Shield Holdings, UH Partners, and individual sellers. The purchase price is $100 million, subject to leakage adjustments. The transaction is subject to customary conditions, including insurance regulatory approvals. Closing is expected in Q1 2027. Tiptree also reported Q2 2026 results in a related press release. Watch for regulatory approval timeline and any leakage adjustments affecting final price.

OLED.brief: Universal Display Corp filed an 8-K announcing a $400 million share repurchase program authorized by its board, in addition to first-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings. The repurchase is open-market, with no fixed expiration date. As an issuer buyback, this signals capital return to shareholders amid measured near-term market conditions but long-term OLED growth. No financial advisor or premium is specified. Watch execution pace and any insider selling patterns for capital allocation signaling.

CWEN-A.brief: Clearway Energy, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing that on October 1, 2026, its subsidiary Honeycomb 2 Purchaser LLC entered a Membership Interest Purchase Agreement with Honeycomb 2 CE Seller LLC, a Clearway Energy Group affiliate, to acquire membership interests in Honeycomb 2 TargetCo LLC, which will indirectly own Escalante BESS II, Escalante BESS III and Granite Mountain BESS West LLC. Base purchase price is approximately $119 million cash, subject to financial-model adjustments; the three Utah battery storage projects total roughly 210 MW. Closing expected in Q4 2027, subject to customary conditions and third-party actions; no board recommendation or advisor named. Post-closing, Purchaser holds 100% Class A units while CEG affiliate Clearway Renew LLC retains 100% Class C units, a structural overhang; watch regulatory and third-party approvals given the long-dated close.

FHN.brief: The New York Stock Exchange filed Form 25-NSE to delist and deregister First Horizon Corp's Depositary Shares (each representing a 1/400th interest in Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock, Series C) due to full redemption, maturity, or retirement on May 1, 2026. Redemption funds were deposited and made available to holders on the same date. Trading was suspended effective May 1, with delisting effective May 12, 2026. This is a routine event-driven delisting for a called security; no premium, board recommendation, or deal structure applies. No risk-arb angle as there is no pending merger or contested event.

AUB.brief: Atlantic Union Bankshares Corp filed an 8-K announcing a $250 million share repurchase program and a quarterly dividend of $0.37 per common share. The buyback may be executed via open market or private transactions, including Rule 10b5-1 plans, through May 5, 2027. Management has discretion over timing and amounts; the program is non-binding. The board declared dividends on common and Series A preferred stock. This is an ordinary capital allocation action; no takeover/merger or activist campaign. Watch for repurchase pace and any acceleration if shares trade at a discount to tangible book value.

COSO.brief: CoastalSouth Bancshares, Inc. disclosed on Form 8-K that its Board of Directors authorized a $15 million stock repurchase plan, effective May 1, 2026, through April 30, 2027. The plan allows open-market, accelerated share repurchase, or privately negotiated purchases under Rule 10b-18 and Rule 10b5-1 trading plans. No specific price, premium, or share count is disclosed. The company is not obligated to repurchase any shares and may modify or discontinue the plan at any time. Watch for periodic repurchase activity and potential EPS accretion; no risk-arb angle as this is an issuer capital return.

FGBI.brief: First Guaranty Bancshares, Inc. filed an 8-K under Item 8.01 Other Events to announce a quarterly cash dividend on its 6.75% Series A Fixed-Rate Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock. On April 16, 2026, the Board declared a $16.875 per share preferred dividend ($0.421875 per Depositary Share) payable on June 1, 2026 to holders of record as of May 15, 2026. The Series A Preferred Stock dividend will be paid to the depositary, which will distribute to Depositary Share holders. No recommendation, advisor, premium, or change in corporate structure is noted. This is a routine dividend declaration, not a special situation; the filing serves as public notice. Monitor for any suspension or rate change.

GHC.brief: On May 1, 2026, Graham Holdings Co disclosed via Form 8-K that its subsidiary Kaplan closed the sale of the Kaplan Languages Group (KLG). No purchase price, premium, or buyer name is disclosed; the company preliminarily expects a $60 million U.S. income tax benefit in 2026 from the transaction. No board recommendation or advisors are named. The filing is minimal, serving as a closing notice under Item 8.01. Watch for subsequent quarterly filings to reveal after-tax gain and any earnout terms; risk-arb spread is not calculable without price terms.

INDB.brief: Independent Bank Corp announced a $200 million stock buyback plan authorized by its Board effective April 30, 2026. Repurchases will commence after completion of the $10.5 million remaining under a July 2025 plan, with open-market and private transactions and Rule 10b5-1 plans. The program expires April 29, 2027, and may be modified or discontinued. No pricing details were provided beyond the aggregate authorization. The filing is an 8-K Item 8.01 Other Events. This is a routine capital return announcement; no special-situation activating events such as a tender offer or going-private transaction are involved.

NKSH.brief: National Bankshares, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a semi-annual dividend of $0.75/share and renewal of a share repurchase authorization up to 250,000 shares from June 2026 through May 2027. The dividend payment is June 1, 2026, to holders of record May 26, 2026. The repurchase plan replaces the expiring plan and management retains discretion on execution. No advisor or board recommendation beyond the standard renewal. The aggregate repurchase represents about 4.2% of shares based on a rough float of ~6 million shares. Watch for actual repurchase pace vs. authorization and implications for capital allocation.

OC.brief: Owens Corning filed an 8-K on April 30, 2026, disclosing the completion of the sale of substantially all of its global glass reinforcements business to affiliates of the Praana Group (Triumph Composites Private Limited and 3B Lux S.r.l.). The enterprise value was revised downward from $755 million to $645 million via an amendment on April 14, 2026. Net after-tax cash proceeds are expected to be approximately $280 million. The company intends to use proceeds for organic growth and shareholder returns. No board recommendation or advisors are named. The transaction closed on April 30, 2026. Watch for execution of capital allocation plans and potential reinvestment or buyback announcements.

RGA.brief: Reinsurance Group of America filed an 8-K announcing full redemption of its $400M 5.75% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Subordinated Debentures due 2056 (CUSIP RZB). Redemption effective June 15, 2026 at 100% of principal plus accrued interest. No board recommendation or advisor named; redemption is mandatory under indenture terms. The notice triggers a debt reduction and lower interest expense, representing a capital return to debtholders at par. Watch for any refinancing plans or balance-sheet deleveraging signals from management; typical risk-arb is minimal as redemption is at par with no premium.

USCB.brief: USCB Financial Holdings and its subsidiary filed an 8-K reporting the mutual termination of a Side Letter Agreement with Patriot Financial Partners, which owned 10.2% of the company's voting stock. The termination followed the resignation of Patriot's board representative. The agreement with another party, Priam, remains in effect. No financial terms, premiums, or transaction values were disclosed. The filing reflects a governance/relationship change rather than a special situation.

WT.brief: WisdomTree filed an 8-K reporting privately negotiated repurchases of $51.9M aggregate principal of its 3.25% Convertible Senior Notes due 2029 for ~$87.3M cash (a premium over par reflecting the conversion value). The transactions, expected to close June 1, 2026, will leave $18.1M of the Notes outstanding. No tender offer is used; these are issuer-initiated repurchases to reduce leverage/conversion overhang, not a formal debt tender. The filing lacks board recommendation or advisor roles. Watch for the closing condition and potential impact on diluted share count; the premium indicates embedded conversion economics.

MFP.brief: Midera Food Processing, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of its spin-off from The Middleby Corporation. Middleby distributed 100% of Midera's common stock to its stockholders, leaving Middleby with no ownership interest. The spin-off was effectuated through a Separation and Distribution Agreement entered on July 5, 2026, along with a Tax Matters Agreement. Midera holds Middleby's former food processing business. The filing formalizes the separation, governance, and tax arrangements between the two entities. Watch for post-spin trading dynamics and any subsequent shareholder actions.

AMRC.brief: Ameresco filed an 8-K reporting the closing of a joint venture contribution and equity purchase agreement. Through its subsidiary, it contributed its biogas business to Neogenyx Fuels LLC in exchange for a 70% equity interest. HASI affiliate invested $400 million, receiving a 30% interest; $100 million cash was paid to Ameresco at close, ~$58 million used to reduce a loan, and the remainder contributed to the JV. No board recommendation or advisor named. Structurally, this is a spin-off-like transfer of assets into a separate entity with external capital. Watch for operational integration, JV governance, and potential monetization of the retained stake.

AURA.brief: Aura Biosciences filed an 8-K disclosing a stock purchase agreement with Matrix Capital Management Master Fund, LP to repurchase up to 6,922,870 shares (all held by Matrix) at $5.64 per share, the same price as the concurrent equity offering. The repurchase is conditioned on closing of that offering and funded from net proceeds exceeding $200M. The transaction, approved by the audit committee, reduces Matrix's ~10.8% stake. Shares become authorized but unissued. The expected closing is no earlier than two business days after the equity offering's close. Watch for the equity offering's completion as a condition precedent.

CWK.brief: Cushman & Wakefield Ltd. filed an 8-K announcing that its wholly-owned subsidiary, the Issuer, elected to partially redeem $100 million of its outstanding $650 million 6.750% Senior Secured Notes due May 2028. The redemption price is 100% of principal plus accrued interest, with the redemption date set for May 15, 2026. This is a debt reduction / capital return move; no board recommendation, advisor, or premium. The trustee, Wilmington Trust, will execute the notice. Watch for further liability management or potential refinancing. Risk-arb angle: None; it is a straightforward partial redemption.

DRH.brief: DiamondRock Hospitality filed an 8-K on October 8, 2026, disclosing completion of its acquisition of The Bellmoor Inn & Spa, a 79-room hotel in Rehoboth Beach, Delaware, for $31.0 million in cash. The deal closed October 1, 2026, and was announced via press release furnished under Regulation FD. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or earnings contribution was disclosed. The transaction expands DiamondRock's leisure/resort portfolio, funded presumably from balance sheet capacity or its credit facility. Watch for updated 2026 guidance, cap-rate commentary, and any follow-on dispositions under the REIT's capital-recycling strategy.

MYFW.brief: First Western Financial Inc filed an 8-K to disclose board authorization of a $5 million common stock repurchase plan, effective June 12, 2026, for one year. The Federal Reserve issued a non-objection on April 29, 2026. Repurchases may occur in open market, privately negotiated transactions, or via Rule 10b5-1 plans. No specific price per share or premium is stated. The plan is discretionary, with no obligation to acquire a set dollar amount. This is a routine share buyback—a capital return event. Watch for execution pace and any trading plan adoption; minimal risk-arb angle due to open-market nature.

PUMP.brief: ProPetro Holding Corp. filed an 8-K reporting the issuance of $690M aggregate principal amount of 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2031, including the full exercise of the initial purchasers' option for an additional $90M. The notes are senior unsecured obligations maturing November 15, 2031, with an initial conversion rate of 43.1616 shares per $1,000 principal (conversion price ~$23.17 per share, a ~37.5% premium over the $16.85 closing price on May 4, 2026). The company may settle conversions in cash, stock, or a combination. Notes are redeemable at par on or after May 15, 2029. This convertible offering serves as a capital return mechanism; watch for dilution management and potential share repurchases with proceeds.

UDR.brief: UDR, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing its Board authorized a 25 million share increase to its existing buyback program, making total authorization ~30 million shares (over $1 billion at current prices). Repurchases may occur via open-market, block, or private deals with no expiration date. The filing is a straightforward capital return announcement; board recommendation is implicit given the authorization. No advisor was named. The existing January 2008 program is unchanged. The filing does not involve a merger, tender offer, activist campaign, or strategic review. What to watch: pace of execution and any impact on share price and capital allocation strategy.
