VABK.brief: Virginia National Bankshares Corporation filed an 8-K on October 8, 2026, disclosing that on October 6, 2026 its board authorized a share repurchase plan for up to $18.7 million of common stock, par value $2.50 per share, through October 5, 2027. Repurchases may occur in the open market, privately negotiated transactions or otherwise, structured within Rule 10b-18 pricing and volume limits, with possible Rule 10b5-1 plans. No price per share or premium was stated. The plan is discretionary and may be extended, modified, suspended or discontinued. Watch buyback pace versus capital and liquidity.

ZION.brief: Zions Bancorporation filed an 8-K reporting the sale of 460,153 Class B-1 shares of Visa Inc. on May 4, 2026, for $215 million in aggregate proceeds, generating a pre-tax gain of approximately the same amount in Q2 2026. The shares were originally received in 2007 from a Visa restructuring and IPO. No board recommendation, advisors, premium, or deal mechanics are disclosed as this is a portfolio asset sale, not a corporate action. Watch for any subsequent disclosures on capital deployment of the gain; no risk-arb angle applies.

AVTX.brief: Avalo Therapeutics filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement for an underwritten public offering of common stock and pre-funded warrants. The offering includes shares and pre-funded warrants exercisable at $0.001 below the public price, with an ownership limitation of 4.99% or 9.99%. The last reported sale price on May 4, 2026, was $13.78 per share. Underwriters include Leerink Partners, TD Cowen, and BofA Securities, with a 30-day greenshoe option. This capital-raising event is not a special situation; it is a routine equity shelf takedown. The filing does not indicate a strategic review or M&A event.

BHVN.brief: Biohaven Ltd. disclosed via Form 8-K that its subsidiary entered into a licensing agreement with SK Biopharmaceuticals, granting exclusive worldwide rights to its Kv7 platform including opakalim. Terms include a $400M upfront (deferred), up to $150M milestones, and tiered royalties. This is a strategic out-licensing deal, not a typical special-situation corporate event, so it does not map cleanly to the specified categories.

EXEL.brief: Exelixis filed an 8-K reporting Q1 2026 earnings and announcing a new stock repurchase authorization of up to $750 million by December 31, 2027. The board authorized the buyback, enhancing existing capital return programs. No specific price or premium is stated. The program is open-market, with mechanics typical of discretionary repurchases. The filing is primarily an earnings release with a supplementary buyback announcement. Watch for execution pace and potential impact on share count and EPS.

MSBI.brief: Midland States Bancorp filed an 8-K announcing its board approved an amendment to increase its stock repurchase authorization from $25 million to $45 million and extended the program's expiration to December 31, 2026. As of the filing, the company had already repurchased 923,837 shares at an average price of $21.46, totaling $19.8 million of the original authorization. The program is subject to market conditions, corporate and regulatory requirements, and may be suspended or discontinued at any time. Watch for future buyback execution pace and any Rule 10b5-1 plan amendments as indicators of management's view on valuation.

OCGN.brief: Ocugen, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing the completion of a $115.0 million private offering of 6.75% Convertible Senior Notes due 2034 issued under an indenture with U.S. Bank Trust Company, N.A. as trustee. The notes are unsecured, rank senior to subordinated debt, and mature May 15, 2034. Interest is payable semi-annually starting November 15, 2026. Conversion is cash-settled until a reserved share effective date, subject to Nasdaq Exchange Cap of 67,629,947 shares pending stockholder approval. No premium, acquisition, or strategic event; this is a financing transaction. Watch for stockholder vote on share issuance and potential dilution management.

MYPS.brief: PLAYSTUDIOS filed an 8-K announcing a 1-for-10 reverse stock split of its Class A and Class B common stock, effective 5:00 p.m. ET September 30, 2026, with split-adjusted Nasdaq trading beginning October 1, 2026 under ticker MYPS. The company also disclosed buying back roughly 4.3 million Class A shares during Q3 2026 through September 24 for $3.0 million, averaging about $0.71 per share, under an existing Rule 10b5-1 plan. Management continues evaluating further capital-return opportunities. Watch for post-split liquidity, continued buyback pace, and any Nasdaq minimum-bid compliance angle.

PMI.brief: Picard Medical disclosed on Form 8-K that NYSE American accepted its compliance plan to remedy non-compliance with continued listing standards Sections 1003(a)(i) and (ii), triggered by stockholders' equity of $3.8M (Dec 2025) and a $(1.4M) deficit (Mar 2026) plus recent losses. The plan allows continued listing under ticker PMI subject to achieving prescribed milestones with quarterly NYSE American review, within an 18-month cure period from the original non-compliance notice. The company issued a press release on July 27, 2026. Watch: ability to execute operational and financial milestones to avoid eventual delisting.

RDW.brief: Redwire Corp filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement for an at-the-market (ATM) equity offering of up to $350 million in common stock under a new sales agreement with multiple agents. The filing replaces a prior November 2025 agreement, under which $249.7 million had already been sold. Shares are sold on a commercially reasonable efforts basis on NYSE via agents earning up to 3.0% commission. Last reported price was $8.69. Proceeds are for general corporate purposes. No special-situation catalyst; routine equity shelf takedown.

MASS.brief: 908 Devices Inc. filed an 8-K reporting its acquisition of NIRLAB SA for $15M headline price (subject to adjustments), consisting of $13M cash and 293,368 shares of 908 Devices common stock. The stock consideration was priced at the higher of the 30-day VWAP closing price or a $5.88 floor. An additional $8M in earn-out consideration is payable. The board deemed the terms fair and authorized the deal. Sellers provided customary representations; a general holdback secures post-closing obligations and releases after 12 months. The transaction closed on May 4, 2026. To watch: earn-out milestones and integration of NIRLAB's spectroscopy tech.

BVFL.brief: BV Financial, Inc. filed an 8-K on May 5, 2026, disclosing the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond non-objection to a stock repurchase program of up to 10% of outstanding common stock (~861,000 shares). Repurchases will commence after the current program finishes (~45,000 shares remaining). Purchases may be made via open market, private transactions, block trades, or a Rule 10b5-1 plan. No specific price, premium, or timeline was given. The board has not retained an outside advisor. The filing is a routine capital return announcement, not a special situation. Watch: execution pace and any future accretive actions.

XRN.brief: Chiron Real Estate Inc. filed an 8-K/A amending its October 5, 2026 initial report to supply audited financials and supplemental operating data on its completed acquisition of The Pinnacle, a senior housing community in North Bethesda, Maryland, bought for $173.2 million under an agreement dated on or before the October 1, 2026 closing. The newly opened property was mid-lease-up: 5% occupancy at June 30, 2026, 31% at September 30 and October 1, with 54 leased units at $12,369 average monthly rent. No board recommendation or advisor named. Watch lease-up velocity toward management's 2029 stabilization target of over 7% yield-on-cost.

ERII.brief: Energy Recovery, Inc. disclosed on Form 8-K that CEO David Moon will retire after a successor is appointed, and CFO Mike Mancini resigned effective May 6, 2026, with no financial or accounting disagreements. Interim CFO Aidan Ryan was appointed. The filing reports Q1 2026 earnings but the material event is the simultaneous departure of two top executives. No financial terms, premium, or board recommendation are given. The transition is voluntary but abrupt; watch for a permanent CEO hire and any strategic shift under new leadership. No risk-arb angle.

NXDR.brief: Nextdoor Holdings filed a Form 25 on October 13, 2026, notifying the SEC of the removal of its Class A common stock, par value $0.0001 per share, from listing and registration on the New York Stock Exchange. The filing cites Rule 17 CFR 240.12d2-2(b), indicating the Exchange complied with its rules to strike the class, rather than a voluntary issuer withdrawal under 12d2-2(c). The form was signed by Indrajit Ponnambalam, Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer. No stake percentage, per-share price, premium, expected close date, board recommendation, advisor, collateral, overhang, ownership split, or regulatory clock is stated. The filing is the US equivalent of a delisting notification. What to watch: the underlying transaction that triggered the delisting, since the Form 25 alone leaves deal economics and any merger consideration unresolved.

MBGL.brief: Mobility Global Inc. filed an 8-K reporting its spin-off from S&P Global Inc., effective July 1, 2026. S&P Global distributed 100% of Mobility Global common stock to its shareholders on a one-for-one basis as of the June 15 record date. The separation, involving restructuring transactions and several ancillary agreements (Separation and Distribution, Tax Matters, Transition Services, Employee Matters), left Mobility Global an independent public company listing on NYSE under "MBGL" with no retained ownership by S&P Global. No premium, price, or advisor is specified. The distribution was tax-free to S&P Global shareholders. Watch for Mobility Global's first earnings as a standalone entity and any post-spin trading dynamics.

AORT.brief: Artivion, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing the completion of its acquisition of Endospan Ltd., an Israeli aortic-stability-device company. The base purchase price was $175.0 million, paid entirely in cash, with a net payment of approximately $131.3 million after offsetting intercompany loans. Contingent consideration of up to $200.0 million is payable based on future milestones. The transaction was executed via a Securities Purchase Option Agreement dated September 11, 2019, as amended. Escrow accounts of $16.5 million (indemnity) and $1.0 million (adjustment) were established. No board recommendation or advisor is named. Artivion financed the deal from internal sources. The acquisition closed immediately upon filing. Watch for integration of the Nexus product line and potential milestone achievements triggering contingent payments.

BBT.brief: Beacon Financial Corp filed an 8-K under Item 8.01 to inform stockholders that it will propose a charter amendment at the next annual meeting to allow director removal with or without cause by a majority vote, aligning with DGCL Section 141(k). No financial terms, stake percentage, premium, or advisor are mentioned. The board decided not to call a special meeting due to cost. This is a governance update, not a special-situation event such as a merger or activist campaign. No deal mechanics or risk-arb angle apply.

FCCO.brief: First Community Corp announced a share repurchase plan authorized by its Board, allocating up to $7.5 million (approx. 3.4% of total shareholders' equity as of Mar 31, 2026) to buy back common stock through May 5, 2027. Repurchases may occur via open market or privately negotiated transactions at management's discretion, subject to market conditions, share issuance, and regulatory requirements. The plan is not a binding obligation and can be suspended or cancelled at any time. No specific price, premium, or tender offer mechanics are outlined. Focus on execution pace, actual buyback volumes, and potential EPS accretion.

GTN.brief: Gray Media filed an 8-K reporting the repurchase of $100M of its 10.500% senior secured first lien notes due 2029 and $20M of its 5.375% senior notes due 2031, both at par plus accrued interest in a privately negotiated transaction on July 21, 2026. Funded via cash on hand and revolver borrowings, this debt reduction improves capital structure and signals management's confidence in cash flows. With no premium or tender offer mechanics, watch for further debt management or leverage metric improvement as ongoing capital allocation focus.

GEN.brief: Gen Digital Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing financial results and a Board-approved restructuring program on May 5, 2026. The restructuring aims to streamline operations and adopt AI technologies, with expected charges of ~$50M implemented over twelve months. This is an internal cost-reduction initiative; no acquisition, divestiture, or other special situation event is identified. The restructuring is described as part of ongoing transformation efforts, with estimates subject to change. The disclosure is strategic, but lacks specific details like job cuts or advisors, and the program is not a standalone event typically triggering a major category. Watch for future updates on costs and timing.

LTH.brief: Life Time Group Holdings, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a share repurchase from affiliates of Leonard Green, TPG, and Partners Group. The company bought 2,192,500 shares at ~$28.60 each for ~$62.7 million in a private transaction. The repurchase was authorized under a board-approved stock buyback program from February 2026. Mechanics: the deal was a private sale exempt from registration, reducing overhang from large sponsors. What to watch: the company may continue repurchases under its existing program; no premium or discount relative to market was disclosed, so the risk-arb angle is minimal.

PCTY.brief: Paylocity Holding Corp filed an 8-K on May 7, 2026, announcing its board approved a $1 billion increase to its existing share repurchase program, supplementing the $350 million remaining as of March 31, 2026. The program allows repurchases via open market, 10b5-1 plans, or private transactions, with timing and amount dependent on market conditions and other factors. No specific price or expiration was set; the program does not obligate repurchase of any shares and may be modified or suspended. This capital return signals management's view of undervaluation; watch for actual buyback pace to gauge commitment.

POST.brief: Post Holdings filed an 8-K disclosing the planned transition of President/CEO Robert V. Vitale to Executive Chairman, effective October 1, 2026, and the appointment of COO Nicolas Catoggio as President/CEO. The board approved the changes on May 5, 2026. No deal terms are provided as this is a management succession event. The filing also includes routine quarterly earnings results. The transition is orderly with sufficient notice, making this a forced/planned departure rather than abrupt. Watch for any strategic shifts under new leadership or potential related activism.

SPT.brief: Sprout Social, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing that its board authorized a $50 million share repurchase program. The program allows the company to buy back its Class A common stock (NASDAQ: SPT) in open-market or privately negotiated transactions. No specific price, premium, or duration was disclosed; execution details will be determined by management. The repurchase is discretionary and may be suspended or terminated at any time. The filing is a routine capital-return event, not a tender offer. Watch for subsequent 10b5-1 plans or actual repurchase disclosures for sizing and execution pace.

AGNT.brief: AGNT, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting completion on September 14, 2026 of a previously disclosed repurchase of 8,693,290 common shares from Frank Selden, trustee of the Gratitude 2022 Trust, for an aggregate $31,991,307.20, implying roughly $3.68 per share. The block was bought at a 10% discount to the 5-day volume-weighted average price to meet the trust's time-sensitive tax and estate administration needs after trustee Penny Sanford's death. The independent Audit Committee unanimously approved the related-person transaction, stating it accelerates the capital return program beyond open-market purchases. Watch execution versus the remaining buyback authorization and any overhang from the trust.

APG.brief: APi Group Corp (NYSE: APG) filed an 8-K announcing a $500M senior unsecured notes offering by its wholly owned subsidiary APi Group DE, Inc. to fund acquisitions of Onyx-Fire Protection Services and Wtech Fire Group, plus an amendment to its existing credit agreement to extend Term Loan B maturity to 2033 and upsize the revolver to $1.0B maturing 2031. The notes are offered under Rule 144A/Regulation S. No specific terms, pricing, or advisor named in excerpt. What to watch: market reception of the notes offering and timing of the acquisitions.

ITRI.brief: Itron, Inc. filed an 8-K on 8 May 2026 reporting that its board authorized a new $200M share repurchase program on 6 May 2026, effective 8 May 2026, over 18 months. Repurchases will be made in open market or via Rule 10b5-1 plans, complying with Rule 10b-18. No price per share, premium, or advisor is stated. The program is discretionary and may be suspended without notice. This is a capital-return event as the issuer directly returns cash to shareholders via buybacks. Watch for execution pace and any trading suspensions.

ALV.brief: Autoliv (issuer) filed an 8-K reporting management approval of a plan to close its manufacturing plants in Türkiye, ceasing steering wheel, airbag, and seatbelt production. The expected pre-tax charge is ~$142M (Q2 2026), with ~$129M cash costs for severance and $13M non-cash write-offs. Annual pre-tax benefit of ~$40M is anticipated from 2027, fully realized by 2028, with ~2,200 employees reduced. The plan addresses excess EMEA capacity. Watch for execution risk in the Turkish Lira currency exposure and regulatory/timing aspects of the closures.

KWY.brief: Kingsway Financial Services Inc. (registrant) filed an 8-K reporting that its subsidiary, Kingsway Warranty Holdings LLC, sold all equity interests of Trinity Warranty Solutions LLC to Trinity Warranty Holding LLC. The aggregate consideration is $5 million cash at closing plus $3 million in secured subordinated promissory notes due in ten years, subject to customary working capital adjustments. The sale closed on May 8, 2026. Representations, warranties, and indemnification provisions include a $50,000 deductible and $500,000 liability cap. What to watch: potential indemnification claims and collection risk on the seller-financed note.

OSPN.brief: OneSpan Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing the termination of its prior stock repurchase program and the adoption of a new $50 million authorization effective May 7, 2026, through May 7, 2028. The program allows open-market, privately negotiated, or tender offer purchases, at the company's discretion based on market conditions. No specific share number or price terms are required. As a capital return event, the buyback signals management's view of undervaluation; watch for actual repurchase cadence and impact on diluted share count. No advisor or board recommendation details are provided.

PHR.brief: Phreesia, Inc. filed an 8-K (Item 8.01) on May 7, 2026, announcing a restructuring plan to reduce operating expenses. The plan involves eliminating approximately 220 positions, about half of which are contractor roles. Costs are expected to be immaterial and incurred primarily in fiscal 2027, with meaningful annualized run-rate savings reflected in the company's Adjusted EBITDA outlook. The board is not specifically mentioned. No advisor named. The restructuring is a cost-saving initiative, not a liquidation or spin-off. Watch for execution risks and actual savings vs. guidance; no risk-arb angle.

RITM.brief: Rithm Capital Corp. filed an 8-K announcing a private offering of $500 million in senior unsecured notes due 2031. The proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes, possibly including debt repayment. The notes are offered to qualified institutional buyers under Rule 144A and to non-U.S. persons under Regulation S. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The offering is unregistered and lacks exchange or registration rights. Structurally, this is a debt capital raising, not a return of capital; classification as a capital return is tentative. Watch for pricing terms and use of proceeds allocation.

SITM.brief: SiTime Corporation filed an 8-K reporting the completion of its acquisition of certain timing business assets from Renesas Electronics America Inc. The deal closed on July 1, 2026, for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $1.5 billion in cash plus 3,558,691 shares of SiTime common stock. The cash portion was funded through cash on hand. Concurrently, SiTime entered into a $200 million senior secured revolving credit facility with Wells Fargo as agent. The board recommended the transaction. The acquisition expands SiTime's product portfolio in the semiconductor timing market, and the stock component creates ongoing exposure to SiTime's performance.

TNL.brief: Travel + Leisure Co. filed an 8-K regarding a $900M private offering of 6.250% senior secured notes due 2031. Net proceeds will redeem all $650M of its outstanding 6.625% secured notes due July 2026, repay borrowings under its secured revolver, and for general corporate purposes. The offering is expected to close May 20, 2026, with redemption conditioned on consummation. This is a liability management transaction, restructuring debt capital rather than an acquisition or divestiture. Watch for closing conditions and redemption execution.

TVTX.brief: Travere Therapeutics filed an 8-K on June 1, 2026, reporting an entry into a license and collaboration agreement with Everest Medicines. The agreement grants Travere exclusive rights to develop and commercialize Everest's BTK inhibitor, civorebrutinib, outside of China and certain Asian countries. Financial terms such as upfront payment, milestones, or royalties were not disclosed. The filing is a material definitive agreement under Item 1.01, containing no merger, tender, or governance change. Watch for future disclosures on financial terms and regulatory milestones.

VRDN.brief: Viridian Therapeutics filed an 8-K announcing the completion of a $250M public offering of 1.75% Convertible Senior Notes due 2032, including full exercise of the underwriters' over-allotment option. The notes are unsecured senior obligations, semiannual interest, convertible at holder's option under certain stock price conditions (130% of conversion price for 20 of 30 trading days). The filing details indenture mechanics and conversion triggers. This is a capital-raising event, returning cash to the company via debt issuance. Watch for dilution risk if conversion conditions are met; the 1.75% coupon and 2032 maturity provide low-cost financing for biotech development.

UP.brief: Wheels Up Experience Inc. filed an 8-K regarding Amendment No. 4 to the Investment and Investor Rights Agreement with Delta Air Lines and other lead lenders. The amendment extends the lock-up restriction on approximately 35.6% of the company's outstanding shares held by Delta until May 22, 2027, and aligns the deadline for filing a shelf registration statement to the same date for Delta, with a conditional earlier date for CIH. This is a contractual extension with no immediate transaction impact; no board recommendation or advisors were noted. The filing primarily addresses share transfer restrictions and registration rights, not a special situation event. Watch for any future shareholder actions or registration triggers.

DIBS.brief: 1stdibs.com filed an 8-K reporting Q3 2026 results alongside a planned CEO transition. CEO David Rosenblatt notified the board on November 2, 2026 of his resignation as CEO effective January 1, 2027, moving to Executive Chairperson; he ceases to be an executive officer. Chief Product and Marketing Officer Bradford Shellhammer succeeds him as CEO and principal executive officer on that date, and is expected to join the board via a one-seat expansion. The orderly, pre-announced succession tempers the abruptness; watch board composition and strategic continuity.

AOSL.brief: Alpha & Omega Semiconductor Ltd filed an 8-K reporting the completion of a sale of approximately 20.3% equity interest in its Chongqing joint venture (power semiconductor packaging, testing, and wafer fabrication) to SIMIC Holdings Co., Ltd. for aggregate cash consideration of $150 million, paid in four installments. The transaction closed on May 11, 2026, when the final installment was received. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The sale was previously disclosed in a July 2025 agreement, and no pro forma financials were provided as the interest was not significant. Watch for future operational or strategic shifts post-divestiture.

EPM.brief: Evolution Petroleum Corp. filed an 8-K announcing it closed a previously announced acquisition of mineral, royalty, and overriding royalty interests in the Midland Basin (Reagan, Upton, Glasscock, Midland, Martin Counties, Texas). The purchase and sale agreement was executed August 18, 2026, and the transaction closed August 20, 2026. The press release states the acquisition is immediately accretive to cash flow per share, with expected production to more than double by fiscal 2029. No financial terms were disclosed; the filing notes advisors and board recommendation were not mentioned. The acquisition enhances Evolution's Permian Basin footprint; watch for future operational updates or potential financing details.

JKHY.brief: Jack Henry & Associates filed an 8-K reporting that its Board approved adding 5 million shares to its existing stock repurchase authorization, increasing the total authorization to 6.4 million shares (from 1.4 million remaining). The company has repurchased just over 2 million shares in fiscal year 2026. The buyback program, initiated in October 2002 and increased eight times, will be funded with available cash or short-term borrowings. No price targets or timetables are set. The move signals management's confidence in operations and commitment to shareholder returns. Watch for execution pace and impact on EPS.

WASH.brief: Washington Trust Bancorp, Inc. filed an 8-K on May 12, 2026, announcing that its Board of Directors adopted a stock repurchase program (2026 Repurchase Program) authorizing the repurchase of up to 850,000 shares of common stock, representing approximately 4.5% of outstanding shares (19.1 million shares as of April 30, 2026). No price, premium, or expiration date beyond May 16, 2027, was specified; repurchases are at market prices, subject to market conditions and regulatory constraints. The program can be modified or discontinued at any time. This open-market repurchase program returns capital to shareholders with no structural features like a tender or fixed price. Watch for execution pace and potential suspension if economic conditions deteriorate.

ALLO.brief: Allogene Therapeutics filed an 8-K reporting termination of an exclusive license agreement with Overland parties and entry into a Second Amended and Restated Shareholders Agreement. The license, for CAR T therapies in certain Asian territories, was terminated without consideration; Allogene surrendered equity and will retain ~3% of Overland. No termination payments were made. The restructuring alters Allogene's ownership and governance rights. This is not a standard special situation like an acquisition or spin-off; it is a contract termination and equity restructuring. Watch for any subsequent strategic moves by Allogene.

ARMP.brief: Armata Pharmaceuticals filed Form 8-K disclosing entry into a $25 million secured term loan facility with Innoviva Strategic Opportunities LLC, a subsidiary of principal shareholder Innoviva, Inc. The loan carries a 14.0% annual interest rate, matures January 11, 2029, and is secured by substantially all of the company's assets, with subsidiary guarantees. The agreement includes customary covenants and events of default. While a material definitive agreement, this financing does not constitute a classic special situation such as an acquisition, divestiture, restructuring, or going-private transaction. It is more akin to a debt financing arrangement. The press release also announced Q1 2026 financial results. No deal terms such as price per share or premium were applicable. The filing is routine debt financing, not a special situation.

IBEX.brief: IBEX Limited filed an 8-K on May 13, 2026 announcing its board authorized a $20 million share repurchase program starting May 14, 2026, over one year. Repurchases may be made through open market, privately negotiated, or block trades at management's discretion, subject to market conditions and Rule 10b-18/10b5-1 compliance. The program is funded from existing cash, does not obligate any specific amount, and can be suspended or discontinued anytime. No price per share, premium, or advisor is disclosed. Watch for execution pace and potential impact on shares outstanding; no risk-arb angle as this is a routine capital return, not an M&A event.

LVS.brief: Las Vegas Sands Corp. completed an underwritten public offering of $500M 5.300% Senior Notes due 2031 and $500M 5.650% Senior Notes due 2033. Net proceeds, with cash on hand, will redeem the $1.0B 3.500% Senior Notes due August 2026, pay fees, and for general corporate purposes. The unsecured notes are senior obligations with no subsidiary guarantees, issued under a 2019 indenture supplemented by tenth and eleventh supplemental indentures. Interest is semi-annual; redemption prior to par call dates is at present value. Watch for the August 2026 note redemption execution and potential impact on leverage ratios.

NBBK.brief: NB Bancorp, Inc. filed an 8-K on May 21, 2026 to disclose a slide presentation for an investor bank meeting on June 2, 2026. The presentation includes information on operations and financial performance, with forward-looking statements. No specific deal terms, price, premium, or strategic actions are provided. The filing is a routine disclosure of investor materials, not a special situation.

NVTS.brief: Navitas Semiconductor filed an 8-K on October 6, 2026 announcing the closing, effective that date, of its previously announced acquisition of Claros, Inc. under an Agreement and Plan of Merger dated August 24, 2026, executed through wholly owned subsidiaries Compass Merger Sub 1 Inc. and Compass Merger Sub 2 LLC, with Shareholder Representative Services LLC acting for Claros securityholders. No purchase price, consideration mix, premium, financing, advisor or break fee is disclosed in the excerpt. A related press release and CEO letter frame the deal within the company's 'Navitas 2.0' transformation. Watch integration execution, disclosed deal economics in the press release, and any earnout or holdback terms governing the securityholder representative arrangements.

RCAT.brief: Red Cat Holdings filed an 8-K to report its completed acquisition of Quaze Technologies Inc. on May 19, 2026. Red Cat, through a wholly-owned subsidiary, acquired all Quaze shares for approximately 1,923,308 shares of common stock valued at ~$21 million based on a 20-day VWAP, with up to $5 million in additional earnout shares tied to integration, revenue, and gross margin milestones. The closing shares were issued unregistered under the Securities Act. The filing provides no board recommendation or advisor; the deal closed immediately. Watch for earnout achievement and integration of Quaze's Canadian drone technology into Red Cat's defense portfolio.

AEP.brief: American Electric Power Company (AEP) disclosed entry into forward sale agreements covering 23,543,308 shares of its common stock, at an initial forward sale price of $124.968 per share, in conjunction with an underwritten public offering. The forward purchasers are Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, and Morgan Stanley. AEP expects to physically settle on or before May 31, 2028, receiving net proceeds at that time. The transaction functions as an equity forward, allowing AEP to lock in current pricing while deferring share issuance. This is a capital return mechanism for the issuer. The key watchpoint is AEP's discretion on settlement timing; early settlement may indicate near-term capital need.

BRUN.brief: Nasdaq filed Form 25-NSE on 2026-08-25 to delist Boost Run Inc.'s warrants under Rule 12d2-2(a)(1), effective immediately. The delisting follows the company's failure to meet continued listing standards, with no tender offer or merger involved. The filing removes the warrants from Nasdaq, but the common stock may remain listed. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The delisting becomes effective upon filing, and the warrants will trade over-the-counter. Watch for potential OTC trading and any subsequent company actions or restructurings.

CSX.brief: CSX Corporation filed an 8-K on May 14, 2026, reporting two items: Item 5.02 (departure of a named officer) and Item 5.07 (Annual Meeting voting results). CFO Stephen Fortune separated immediately, eligible for severance under a prior plan; Steve Watkins assumes his role. This officer departure appears orderly, not forced/abrupt. The meeting results show routine elections and advisory votes. No special-situation transaction is present—no M&A, tender, spin-off, activist campaign, or similar event. The filing is a routine current report covering ordinary personnel and governance matters. There is no deal, no price per share, no premium, and no regulatory or risk-arb angle to monitor. Beyond the description, no further analysis is warranted.

GIII.brief: G-III Apparel Group filed an 8-K announcing completion of its acquisition of the Marc Jacobs business from LVMH, effective September 1, 2026. The transaction was structured via a newly formed JV, MJ Topco, with WHP Global affiliate acquiring Marc Jacobs Holdings, after which G-III acquired the operating business while IPCo retained intellectual property. G-III funded its approximately $500 million investment through cash and revolving credit borrowings and will operate under an exclusive license from IPCo. A Transition Services Agreement with LVMH includes G-III guarantees. Watch for integration execution and license economics under WHP ownership.

JBTM.brief: JBT Marel Corp filed an 8-K/A to correct the effective date of a previously announced share repurchase program of up to $200 million of its common stock, moving the start from June 1, 2026, to May 18, 2026, through May 31, 2029. The board authorized the program at its discretion, subject to market conditions. The filing also notes a quarterly dividend of $0.10 per share payable June 9, 2026. No premium, advisors, or structural details were mentioned. Watch for execution pace and potential impact on share price, though no risk-arb angle exists as this is a standard capital return authorization.

GLW.brief: Corning Inc. had its 3.875% Notes due 2026 redeemed at maturity on May 15, 2026, as notified by the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) via Form 25-NSE. The entire class of notes was paid at par and retired. NYSE filed the removal from listing and registration, effective at the opening on May 26, 2026, under Rule 12d2-2(a)(2). Trading was suspended on May 15. There is no board recommendation, advisor, or premium. No collateral or ownership split applies. The removal is purely administrative; no risk-arb angle as this is a debt maturity, not an M&A event.

COLB.brief: Columbia Banking System, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing its Board approved a quarterly cash dividend of $0.37 per common share, payable June 15, 2026 to shareholders of record as of May 29, 2026. The dividend is a recurring capital return event, not a special situation. No M&A, activist, restructuring, or other special-situations catalyst is present. The filing includes a press release as Exhibit 99.1. What to watch: no risk-arb angle; monitor future dividend declarations for sustainability or changes.

DK.brief: Delek US Holdings completed a private offering of $460 million 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2031 via an indenture with U.S. Bank Trust as trustee, per this 8-K. The notes are senior unsecured, fully guaranteed by subsidiary guarantors of the term loan and ABL facilities, mature November 1, 2031, bear no regular interest, and are convertible only on specified conditions (e.g., stock at 150% of conversion price). No price, premium, or use of proceeds is disclosed; this is a financing, not a control event.

MNST.brief: Monster Beverage Corporation filed an 8-K reporting its annual meeting results and a new $500M share repurchase authorization. The Board authorized an additional $500M buyback on May 14, 2026, supplementing the ~$400M remaining from the prior program. Repurchases may occur in open-market or negotiated transactions. No price, premium, or expiration date were specified. There is no independent advisor or premium disclosed, signaling ordinary-course capital allocation. The filing also includes uncontested director elections and routine advisory votes. Watch for the pace of repurchases as a signal of management's view on intrinsic value; no risk-arb angle as this is a straight buyback, not an issuer tender.

AKAM.brief: Akamai Technologies filed an 8-K reporting the completion of a $3.5 billion convertible note offering: $1.75 billion in 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2030 and $1.75 billion in 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2032, sold in a private placement to QIBs under Rule 144A. Net proceeds partially funded a $236.6 million convertible note hedge (offset by warrant proceeds) and a $350 million share repurchase of 2,476,298 shares. Remaining proceeds will fund accelerated CIS capital expenditures. Notes are senior unsecured obligations. The simultaneous debt issuance and stock buyback represent a capital return to shareholders via leverage. Watch for dilution impact from potential conversion and any rating agency actions.

EZPW.brief: EZCORP filed an 8-K reporting it acquired the remaining 12.3% of Founders One, LLC membership interests on May 14, 2026, achieving 100% ownership, and on May 15, 2026, through Founders, bought 1,360.65 shares of Simple Management Group (SMG) from minority holders, raising its SMG stake to 93%. No price per share, premium, or total deal value was disclosed. The board did not make a recommendation and no advisors were named. The transaction had no regulatory clock; it closed immediately. What to watch: EZCORP may seek full ownership of SMG in the near future.

FLG.brief: Flagstar Bank filed an 8-K announcing a $250 million common stock repurchase program authorized by its Board, valid for 12 months via open-market or private transactions, possibly under Rule 10b5-1 plans. Terms: up to $250M over the next year, no set price or number of shares specified. The program may be modified or suspended at any time. Mechanics: open-market or negotiated purchases, subject to capital position, regulatory constraints, and market conditions. This is a capital return event—a buyback authorization—with no stated premium, advisor, or regulatory clock. Watch for actual repurchase cadence and whether it signals management's view of undervaluation.

IBRX.brief: ImmunityBio filed an 8-K to disclose an exclusive development and supply agreement with Japan BCG Laboratory (JBL) for the Tokyo-172 BCG strain. JBL manufactures and exclusively supplies the product; ImmunityBio handles all U.S. development, trials, and regulatory approvals. The agreement is ten years from FDA approval, with ImmunityBio having a right of first negotiation for ex-U.S. territories. No upfront payment; supply vials for regulatory submission are free. Post-FDA approval, ImmunityBio must purchase at least two batches per year. The arrangement is a standard licensing/supply deal with no equity, tender, or special-situation restructuring involved. Watch for FDA approval timeline and commercial launch execution.

LIF.brief: Life360 filed an 8-K reporting that its Board authorized a $225 million share repurchase program. The program allows open-market, privately negotiated, and block-trade buybacks, possibly under Rule 10b5-1 plans. No specific price, premium, or close date is given; the program is multi-year and aims to offset stock-based compensation dilution. The company cites a strong balance sheet and 12 consecutive quarters of positive operating cash flow. Repurchases may be modified or suspended at any time. Watch for ongoing buyback execution and potential impact on share count; no risk-arb angle as this is not a M&A event.

SAM.brief: The Boston Beer Company filed an 8-K announcing a 10b5-1 plan to repurchase up to $25 million of its Class A Common Stock during a period from June 29, 2026 to September 25, 2026. The repurchase is an issuer share buyback undertaken under a pre-arranged trading plan to allow repurchases during blackout periods. The filing includes no details on board recommendation or advisors. The mechanics are a standard 10b5-1 plan, reducing shares outstanding and returning capital to shareholders. Watch for the actual pace of repurchases and any impact on EPS.

BFC.brief: Bank First Corp filed Amendment No. 1 to its Form S-4 registration statement on July 30, 2026, in connection with its proposed acquisition of PSB Holdings, Inc. The all-stock merger agreement, dated May 19, 2026, was unanimously approved by both boards. PSB will merge with and into Bank First, followed by the merger of Peoples State Bank into Bank First's bank subsidiary. The proxy statement/prospectus is preliminary and subject to completion. The transaction requires shareholder approvals and regulatory clearances. No deal terms or premium were disclosed in this excerpt. Watch for final pricing, exchange ratio, and expected closing timeline.

AGM.brief: Farmer Mac filed an 8-K reporting the completion of an exempt public offering of 4,000,000 shares of 6.875% Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock, Series I. The sale was made under an underwriting agreement dated May 12, 2026, with Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC as representative of the underwriters. Terms include a 6.875% dividend rate, non-cumulative, with no stated price per share or premium disclosed. No board recommendation or advisor referenced beyond the underwriter. This is a routine capital-raising transaction, not a special-situation event. Watch for subsequent dividend payments and potential future issuance; no risk-arb angle applies.

KMT.brief: Kennametal filed an 8-K under Items 5.02, 8.01, and 9.01 announcing the appointment of Amanda Cole as Vice President and Chief Human Resources Officer effective July 21, 2026, succeeding Judith Bacchus who will retire as Chief Administrative Officer on October 1, 2026. Ms. Cole joins from Wesco International and will enter into standard indemnification and officer employment agreements. No material terms such as price, premium, or deal value were disclosed. The filing is a routine officer appointment with no structural mechanics or regulatory clock, and does not constitute a special situation event.

VAL.brief: Valaris Ltd filed an 8-K updating its pending acquisition by Transocean Ltd under a Business Combination Agreement dated February 9, 2026. Transocean will acquire all outstanding Valaris common shares for 15.235 Transocean shares per Valaris share, a stock-for-stock offshore drilling merger. On October 13, 2026, Brazil's CADE cleared the deal without restrictions; publication in Brazil's Official Journal on October 15-16, 2026 starts a 15-day waiting period before the decision becomes final. All regulatory approval conditions would then be satisfied, with closing anticipated in Q4 2026. Watch publication timing, the 15-day clock, and remaining closing conditions.

PNC.brief: PNC Financial Services Group filed an 8-K announcing the full redemption on Nov. 1, 2026 (shifted to Nov. 2, 2026, a non-business day) of all 525,000 outstanding Depositary Shares (CUSIP 693475 AQ8) representing $525 million of its Fixed-to-Floating Rate Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock, Series S, each a 1/100th interest. Redemption price is $1,000 per Depositary Share, excluding declared but unpaid dividends, which are paid separately to holders of record. Shares held via DTC and redeemed through Computershare Trust Company, N.A. as Depositary. Watch preferred redemption mechanics and dividend record-date timing.

CTRE.brief: CareTrust REIT's UK subsidiary completed the acquisition of the entire issued share capital of LNT care home property companies holding 23 completed care homes on October 1, 2026, with a 24th pending regulatory approval, under a September 30, 2026 Share Purchase Deed. Purchase price is £24 million per property, approximately £576 million ($764 million) aggregate for the 24 Completed Properties, plus put/call options for up to 21 In-Development Properties at roughly £504 million ($669 million) through December 31, 2027. Properties are triple-net leased to Crystal Care Holdco with LNT guarantees. Watch opco acquisition options, regulatory approvals, and lease-up execution risk.

PRSU.brief: Pursuit Attractions & Hospitality, Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing an amendment to its Equity Purchase Agreement with Flyover Attractions B.V. and Brogent Technologies, Inc. to extend the outside closing date from May 21, 2026, to July 31, 2026, for the sale of its Flyover flying theater attractions business. No price, premium, or advisor was mentioned. The amendment only modifies the deadline; other terms remain unchanged. Closing is subject to customary conditions. The extension pushes back a potential termination date, signaling ongoing regulatory or logistical hurdles. Watch for whether the deal closes by the new deadline or is terminated.

WSBC.brief: WesBanco, Inc. filed an 8-K on May 20, 2026, announcing a new stock repurchase program approved by its Board of Directors authorizing the repurchase of up to an additional 4.0 million shares of common stock, combining with 0.9 million remaining from a prior authorization for a total of 4.9 million shares, representing approximately 5.1% of shares outstanding as of March 31, 2026. The program has no expiration date and may be effected through open market purchases, privately-negotiated transactions, block trades, or Rule 10b5-1 plans, funded from existing cash and liquidity sources. The filing is a standard capital return event. Watch for execution pace against market conditions.

GTLS.brief: Chart Industries filed Form 15 to terminate its registration under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act, effective July 29, 2026. The filing certifies that the company has fewer than 300 holders of record of its common stock, thereby suspending its duty to file periodic reports with the SEC. This action was taken by the registrant itself, with John Harrell signing as authorized signatory. There are no deal terms, premium, advisor, or transaction structure involved. The move typically follows a going-private transaction or a significant reduction in shareholder base. What to watch: potential liquidity reduction and reporting relief for the company.

QBTS.brief: D-Wave Quantum filed an 8-K/A amending its September 8, 2026 report on a Department of Commerce Other Transaction Agreement worth up to $100 million. On September 8, 2026, D-Wave executed a Securities Issuance Agreement and issued 7,095,721 unregistered common shares to the Department at $14.093 per share, raising roughly $100 million in non-cash consideration tied to the award. Shares were sold under Section 4(a)(2) exemption. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or close date stated. Watch for dilution, registration rights, and government ownership overhang.

VMRK.brief: Equity Residential filed an 8-K disclosing pending all-stock merger-of-equals with AvalonBay Communities, structured as a merger with Canopy Merger Sub, a wholly owned subsidiary of Equity Residential. The combined company will operate as Vivmark Residential. The Form S-4 registration statement was declared effective July 13, 2026, and joint proxy statements were mailed. Shareholder litigation and demand letters allege disclosure deficiencies; both companies deny merit. Watch for court rulings on disclosure claims and shareholder votes; regulatory and shareholder approvals pending, with stock-for-stock exchange ratio and closing date not disclosed.

LXU.brief: The NYSE filed Form 25-NSE to delist LSB Industries' Preferred Stock Purchase Rights, effective September 8, 2026, after the entire class was redeemed or expired on August 24, 2026. All rights were extinguished, and trading was suspended that same day. This is a routine delisting following the expiration of shareholder rights, typically tied to a prior corporate action such as a merger or rights termination. No financial terms or premiums were disclosed. Watch for any related merger completion or rights-triggering event.

LILAK.brief: Liberty Latin America Ltd. filed an 8-K announcing the declaration of a special dividend of Series A Preference Shares. For every ten common shares, holders receive one share of newly issued 9.0% Fixed Rate Cumulative Perpetual Redeemable Series A Preference Shares, par value $0.01. The dividend is payable quarterly starting September 15, 2026, at 9.0% per annum of the liquidation price. Unpaid dividends accumulate and increase the liquidation price after a 30-day cure period. The board authorized the dividend via an authorized committee. This capital return distributes preferred equity, not cash, enhancing shareholder yield. Watch for potential redemption terms and liquidity impact on common shares; risk-arb angle is limited as it's a dividend, not an M&A event.

STX.brief: Seagate Technology Holdings plc filed an 8-K after its subsidiary Seagate HDD Cayman completed the call of all outstanding 3.50% Exchangeable Senior Notes due 2028. On the September 8, 2026 redemption date, roughly $150.7 million was redeemed at par plus accrued interest; notes submitted by the September 3 deadline were exchanged, with principal paid in cash and excess value settled via 1,647,862 newly issued ordinary shares ($150.51 million notional) plus cash in lieu of fractions. Approximately $150.97 million cash was paid. The debt reduction eliminates exchangeable overhang; potential future share resale is the watch item.

UNM.brief: Unum Group filed an 8-K announcing its board authorized a new $1 billion share repurchase program effective September 1, 2026, replacing the current program that terminates August 31, 2026. Repurchases may occur in open market or privately negotiated transactions, including accelerated share repurchase plans, at management's discretion based on market conditions. No specific price, premium, or completion date was provided. The filing is a routine capital return authorization, not a tender offer or other special-situation event. Watch for execution pace and any significant buyback volume that could support share price.

NFBK.brief: Northfield Bancorp, Inc. filed Form 15-12G on August 3, 2026, to terminate registration of its common stock under Section 12(g) and suspend reporting obligations under Sections 13 and 15(d) of the Exchange Act. The filing, executed by Dennis E. Gibney as Chief Banking Officer of successor Columbia Financial, Inc., cites Rule 12g-4(a)(1) and indicates no remaining holders of record. This follows the consummation of a merger where Columbia Financial acquired Northfield. The deregistration eliminates SEC reporting and related costs, but also removes public disclosure. Risk-arb note: focus shifts to post-merger integration and any remaining shareholder litigation or appraisal claims; no premium relevant.

AMT.brief: American Tower filed an 8-K on Sept. 14, 2026, reporting completion of a registered public offering of $1.6B senior unsecured notes across three tranches: 5.300% due 2031, 5.560% due 2033, and 5.750% due 2036, netting approximately $1,579.9M. The REIT intends to repay $600M of 1.450% notes due 2026 and outstanding revolver debt. No board recommendation or advisor was cited, and the filing is an ordinary debt-structuring action rather than a canonical special situation; watch for leverage metrics and refinancing cadence as rate-risk signals.

AHRT.brief: AH Realty Trust, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the first closing of its Multifamily Disposition, selling 9 of 11 multifamily properties for ~$485M in aggregate proceeds under a $562M purchase agreement with an unrelated third party. The remaining two properties are expected to close by end-2026 and mid-2027. No board recommendation or advisor is named in this filing. The transaction reduces the company's multifamily exposure and generates significant cash. Watch for completion of the remaining sales and use of proceeds.

AVXL.brief: PVG Asset Management Corp., with affiliates holding 337,663 Anavex Life Sciences shares, filed a definitive proxy statement on August 27, 2026, to elect six nominees—Patrick S. Adams, Jason Kolbert, Ralf von Ziegesar, Rene Mora, John Boris, and Curtis Hogue—to Anavex's six-member board at the virtual annual meeting on September 24, 2026. PVG cites poor governance and lack of transparency, opposing the board's four incumbent directors and two new nominees. Both sides will use universal proxy cards. The contest targets board control, not a transaction. Watch for voting outcomes, potential settlement, and board composition changes.

CVCO.brief: Cavco Industries filed an 8-K (Item 8.01) announcing a $150 million stock repurchase program approved by its board on May 18, 2026. Purchases may be made in open market or privately negotiated transactions; no specific price, share count, or expiry date is set. The program is discretionary and can be suspended at any time; it will be funded by existing cash. The filing also contained fiscal Q4 and FY2026 earnings results. The buyback announcement is a non-binding capital return authorization. Watch for actual execution pace as a signal of management's view on undervaluation. There is no risk-arb angle as this is not an M&A event.

LVWR.brief: LiveWire Group disclosed on July 23, 2026 that it received an NYSE notice for non-compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price rule (Section 802.01C) due to a 30-day average closing price below $1.00. The company has a six-month cure period to regain compliance by achieving a $1.00 closing price and 30-day average on the last trading day of any calendar month. No immediate delisting impact; business operations and SEC reporting unaffected. The board has not announced a specific cure plan. Company intends to notify NYSE of its intent to cure. Watch for potential reverse stock split or other shareholder-approved measures if compliance not regained.

EDIT.brief: Editas Medicine filed an 8-K to announce an underwritten public offering of 55,555,556 shares of common stock and accompanying warrants to purchase an equal number of shares. The combined public offering price is $2.25 per unit, with net proceeds estimated at ~$117 million. Cantor Fitzgerald and Wells Fargo Securities are lead underwriters. The company expects closing on May 27, 2026. The warrants have an exercise price of $3.50, are immediately exercisable, and expire 30 days after announcement of Phase 1 data. This dilutive financing strengthens the balance sheet and funds operations, so the key watchpoint is potential near-term dilution and the stock's reaction to the offering.

XZO.brief: Exzeo Group, Inc. filed an 8-K on August 14, 2026, announcing that its Board authorized a share repurchase program of up to $25 million of its common stock, subject to market conditions. The program, effective for one year, permits repurchases via open-market, block, privately negotiated, or Rule 10b5-1 trading plan transactions, consistent with Rule 10b-18. No specific share count or price targets were disclosed; management holds discretion on timing and amounts. The program may be suspended or cancelled without notice. Watch for actual repurchase execution levels in periodic filings as a proxy for management's valuation view.

HLLY.brief: The NYSE filed a Form 25-NSE to delist and deregister Holley Inc.'s redeemable warrants (each whole warrant exercisable for one share of common stock at $11.50) as of July 27, 2026, after the instruments converted to represent only the right to receive an immediate cash payment upon exercise. The delisting follows a suspension of trading on July 15, 2026, under Rule 12d2-2(a)(3). No board recommendation or advisor is named. The action is mechanical, stemming from the warrants' conversion event. The risk-arb angle is moot; the delisting removes these warrants from public trading, with holders entitled to cash only.

KNSA.brief: Kiniksa Pharmaceuticals filed an 8-K regarding a deed of waiver with Baker Bros. Advisors LP, on behalf of certain shareholders. The deed waives the shareholders' conversion rights for Class A1/B1 shares into Class A/B shares if such conversion would result in beneficial ownership exceeding 49.9% of the company's outstanding voting rights. The waiver requires a 75% shareholder vote to amend, terminate, or waive. This is a governance/ownership restriction, not a capital markets event or restructuring. What to watch: any future attempts to modify the ownership cap or change in control dynamics.

NL.brief: NL Industries, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of its reincorporation merger from New Jersey to Delaware, effective May 26, 2026. The merger was executed via an Agreement and Plan of Merger dated May 19, 2026, under which Predecessor Corporation merged into NLI Holdings, Inc., the surviving entity. Each share of Predecessor common stock automatically converted into one share of successor common stock with identical par value. The reincorporation was approved by shareholders on May 14, 2026. This filing also establishes NLI Holdings as the successor issuer under Rule 12g-3. No terms are applicable as this is a domicile change, not an acquisition or restructuring. Watch for normal NYSE listing continuation under the new name.

PGNY.brief: Progyny, Inc. disclosed in an 8-K that its Board approved a share repurchase program of up to $200 million of common stock. The program will be funded from available cash; repurchases may occur in the open market (including Rule 10b5-1 plans) at management's discretion based on stock price and market conditions, and may be suspended or discontinued at any time. No specific price, premium, or timeline was provided. The program does not commit the company to any particular number of shares. Watch for periodic disclosures of repurchase activity under this authorization.

APLE.brief: Apple Hospitality REIT, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting annual meeting voting results and extending its share repurchase program to July 2027 with a $242.5 million authorization. Repurchases may be made in open market, through 10b5-1 plans, or in private transactions, depending on market conditions. No advisor or board recommendation details are provided beyond the board's approval. The filing is not a routine current report, as the program extension is a capital return event. Focus on actual repurchase execution against the authorization, noting that conditions, including market conditions and other factors, may affect timing and volume.

APOG.brief: Apogee Enterprises filed an 8-K confirming completion of its acquisition of SIA Alzette, a Latvian limited liability company whose subsidiaries include GroGlass, a glass coatings producer. Under the September 2, 2026 Share Purchase Agreement, Apogee's wholly-owned subsidiary Tiger MergeCo SIA acquired 100% of SIA Alzette's equity for roughly €62.5 million cash-free, debt-free, subject to customary adjustments, plus up to €10 million of contingent earnout consideration payable over three years tied to specified financial performance targets. Apogee funded the deal with cash and revolver borrowings. The transaction was announced September 3, 2026; no board recommendation or advisor was disclosed.

AXTA.brief: Axalta filed an 8-K supplemental proxy disclosures for its pending acquisition by AkzoNobel. The merger agreement, originally signed Nov 18, 2025, was amended multiple times, with a special meeting scheduled for Aug 5, 2026. Axalta voluntarily supplements the definitive proxy statement. Structural details include two-step merger with AkzoNobel subs, with Axalta surviving first merger then merging into second sub. No price terms disclosed in this excerpt. Watch for shareholder vote outcome and regulatory approvals to complete the transaction.

DUOT.brief: Duos Technologies Group filed an 8-K disclosing the September 30, 2026 sale of 100% of Duos Edge AI GPUaaS, LLC to Axe Compute, Inc. under an Equity Purchase Agreement. The SPV held 288 Supermicro B300 servers (2,304 GPUs) plus networking gear. Consideration: Axe repaid roughly $87.8 million of SPV debt and owes a deferred purchase price of $715,000 per month for 60 months, accelerated to the earlier of 12 months post-closing or new cluster-secured financing. The deal removes about $98.1 million of prospective equipment financing; no board recommendation or advisor is named. Watch deferred-payment credit risk and acceleration triggers.

LOCO.brief: El Pollo Loco Holdings filed an 8-K announcing a $40M share repurchase program approved by its Board of Directors. Shares may be bought on open market, block trades, or privately, with management discretion on timing and amount. No specific price, premium, or date set; no advisors named. Mechanics allow Rule 10b5-1 plans, but program is non-binding and may be suspended. This is a discretionary buyback, not a tender offer. Watch for actual repurchase execution and impact on free cash flow.

H.brief: Hyatt Hotels Corp filed an 8-K announcing its Board authorized an additional $1.0 billion share repurchase program for its Class A and Class B common stock. Repurchases may occur via open market, private transactions, Rule 10b5-1 plans, or accelerated share repurchase transactions at the company's discretion, subject to market conditions and applicable law. The authorization does not obligate Hyatt to repurchase any specific amount and may be suspended or discontinued at any time. Investors should watch the pace of buyback execution and potential impact on earnings per share.

NTAP.brief: NetApp filed an 8-K reporting fiscal Q4 2026 results and announcing a $1.0B share repurchase authorization. The new buyback has no expiration date; repurchases may be executed via open-market (Rule 10b-18), 10b5-1 plans, privately-negotiated transactions, or accelerated share repurchases. No specific price per share, premium, or close date is stated. The board authorized the repurchase; no financial advisor is named. The program offers flexibility but no commitment. Watch for the pace of execution under the renewed buyback authorization; the lack of set terms leaves the rate of capital return uncertain.

PD.brief: PagerDuty, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing a new $100 million share repurchase program authorized by its Board, replacing earlier programs. The program allows repurchases via open market, private transactions, or Rule 10b5-1 plans, with no obligation to buy a specified number; it will be funded from existing cash and run through May 26, 2028, unless extended or terminated. PagerDuty is the issuer. Watch for execution pace and any market reaction; risk-arb angle is minimal as this is a discretionary buyback, not a fixed-price tender.

PEB.brief: Pebblebrook Hotel Trust filed an 8-K reporting Q2 2026 results and announcing a new $50.0 million preferred share repurchase program authorized July 24, 2026, to start after the current $100.0 million program (with $45.6 million available) is completed. The new program covers Series E, F, G, and H preferred shares, with aggregate liquidation value eligible at $639.5 million. No price, timing, or expiration is set; repurchases will be at the company's discretion. This is a capital return via preferred buybacks. Watch for execution pace and impact on preferred yields.

RR.brief: Richtech Robotics filed an 8-K on August 21, 2026, disclosing its board authorized a stock repurchase program of up to $12 million of Class B common stock, with a one-year term ending August 21, 2027. The program will be executed via a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan, subject to market conditions, and may be modified or terminated at any time. The company also approved a healthcare cash stipend of $750 per bi-weekly paycheck for its CEO, CFO, and COO, an aggregate of about $19,500 annually. No shares were specified. Watch for execution pace and potential price support.

TSCO.brief: Tractor Supply Company (TSCO) acquired VIP Petcare (operating as VIP Petcare and PetVet) from PetIQ, a Bansk Group company, as announced in an 8-K filed May 28, 2026. VIP Petcare is the largest U.S. mobile veterinary care provider, operating in ~2,700 retail locations, including 1,700 Tractor Supply stores, serving over 1 million pets annually. Terms—price, premium, and consideration—were not disclosed. The acquisition strengthens Tractor Supply's pet health platform by integrating veterinary services, pharmacy, and retail. No board recommendation or advisors named. The deal is expected to close pending regulatory approvals; watch for integration updates and any antitrust review.

EAF.brief: GrafTech entered into an equity distribution agreement (May 29, 2026) to sell up to $50M of common stock via an at-the-market (ATM) offering through Evercore as agent. Stock price was $10.00/share on May 28. The company pays a 3.0% commission; settlement next trading day via DTC. This is a shelf takedown under Rule 415 — proceeds typically used for general corporate purposes or capital returns. No board recommendation or advisor mentioned. The ATM structure allows gradual issuance, reducing market overhang. Watch dilution pace and use of proceeds for buybacks or debt reduction.

IDT.brief: IDT Corporation filed a Form 8-K to announce a quarterly cash dividend of $0.07 per share declared by its Board of Directors. The dividend is payable on June 18, 2026, to stockholders of record as of June 9, 2026. The filing is a routine dividend announcement with no special-situation event such as a merger, tender offer, restructuring, or management change. The registrant is acting solely as the issuer of the dividend, and there are no deal terms, advisors, or structural mechanics applicable. This is a standard capital allocation action and does not qualify as a special situation.

NNE.brief: Nano Nuclear Energy Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing that on September 28, 2026, it and subsidiary HALEU Energy Fuel Inc. agreed to acquire all U.S. nuclear fuel processing assets of Radnostix, Inc. and International Isotopes Fluorine Products, Inc., including NRC Material License SUB-1011, a New Mexico air permit, patents and Sequoyah Fuels documentation tied to a planned DUF6 deconversion plant in Lea County. Consideration is not disclosed beyond a $0.5 million Citibank escrow deposit. Closing is expected in roughly 90-120 days, subject to NRC license-transfer consent and New Mexico approvals; watch regulatory timing risk.

ORRF.brief: Orrstown Financial Services Inc. filed an 8-K disclosing two events: (a) a full redemption of its $31M 4.5% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Subordinated Notes due 2030 on June 30, 2026, at 100% of principal plus accrued interest. The notes were assumed from its July 2024 merger with Codorus Valley Bancorp. (b) A vendor cybersecurity incident exposing customer information, but the company's systems were not breached and no material impact is expected. The redemption is a routine debt management action; the cybersecurity disclosure is an operational update. Neither constitutes a classic special-situation event, and no strategic shift is announced.

BTU.brief: Peabody Energy Corp filed an 8-K announcing the pricing of $225 million aggregate principal amount of 0.50% convertible senior notes due 2031, offered privately to qualified institutional buyers under Rule 144A. The notes are senior unsecured obligations, settle June 2, 2026, with an underwriter option for an additional $25 million. Interest is payable semi-annually; conversion rights begin December 1, 2030, with settlement in cash, stock, or a combination. This is a routine debt capital markets transaction, not a special situation. No special-situation elements are present.

CBU.brief: Community Financial System, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing the completion of its acquisition of ClearPoint Federal Bank Trust, a federally chartered savings association and leader in trust administration for the death care industry. The deal, originally announced January 14, 2026, was effected via merger with Community Bank, N.A., a wholly-owned subsidiary. ClearPoint has over $1.5 billion in assets under management and a historical three-year revenue CAGR of 9.7%. No financial terms, price per share, premium, or advisors were disclosed. The acquired business will operate as ClearPoint Trust, a division of Community Bank. Watch for integration updates and revenue contribution from Nottingham Financial Group.

EHC.brief: Encompass Health issued $500M of 5.875% Senior Notes due 2034 via a private Rule 144A/Reg S offering, netting ~$491.2M after discounts and expenses. Proceeds will redeem $400M of its 4.500% notes due 2028 at par and repay $100M under its revolver, representing a liability management / capital-return event through refinancing to lower near-term debt. The indenture with Computershare includes standard make-whole redemption provisions. No change in equity structure; watch ability to refinance remaining $400M of 2028 notes if callable. This is a debt capital return, not an equity distribution.

FCPT.brief: Four Corners Property Trust (FCPT) filed an 8-K disclosing the closing of its acquisition of 102 veterinary properties from Shore Capital Real Estate Partners Holdco, LLC for $268.0 million, based on ~$17.37 million initial annual cash rent. The purchase was via a subsidiary under a Purchase and Sale Agreement dated May 29, 2026. All properties are operated by Mission Pet Health. The all-cash deal closed July 16, 2026, with a rent credit received at closing. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The acquisition adds net-leased retail/restaurant properties to FCPT's portfolio. Watch for integration execution and cap rate accretion relative to FCPT's stated 6.6% YTD weighted average cap rate.

KRMN.brief: Karman Holdings Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the completion of its acquisition of Walker Precision Engineering for approximately $95 million in cash, subject to customary adjustments, via a wholly owned subsidiary. To fund the deal, Karman entered a Sixth Amendment to its Credit Agreement, increasing term loans by $100 million to a total original principal of $863.961 million, and will use proceeds for the purchase and related fees. The filing also discloses the credit facility modification and provides an update on the transaction. No advisors or premium details are mentioned. Watch for integration progress and any post-closing adjustments.

ORLY.brief: On June 1, 2026, O'Reilly Automotive's board approved a $2.0 billion increase to its share repurchase authorization, raising the aggregate to $31.75 billion, effective for three years. Repurchases will be made in open market transactions at prevailing prices based on market conditions and corporate factors, with no fixed timetable or obligation to buy any shares. The program may be modified, suspended, or terminated at any time. No advisor, premium, or price terms are disclosed. The filing is an 8-K Item 8.01 (Other Events) announcing expanded buyback capacity. Watch for actual repurchase cadence; the authorization signals management's view on capital allocation and undervaluation but carries no commitment.

STEP.brief: StepStone Group Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the third exchange completed May 29, 2026, acquiring ~5% equity interests in each of three Asset Class Entities (SRE, SRA, SPD) from third-party sellers. The aggregate consideration was approximately $10M cash (pre-adjustment ~$11M), 972,685 shares of Class A common stock, and 2,438,273 Class D units. Post-exchange, StepStone holdings rose to 65% in each entity. Consideration based on exchange ratios tied to estimated adjusted net income and an adjusted trading multiple. Shares and units issued unregistered under Section 4(a)(2). Watch for continued step acquisitions and potential full consolidation or future registration events.

UFPI.brief: UFP Industries Inc. filed an 8-K on June 1, 2026, announcing that its Board authorized a share repurchase program of up to $300 million of its outstanding common stock, expiring April 30, 2027. The repurchases may be executed via open market, private negotiations, or Rule 10b5-1 plans. Timing and amount depend on market conditions and share price. The company is not obligated to repurchase shares. The prior authorization was replaced. Watch for future buyback execution pace; no premium or advisor was noted.

VVX.brief: V2X, Inc. disclosed through subsidiaries a refinancing of existing term loans via Amendment No. 6 to the First Lien Credit Agreement. The amendment creates New Term Loans of $868.5 million maturing December 6, 2030, replacing all outstanding prior term loans. Interest is SOFR + 2.00% or base rate + 1.00%, with a potential 0.25% step-down based on ratings. Voluntary prepayments are allowed without penalty except for certain repricing events. This is a debt restructuring/refinancing, not a special-situation transaction like a sale or acquisition. Terms are routine for credit agreements; no premium, equity stake, or board recommendation is involved.

TTI.brief: The filing is a 424B5 preliminary prospectus supplement by TETRA Technologies, Inc. for a proposed public offering of $100,000,000 of its common stock, with an underwriter over-allotment option of up to $15,000,000. The price per share is to be determined based on the market, with the last-reported price of $10.36 on June 1, 2026. The offering is underwritten by J.P. Morgan as lead book-runner and Jefferies. Proceeds will go to the company. This is a routine capital-raising equity follow-on offering, not a special situation.

AVA.brief: Avista Corp filed an 8-K disclosing a non-binding MOU with a developer for a large load electric service interconnection. The customer seeks 125 MW starting in 2029, expanding to 500 MW by 2032. Next steps include an Engineering and Procurement Contract, regulatory approval from the Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission, and definitive agreements. No financial terms, board recommendation, or advisors are named. This is a preliminary infrastructure development agreement, not a special situation, with no M&A or corporate action. Watch for regulatory filings and definitive agreements.

WLY.brief: John Wiley & Sons, Inc. disclosed via Form 8-K that its indirect wholly-owned subsidiary, John Wiley & Sons Ltd., entered into an Equity Purchase Agreement on June 1, 2026, to acquire all outstanding equity of CIG Emerald Midco LLC (doing business as Emerald Publishing) from CIG Emerald Midco LLC and Emerald Holding. The purchase price is GBP 337.5 million (~$452 million) in cash, funded from cash on hand. The acquisition of over 480 peer-reviewed journals and 8,000 books expands Wiley's research publishing portfolio. The filing includes customary representations, warranties, and indemnification provisions. No advisor or board recommendation is stated. Watch for closing conditions and regulatory approvals.

URGN.brief: UroGen Pharma filed an 8-K announcing it entered into a settlement and license agreement with Teva resolving patent litigation over Jelmyto (mitomycin). Teva will receive a non-exclusive license to sell a generic version starting September 15, 2030, conditional on FDA approval. All ongoing litigation in the District of Delaware will be terminated. The agreement is subject to FTC/DOJ review. This is a routine patent settlement/licensing event, not a special situation. No deal terms or financial details are disclosed.

SPCE.brief: Virgin Galactic Holdings, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting a notice of redemption for up to $30.5M of its 9.80% First Lien Notes due 2028. The redemption, set for June 10, 2026, will be settled by issuing common stock at par plus accrued interest. The exact shares depend on a five-day VWAP; a floor price limits redemption if VWAP falls below it. This follows a prior $10M redemption, retiring all mandatory principal payments through 2027. The move is part of broader liquidity management ahead of commercial operations in Q4 2026. Watch share count dilution and stock price floor mechanics.

ATNI.brief: ATN International, Inc. filed an 8-K on August 5, 2026, reporting Q2 2026 results and announcing a $15 million increase to its existing share repurchase program, raising total authorization to $30 million, with $15 million previously available. The program permits open market purchases, 10b5-1 plans, privately negotiated transactions, accelerated repurchases, block trades, or tender offers. No repurchase obligation or expiration date exists, and the Board may amend or terminate it anytime. The filing is routine earnings disclosure combined with a capital return authorization increase, reflecting ongoing shareholder return initiatives. Watch for future repurchase activity and potential tender offer or ASR execution.

RGNX.brief: REGENXBIO filed an 8-K reporting a September 23, 2026 Settlement Agreement with The Trustees of the University of Pennsylvania and Sarepta Therapeutics, Inc./Sarepta Therapeutics Three, LLC, joined by Catalent, resolving patent infringement litigation over U.S. Patent Nos. 10,526,617 and 11,680,274 tied to Sarepta's SRP-9001 (ELEVIDYS). Sarepta pays $39.0 million within 10 days; all suits terminate with prejudice. REGENXBIO grants a covenant not to sue for AAVrh74-capsid gene therapies and existing ELEVIDYS, with limited scope. Agreement to be filed with Q3 2026 Form 10-Q. Watch cash recognition and residual patent scope.

BRT.brief: BRT Apartments Corp. filed an 8-K on September 17, 2026, reporting that its board authorized replenishment of the stock repurchase program, increasing authorized repurchases to $10 million. No price per share, premium, expiration date, or advisor was named. Separately, BRT amended its VNB New York credit facility, cutting the rate to three-month term SOFR plus 210 bps (from 250 bps), lowering the minimum rate to 5% (from 6%) and the adjustable cap rate to 6.25%, with $40 million available. Watch repurchase pace versus trading liquidity and no stated 10b5-1 plan.

JBIO.brief: Jade Biosciences, Inc. filed an 8-K on June 3, 2026 to disclose entry into an underwriting agreement for an underwritten public offering of 10,000,000 shares of common stock at $15.00 per share, with a $14.10 per share purchase price for underwriters. The filing is a routine capital raise via an existing shelf registration statement (Form S-3), not a special situation. The offering is expected to close June 5, 2026 and proceeds of ~$140.3 million will fund general corporate purposes. No activist campaign, acquisition, divestiture, restructuring, or other control event is involved.
