Concurrently, the company repurchased approximately $225 million of its ordinary shares at $249.29 per share from note purchasers, funded with cash on hand and under its July 2024 repurchase program. Net proceeds were approximately $1.226 billion for general corporate purposes. The repurchase supports share buyback while raising exchangeable debt; watch for dilution offset and note conversion dynamics.

PAL.brief: Proficient Auto Logistics filed an 8-K reporting the completion of a $75.0 million private offering of 5.500% convertible senior notes due 2033, issued under subscription agreements dated August 10, 2026, and an indenture with U.S. Bank Trust Company as trustee. The notes are senior, unsecured obligations maturing August 15, 2033, with semi-annual interest and conversion conditions tied to stock price thresholds. The offering represents a capital raise via convertible debt, which may be used for acquisitions or other purposes, though the filing does not specify use of proceeds. Watch for conversion triggers and potential dilution, though no repurchase or dividend is indicated.

HASI.brief: HA Sustainable Infrastructure Capital, Inc. filed Form S-4 on August 10, 2026, registering securities in connection with a proposed holding company reorganization. The filing involves HA Sustainable Infrastructure Capital, Inc. and its subsidiaries, including Hannon Armstrong Sustainable Infrastructure, L.P., Hannon Armstrong Capital, LLC, and various HAC/HAT Holdings LLCs. Terms such as stake %, price per share, premium, and dates were not disclosed in the excerpt. The board recommendation and advisors were not specified. Structural notes indicate a multi-entity reorganization with guarantor registrants, suggesting a holding company formation under General Instruction G. Regulatory clock and mechanics remain pending. Watch for the exchange ratio, shareholder vote, and effective date as the risk-arb angle centers on the reorganization's closing certainty.

RXST.brief: In Amendment No. 2 to its Schedule TO, RxSight, Inc. reported final results of its exchange offer for eligible employee stock options. The offer expired September 4, 2026; 205 employees tendered options covering 3,761,461 shares (91.9% of eligible). On September 5, 2026, the company granted replacement options for 1,643,324 shares to named executive officers and restricted stock units covering 760,738 shares to non-executive employees under its 2021 Equity Incentive Plan. The exchange is an issuer tender offer under Rule 13e-4, aimed at option repricing/retention. What to watch: accounting charges and employee retention impact; no public shareholders affected.

NCMI.brief: National CineMedia, Inc. reported that its wholly-owned subsidiary NCM Holdings, LLC closed the previously announced acquisition of Captivate Holdings, LLC and Captivate Network Holdings, Inc. on September 18, 2026. Concurrently, the buyer entered a credit agreement with Crestline Direct Finance as administrative and collateral agent, comprising a fully funded $275.0 million senior secured first lien term loan plus a $25.0 million revolver, with $10.0 million drawn at closing. Proceeds financed the acquisition, repaid Captivate debt, refinanced the U.S. Bank credit agreement, and covered fees. Term loan and revolver each mature September 18, 2031, priced at SOFR plus 7.00% or base rate plus 6.00%.

BKSY.brief: The New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) filed Form 25-NSE on August 26, 2026, to delist BlackSky Technology Inc.'s redeemable warrants (each exercisable for one-eighth of a Class A common share at $92.00 per whole share). NYSE determined the warrants were unsuitable for continued listing due to "abnormally low selling price" under Section 802.01D, suspending trading on August 10, 2026. The company did not appeal within the ten-business-day window. Delisting becomes effective September 8, 2026. The common stock remains listed; the warrant delisting removes an overhang but poses no direct arb angle.

PH.brief: Parker-Hannifin filed an 8-K reporting completion on September 14, 2026 of registered senior note offerings totaling $2.4 billion (four USD tranches maturing 2028-2033) and €2.025 billion (three euro tranches maturing 2030-2036) under its Form S-3 shelf. Net proceeds, plus cash, repay borrowings under the December 10, 2025 364-day term loan with Barclays and other lenders used for the Filtration Group Corporation acquisition. Notes are senior unsecured, rank pari passu with existing senior unsecured debt, carry customary defaults and a 101% change-of-control put. Watch refinancing economics and leverage deleveraging; no equity deal terms.

EQR.brief: The NYSE filed Form 25-NSE to delist ERP Operating Limited Partnership's 7.57% Notes due August 15, 2026, because the entire class was redeemed or paid at maturity on that date. Trading was suspended effective August 17, 2026, with delisting effective at the opening of business on August 28, 2026, per Rule 12d2-2(a)(2). No premium, price, or advisor details apply as this is a routine maturity event. Watch for final redemption payout confirmation and any residual claims processing.

CHRS.brief: Coherus Oncology, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting entry into a new senior secured term loan facility. On August 12, 2026, the company, with subsidiaries, entered a Loan and Security Agreement with Innovatus Life Sciences Lending Fund I, LP, as collateral agent, providing a $55 million Tranche A Term Loan maturing August 2031. The company drew the full amount on August 14, 2026, using proceeds to repay prior senior debt. The loan bears floating interest at 4.15% plus the greater of Prime Rate or 6.75%, with interest-only payments for 36-48 months. Additional tranches of $25 million and $20 million are available under conditions. This is a debt refinancing, not a special situation.

WYFI.brief: WhiteFiber, Inc. disclosed an 8-K that its subsidiary Enovum Data Centers Corp. signed a Real Estate Purchase and Sale Agreement to buy industrial manufacturing properties in Yadkin County, North Carolina, from Unifi Manufacturing, Inc. for $60.0 million in cash. The deal includes a $2.25 million earnest deposit, with $1.0 million potentially non-refundable if the inspection period extends, and an energy capacity study condition. Closing occurs 45 days after the inspection period expires September 15, 2026. The companies must finalize property separation agreements, post-closing occupancy, and partial leaseback terms. Watch for potential delays if energy capacity or separation approvals fail.

BETR.brief: Better Home & Finance Holding Co filed an 8-K/A (Amendment No. 1) on October 14, 2026, updating Item 3.01 to disclose receipt of a Nasdaq written notice dated October 13, 2026, following telephonic notice October 8. Triggering event: board resignations and removals disclosed in earlier 8-Ks (October 2 and October 6, 2026) left the company non-compliant with Nasdaq Listing Rules 5605(b)(1) majority-independent board and 5605(c)(2) three-member independent audit committee; the original filing also cited 5605(d) compensation committee and 5605(e)(1) nomination oversight. The company has until November 27, 2026 (45 calendar days) to submit a compliance plan; if accepted, Nasdaq may extend up to 180 calendar days from the notice date. Listing is unaffected immediately. Watch board reconstitution pace, franchise/shareholder governance risk, and whether Nasdaq accepts the plan or initiates delisting proceedings.

FTK.brief: Flotek Industries filed an 8-K reporting that the Puerto Rico Electric Power Authority (PREPA) terminated the Power Purchase and Operating Agreement (PPOA) effective August 18, 2026. The contract, assigned from Enchanted Rock with PREPA's consent on July 31, 2026, was a 10-year deal expected to generate $40 million annual revenue and a $400 million backlog. PREPA cited two grounds: failure to furnish performance security and the Oversight Board's revocation of approval. No revenue or payments had been received, and 2026 guidance was unaffected. Watch for potential disputes or claims from termination.

REXR.brief: Rexford Industrial Realty, Inc. reported on Form 8-K that its operating partnership and certain subsidiaries completed the disposition of a 22-property industrial portfolio to an affiliate of EQT Real Estate on September 16, 2026, under an August 13, 2026 purchase agreement. Aggregate purchase price was approximately $1.2 billion before customary credits, prorations and closing adjustments. Net proceeds are earmarked for general corporate purposes, including debt repayment, common stock repurchases, and internal repositioning and development projects. No advisor, premium, or per-share terms were disclosed. Watch for use-of-proceeds deployment, buyback pace, and cap-rate read-through for industrial REIT pricing.

WEC.brief: WEC Energy Group and subsidiary Wisconsin Electric Power Company (WEPCO) filed an 8-K disclosing a 20-year Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) with Nextera Energy Point Beach LLC to purchase 86% of capacity, energy, ancillary services, and environmental attributes from Units 1 and 2 of the Point Beach Nuclear Plant. Terms: PPA runs from October 6, 2030 through October 5, 2050 (Unit 1) and March 9, 2033 through March 8, 2053 (Unit 2), replacing an existing expiring agreement. PPA requires Public Service Commission of Wisconsin approval; may be terminated if approval not obtained by January 1, 2028 (extendable to July 1, 2028). What to watch: regulatory approval timeline and customer savings versus current agreement.

WEAV.brief: Weave Communications filed a Form 15-12G on November 6, 2026, terminating registration of its common stock under Section 12(g) and suspending Sections 13 and 15(d) reporting obligations, effective the same date. The filing follows the October 26, 2026 consummation of a merger under an August 18, 2026 Agreement and Plan of Merger among Weave, Willow Parent, LLC and Willow Merger Sub, Inc., with Merger Sub merging into Weave, which survived as a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent. Holders of record fell to one. The filing cites Rule 12g-4(a)(1) and Rule 12h-3(b)(1)(i). No price, premium, advisor or break fee disclosed; the going-private mechanics leave no public float, so the risk-arb angle is closed—watch only for any residual dissenters' appraisal or post-closing true-up.

NLY.brief: The New York Stock Exchange filed a Form 25-NSE on 2026-10-01 to delist and deregister Annaly Capital Management's 6.750% Series I Fixed-to-Floating Rate Cumulative Redeemable Preferred Stock under Rule 12d2-2(a)(1), its US exchange-delisting equivalent. The entire class was called for redemption, maturity or retirement on 2026-10-01; sufficient funds for payment were deposited with an authorized paying agency and made available to holders that same day. Trading was suspended October 1, with removal from listing and registration effective at the opening of business on 2026-10-12. No board recommendation, advisor, price per share, premium, break fee or ownership split was disclosed. Risk-arb angle: preferred redemption mechanics govern; watch for final distribution/payment confirmation from the paying agent.

BLZE.brief: Backblaze, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the issuance of $201.25 million aggregate principal amount of 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2031, including full exercise of the initial purchasers' option for an additional $26.25 million. The notes are senior, unsecured, non-interest-bearing, mature August 15, 2031, and are convertible into Class A common stock under specified conditions, including a stock price trigger of 130% of the conversion price. The indenture with U.S. Bank Trust Company as trustee does not limit additional debt. This is a convertible debt issuance, effectively a capital-raising event, with conversion features creating potential dilution. Watch for conversion triggers and stock price performance relative to the conversion price.

JMSB.brief: John Marshall Bancorp, Inc. filed an amended Form S-4/A registration statement on October 13, 2026, tied to its September 7, 2026 merger agreement with Eagle Financial Services, Inc. (EFSI). The filing registers JMSB common stock to be issued to EFSI shareholders; deal terms such as exchange ratio, per-share price, aggregate value, and premium are not stated in the excerpt. Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP advises JMSB; Troutman Pepper Locke LLP advises EFSI. Both parties will mail a joint proxy statement/prospectus seeking shareholder approvals. The transaction is subject to registration effectiveness and customary closing conditions. Watch for the market-implied exchange ratio, regulatory approvals, dissenting shares, and any revised financial projections.

OPEN.brief: Opendoor Technologies Inc. filed an 8-K reporting the issuance of $650.0 million aggregate principal amount of 0.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2030 in privately negotiated subscription transactions with certain investors. The notes are senior, unsecured, non-interest-bearing, and mature on August 15, 2030. Conversion rights begin February 15, 2030, with an initial conversion rate of 212 shares per $1,000 principal, implying an initial conversion price of approximately $4.72 per share. Settlement is at the company's election in cash, stock, or a combination. The indenture is dated August 19, 2026, with U.S. Bank Trust Company as trustee. The filing is routine financing with a conversion feature, not a typical special situation; classify as Other.

IIIN.brief: Insteel Industries Inc. filed an 8-K announcing the closure of its Upper Sandusky, Ohio facility, consolidating welded wire manufacturing to remaining plants. Up to 65 positions will be eliminated; operations cease by end of October 2026. The company expects a $4.6 million restructuring charge, including $2.5 million equipment relocation, $0.4 million employee separation, $1.0 million asset impairment, and $0.7 million other costs. Cash expenditures begin in Q1 FY2027. This is a cost reduction/restructuring event, not a strategic review. Watch for execution timing and potential supply disruptions.

LDI.brief: loanDepot, Inc. disclosed receipt of an NYSE notice on August 21, 2026, for non-compliance with Section 802.01C of the Listed Company Manual, as its Class A Common Stock average closing price fell below $1.00 over 30 consecutive trading days. The company has a six-month cure period to regain compliance by achieving a closing price and 30-day average of at least $1.00. No immediate impact on listing, operations, or SEC reporting. The company intends to notify the NYSE of its intent to cure. Watch for potential reverse stock split or other price-cure actions and shareholder approval implications.

PFS.brief: The filing is an 8-K reporting that Provident Financial Services, Inc. completed a public offering of $175 million of 6.50% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Subordinated Notes due 2036 under an existing S-3ASR shelf. Issued August 24, 2026, the notes are subordinated unsecured obligations. Net proceeds will repay $150 million of 2.875% notes due 2031 and $20 million of variable-rate junior subordinated notes due 2033, with remainder for general corporate purposes. Piper Sandler and Keefe, Bruyette & Woods led the underwriting. This is a routine debt issuance and refinancing, not a special situation.

TSN.brief: Tyson Foods filed an 8-K reporting early tender results and pricing for cash tender offers for its 3.550% Senior Notes due 2027, 5.400% Senior Notes due 2029, and 4.350% Senior Notes due 2029. The offers, commenced August 10, 2026, are subject to acceptance priority levels, a maximum tender cap, a 2027 sub-cap, and pro rata allocation. Early settlement is set for August 26, 2026. The company also amended terms of the offers. This is a debt buyback, not an equity special situation. Watch for final acceptance and any impact on leverage; risk-arb angle is minimal as it is a liability management exercise.

UBSI.brief: United Bankshares filed an 8-K announcing a third-quarter dividend of $0.38 per share and a new share repurchase plan (2026 Plan) authorizing up to 6.8 million shares (~5% of outstanding). The plan replaces the November 2025 plan, terminated immediately. Repurchases may occur via open market or private negotiations; management retains discretion on timing and quantity. No board recommendation, advisors, or fixed terms beyond the authorization. The filing is a routine capital return event, not a special situation requiring event-driven analysis.

CINF.brief: Cincinnati Financial Corp filed an 8-K on August 25, 2026, disclosing that its Board authorized an additional 15 million shares repurchase under its existing program, supplementing the prior 15 million share authorization from January 2018. The buyback has no fixed expiration. This capital return action is the sole event; no deal terms or pricing were specified. An investor presentation was also furnished under Item 7.01. Watch for quarterly repurchase activity and remaining authorization disclosures in future 10-Q filings.

PARR.brief: Par Pacific Holdings filed an 8-K on August 25, 2026, announcing the signing of an agreement (the 'Agreement') via press release in Exhibit 99.1. The counterparty appears to be Laramie Energy, LLC, based on the excerpt. The filing contains forward-looking statements and indicates a transaction ('Transaction') with expected closing timing. Specific terms such as price per share, premium, or value are not disclosed in the provided excerpt. The board's recommendation and financial advisors are not mentioned. The filing is an 'Other Events' item, suggesting a strategic acquisition by Par Pacific, likely of oil and gas assets or a company. Watch for further details on transaction value and regulatory approvals.

RGEN.brief: Repligen Corporation filed an 8-K on October 6, 2026, disclosing completion of its previously announced acquisition of BioLife Solutions, Inc. via a two-step merger under the July 21, 2026 Agreement and Plan of Merger. BioLife holders received per-share consideration of 0.1442 Repligen shares plus $11.25 cash, with cash in lieu of fractional shares. The Form S-4 was declared effective September 4, 2026, alongside BioLife's definitive proxy. Mechanics include appraisal-rights carve-outs and option treatment. Watch integration execution, stock-consideration dilution, and any dissenting-share appraisal claims.

ALRS.brief: Alerus Financial Corporation filed an 8-K announcing a cash dividend of $0.22 per share payable October 9, 2026 to holders of record September 25, 2026, and a new stock repurchase program authorizing up to 1,250,000 shares, effective upon completion of the prior program (about 320,033 shares remaining as of August 26, 2026) or its expiration on February 18, 2027. The new program expires August 26, 2029. Repurchases may occur in open market transactions under Rule 10b-18 or via Rule 10b5-1 plans. No repurchase obligation exists; timing depends on market conditions and regulatory factors. What to watch: pace of buyback execution relative to the prior program's remaining capacity.

CON.brief: Concentra Group Holdings Parent filed an 8-K reporting Q3 2026 results (Item 2.02), an investor presentation (Item 7.01), and two capital-return actions (Item 8.01). The board declared a $0.0625 per-share cash dividend payable on or about December 4, 2026 to holders of record November 19, 2026, and authorized a new 2026 share repurchase program of up to $250 million of common stock with no expiration, additive to the November 2025 program. Repurchases may occur in the open market or privately negotiated; no advisor or recommendation named. Watch buyback execution pace against free cash flow and leverage.

NBR.brief: Nabors Industries filed an 8-K reporting the acquisition of Quaise Energy Series B-1 Preferred Stock through its subsidiary NETV, paying $35 million in stock consideration via 391,944 Nabors common shares. The transaction includes a collar mechanism: if Quaise sells the shares within 20 days and market value falls below $33.25 million, Nabors issues additional shares or cash; above $36.75 million, Quaise pays Nabors the excess. Registration rights obligate Nabors to file a resale prospectus. This is an equity investment with derivative-like price protection, not a classic special situation; watch collar mechanics and share overhang.

PPL.brief: PPL Corp filed an 8-K reporting the Rhode Island Public Utilities Commission's (RIPUC) decision in subsidiary Rhode Island Energy's (RIE) base distribution rate case. RIPUC authorized $44.1M electric and $93.7M gas annual revenue increases, a 9.275% ROE, and 48/52 debt/equity ratio. It denied RIE's hold harmless proposal but approved an alternative increasing bill credits by ~$11M to ~$170M, effective October 2026-September 2027. PPL reaffirmed 2026 earnings guidance. Regulatory outcome; watch for final written order and possible appeals.

VEL.brief: Velocity Financial's subsidiary Velocity Commercial Capital entered an Equity Purchase Agreement to acquire all equity interests of three entities (formed via statutory division) from Toorak Capital LLC. Consideration is approximately $62 million plus estimated tangible book value, subject to adjustments. Closing conditions include regulatory approvals, completion of a related 'Back Book Acquisition,' warehouse financing conditions, and no material adverse effect. The deal must close within 120 days or termination rights apply. Watch for regulatory approvals and the Back Book Acquisition completion as key conditions to closing.

AAON.brief: AAON, Inc. filed an 8-K on August 21, 2026, announcing a rebranding to operate under the trade name 'The Aaon Group.' This is a non-financial, organizational identity change reflecting the company's evolution into a multi-brand enterprise with operating brands AAON and BASX. The filing includes a press release and updated investor presentation furnished under Items 7.01 and 8.01. There are no deal terms, financial metrics, or transactional elements. The filing is a routine corporate communication, not a special situation, though the rebranding may signal strategic positioning. What to watch: any future structural changes or divestitures under the new enterprise identity.

MBUU.brief: Malibu Boats (MBI) filed an 8-K presenting unaudited pro forma condensed combined financials for FY2026 to reflect its completed acquisition of Saxdor Yachts Oy, a Finnish yacht maker, under a Stock Purchase Agreement closed March 2, 2026. The filing updates previously disclosed pro forma information as required for Form S-3, noting the fiscal-year statement does not project future results. No deal terms, price, premium, or advisors are disclosed. The report is informational only, with no shareholder vote or regulatory clock. What to watch: any subsequent earnings impact from Saxdor integration and potential accretion or dilution disclosures in future filings. Risk-arb angle: deal is closed, so no arbitrage opportunity remains.

SFST.brief: Southern First Bancshares, Inc. filed an 8-K announcing its Board of Directors authorized a share repurchase plan of up to $10.0 million of its common stock, approximately 2% of outstanding shares. Repurchases may occur via open market or privately negotiated transactions at management's discretion, subject to market conditions and legal requirements. No price per share, premium, or timeline was specified; the plan expires after August 23, 2027, unless renewed with Board and Federal Reserve approval. The company is not obligated to repurchase shares. Watch for execution pace and capital management implications.

OKE.brief: ONEOK Inc. filed a Form 15-12G on September 28, 2026, certifying termination of registration of its common stock and registered debt under Section 12(g), and suspension of Sections 13 and 15(d) reporting obligations. The filing follows a September 10, 2026 Oklahoma holding-company reorganization under Section 1081.G of the Oklahoma General Corporation Act, implemented via a September 9, 2026 Agreement and Plan of Merger among Legacy ONEOK, Falcon TopCo, and Falcon Merger Sub. Legacy ONEOK merged into Merger Sub, which survived as a subsidiary of Falcon TopCo; Falcon TopCo was renamed ONEOK, Inc. and succeeded Legacy ONEOK under Rule 12g-3(a). Each Legacy share converted one-for-one into new ONEOK common stock with identical rights. One holder of record remains; new ONEOK retains reporting obligations. Watch for successor-registration confirmation and any related delisting mechanics.

PSNL.brief: Personalis, Inc. filed a definitive proxy statement (DEFM14A) on 2026-10-21 seeking stockholder approval of its acquisition by Tempus AI, Inc. via a two-step merger. Personalis holders receive stock consideration at a fixed exchange ratio of 0.3356 Tempus Class A shares per share if Tempus trades at or below a $48.42 floor, or $16.25 divided by the Tempus stock price if above, implying $16.25 per share at the floor. Tempus may elect cash for up to 50% of shares at $16.25. Both boards approved; no advisor named in excerpt. Watch Tempus share price relative to the floor and any cash election, which would alter the consideration mix.

RHP.brief: Ryman Hospitality Properties, via subsidiary RHP Property GLO, LLC, completed its acquisition of the JW Marriott Orlando Grande Lakes and Ritz-Carlton Orlando, Grande Lakes for ~$1.38 billion from GLO Hotel Owner LLC. Funding combined net proceeds of a 5,865,000-share common stock offering at $117.00/share, $700M of 6.250% senior notes due 2035, and cash. The deal closed September 1, 2026; 2026 guidance was revised. Watch integration performance and post-deal leverage trends.

BBCP.brief: Concrete Pumping Holdings filed an 8-K reporting Q3 FY2026 results and announced initiation of a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.13 per share, payable October 2, 2026, to holders of record September 18, 2026. The Board also approved extension of the existing share repurchase plan. Revenue rose 13% to $116.8 million; adjusted EBITDA up 13% to $30.4 million. Full-year outlook raised. The dividend initiation and share repurchase extension signal a capital return program. Watch for continued execution and any incremental buyback activity.

EQBK.brief: Equity Bancshares filed Amendment No. 1 to its Form S-4 registration statement on October 16, 2026, registering shares for its acquisition of Lincoln Bancorp under a September 2, 2026 Agreement and Plan of Reorganization. The structure is a two-step merger: Penny Merger Sub, Inc., an Iowa subsidiary of Equity, merges into Lincoln, which survives as a wholly owned Equity subsidiary, then merges upstream into Equity. The filing is a joint preliminary proxy statement/prospectus for Lincoln shareholders; no exchange ratio, per-share price, implied value, premium, board recommendation, advisor, break fee or outside close date is stated in the excerpt. Watch for the pricing terms and Lincoln shareholder vote timing in subsequent amendments.

NPWR.brief: Net Power Inc. filed an 8-K reporting that on September 8, 2026, NET Power, LLC, OpCo and the Company entered three integrated Transaction Agreements with Baker Hughes affiliates Nuovo Pignone S.r.l. and Nuovo Pignone International S.r.l.: a JDA Suspension Agreement, a Commercial Agreement Suspension Agreement, and a First Amendment to the License Agreement. The agreements indefinitely suspend utility-scale oxy-combustion development and commercialization arrangements, terminate specified La Porte Demonstration Facility access and exclusivity rights, preserve NP's exclusive utility-scale equipment license, and establish revised industrial-scale licensing. No plant deployment obligation, royalty amount, or royalty assurance was agreed. No board recommendation or advisor disclosed.

BLFS.brief: BioLife Solutions, LLC, as successor by merger to BioLife Solutions, Inc., filed Form 15-12G on October 16, 2026, terminating registration under Section 12(g) and suspending Section 13/15(d) reporting duties for its common stock ($0.001 par) following a completed cash-and-stock acquisition by Repligen Corporation. The merger closed October 6, 2026 under a July 21, 2026 Agreement and Plan of Merger: Merger Sub 1 merged into BioLife, then BioLife merged into Merger Sub 2, renamed BioLife Solutions, LLC, a wholly owned Repligen subsidiary. Holders of record fell to 1, eliminating listing and periodic reporting. Deal terms, board recommendation, and advisor fees are not stated in the excerpt; watch delisting mechanics and any residual noteholder claims.

ELMT.brief: Elmet Group Co. filed an 8-K disclosing a September 23, 2026 share purchase agreement with Masan Horizon Company Limited to acquire 55,138,174 ordinary shares, a 4.99% stake in Vietnam-listed Masan High-Tech Materials Corporation (UPCoM: MSR), for about $124.75 million in a put-through trade. Closing is expected October 1, 2026, settlement October 5, 2026, subject to commercial agreements, regulatory and market approvals, and no material adverse effect. If the per-share price falls outside UPCoM's daily permitted trading band, closing defers. Watch regulatory approvals and VND conversion risk.

FELE.brief: Franklin Electric's wholly owned subsidiary FE Force, LLC closed the purchase of all outstanding stock of Cat Pumps Corporation from its shareholders on September 4, 2026, per an 8-K filed September 8, 2026. Consideration comprised roughly $350 million cash, subject to adjustment, plus performance restricted stock units with a $25 million target value tied to 2028 gross profit thresholds, payable 0% to 200%. Cash was funded from available cash and existing credit facilities. The PRSUs were issued under a Section 4(a)(2) private-placement exemption. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or regulatory clock was disclosed. Watch integration execution, purchase-price adjustments, and PRSU milestone risk.

GE.brief: GE Aerospace filed an 8-K disclosing a definitive agreement to acquire Consolidated Precision Products (CPP), a manufacturer of highly engineered castings, for an all-cash purchase price of $11.75 billion subject to closing adjustments. The deal was announced via press release and investor presentation on September 8, 2026, and is expected to close in the second half of 2027, pending regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions. No board recommendation or financial advisor was named. The long regulatory clock and sizable cash outlay frame the risk-arb watch: antitrust review timing, financing, and any purchase-price adjustment mechanics.

RGTI.brief: Rigetti Computing filed an 8-K disclosing a September 4, 2026 Other Transaction Agreement between its subsidiary Rigetti Co, LLC and the U.S. Department of Commerce under the CHIPS Act of 2022, awarding up to $100 million for superconducting quantum R&D. The award funds three project tasks — readout electronics miniaturization, advanced cryostat architecture, and high-connectivity chip fabrication. Tranches include $43.9 million available at award date, then $29.9 million and $26.2 million contingent on Department discretion and milestone completion. Term runs to the earlier of milestone completion or the fifth anniversary. No board recommendation, advisor, or deal terms stated.

WAFD.brief: WaFd, Inc. filed a definitive proxy (DEFM14A) on 2026-11-04 seeking shareholder approval of its all-stock merger with EverBank Financial Corp under a September 6, 2026 agreement. EverBank merges into WaFd, which survives and renames itself EverBank Financial Corp; WaFd Bank then merges into EverBank, N.A. The fixed exchange ratio gives former EverBank holders approximately 59.175% and WaFd holders 40.825% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis, with roughly 107.3 million WaFd shares expected to be issued; no price per share or premium is stated, and percentages do not adjust for trading prices. EverBank's 675,000 Series A preferred shares convert into a substantially equivalent new WaFd preferred series; WaFd common and its 4.875% Series A preferred remain outstanding. The board recommends approval; advisors are not named in the excerpt. Watch shareholder vote timing, regulatory approvals, and the fixed-ratio arbitrage spread.

BBW.brief: Build-A-Bear Workshop filed an 8-K on September 9, 2026, reporting its board declared a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.23 per common share. The dividend is payable October 8, 2026, to holders of record at the close of business on September 24, 2026, with a press release filed as Exhibit 99.1. No advisor, premium, stake, or buyback terms were disclosed. The item is a routine capital-return declaration, implying an annualized yield dependent on the prevailing share price. What to watch: sustainability of the payout versus retail discretionary cash flow and any future special-dividend or repurchase announcements.

KURA.brief: Kura Oncology disclosed in an Item 8.01 8-K that it formed Caspian Therapeutics, a wholly owned subsidiary, to develop next-generation menin inhibitors (including KO-7246) for diabetes and cardiometabolic disease. On September 8, 2026, Caspian sold $50.0 million of Series A preferred stock in a private financing; Kura invested $4.3 million. Post-financing, Kura holds approximately 49.2% of Caspian's outstanding capital stock, with a Contribution and License Agreement assigning assets for common shares plus up to $1.5 million reimbursement. The structure is a partial monetization/carve-out; watch milestone disclosures and potential further Caspian financings, which could dilute Kura below control and reframe value.

PSTL.brief: Postal Realty Trust disclosed on Form 8-K that it closed, effective September 4, 2026, the acquisition of a 72-property USPS-leased portfolio from entities affiliated with CEO Andrew Spodek for approximately $27.75 million, excluding costs and adjustments. Consideration comprised $25.75 million cash and $2.0 million of Postal Realty LP OP Units, settled as 85,300 units based on a $23.4465 ten-day VWAP. Spodek beneficially owned 50% of the portfolio and received about $11.88 million cash plus all OP units. A special committee of four independent directors approved the transaction; Spodek recused himself. The 100%-occupied portfolio spans roughly 148,374 net leasable square feet at a $14.71 weighted average rent per square foot. The deal was not subject to the existing right of first offer agreement. Watch related-party optics, unit dilution, and potential valuation scrutiny given the CEO's dual role.

UVE.brief: Universal Insurance Holdings filed a Form S-4 registration statement—the US equivalent of a prospectus for a securities registration—covering an exchange offer of up to $100,000,000 aggregate principal amount of new registered 7.75% Senior Unsecured Notes due 2031 for any and all outstanding unregistered notes of the same series issued in a June 16, 2026 private placement. The new notes are registered under the Securities Act; the exchange satisfies obligations under the registration rights agreement. No board recommendation, advisor, stake, premium, or price per share is disclosed—this is a debt exchange, not a merger or tender for equity. What to watch: expiration timing, participation rate, and whether remaining old notes become freely tradable.

BKV.brief: BKV issued $575M of 1.625% convertible senior notes due 2031 via a private 8-K, including a fully exercised $75M option. Net proceeds of ~$554.7M will fund ~$64.7M capped calls and $35M for 1.45M share repurchases at $24.10, with the remainder for general purposes. Semi-annual interest starts April 2027; conversion is contingent pre-July 2031. The combined debt raise and buyback is a capital structure event, not an M&A deal. Watch for conversion price details, buyback pace, and leverage impact.

CPRT.brief: Copart filed an 8-K reporting completion of its acquisition of ACV Auctions via a two-step tender offer and back-end merger. Merger Sub's offer of $10.50 per share in cash, launched September 17, 2026, expired October 15 with 116,818,409 shares validly tendered and not withdrawn—approximately 68.43% of outstanding ACV stock, satisfying the majority condition and all other offer conditions. Merger Sub accepted and paid for tendered shares, and the remaining merger conditions were satisfied on October 16, 2026, completing the transaction under DGCL Section 251(h). Watchers should monitor the short-form merger process, final equity value, and delisting of ACV shares.

RWT.brief: Redwood Trust filed an 8-K on September 10, 2026, disclosing preliminary agreements to dispose of certain legacy bridge loans with aggregate unpaid principal balance of up to roughly $190 million, plus a routine Q3 common dividend of $0.18 per share. The company targets closing late Q3 or early Q4 2026. The board declared dividends; no advisor was named. The expected impact is an approximately 2% decrease in book value per share from the June 30, 2026 level. Watch definitive documentation execution, final proceeds versus principal, and any further book-value dilution risk.

TRMK.brief: Trustmark Corp's bank subsidiary sold 34 branch properties in MS, FL, TN, AL and TX to Blue Owl Real Estate Capital affiliates for $91.7 million, simultaneously signing 15-year triple-net leases with three five-year renewal options at initial aggregate annual rent of $6.4 million, escalating 1.5% annually. No branches close and no markets exit. The sale-leaseback produced a roughly $61.5 million pre-tax gain, offset by a $61.5 million pre-tax loss from reclassifying held-to-maturity securities and swapping $629.9 million of 1.4%-yield securities into $628.0 million of 5.0%-yield securities. Watch capital, NII and rate-risk effects, not deal-arb.

WYNN.brief: Wynn Resorts, Limited filed an 8-K on September 10, 2026 announcing that indirect wholly-owned subsidiaries Wynn Resorts Finance, LLC and Wynn Resorts Capital Corp. plan a private offering of $900 million aggregate principal amount of Senior Notes due 2035. Net proceeds, plus cash on hand, will be contributed or lent to Wynn Las Vegas, LLC to redeem in full its outstanding 5.250% Senior Notes due 2027 and pay related fees. The filing states no price per share, premium, advisor, board recommendation, or closing date; it is a routine debt refinancing rather than a change-of-control or shareholder-return event.

LEU.brief: Centrus Energy filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement for a $500 million capital raise: 500,000 Class A shares at $199.64, 2,005,513 pre-funded warrants at $199.54 (strike $0.10), and 6,992,382 common warrants in four series struck at $226.8625, $272.2350, $317.6075 and $362.9800, each divided into tranches expiring on anniversaries of the September 10, 2026 trade date; per-share pricing implies an 8.8% premium to the $181.49 last sale. Net proceeds before expenses are $490 million, with up to $2 billion more if warrants are fully exercised. Watch warrant overhang and potential dilution.

GMRS.brief: GMR Solutions Inc. filed an 8-K on September 11, 2026 disclosing that subsidiary Global Medical Response, Inc. obtained binding lender commitments to reprice its existing first lien term loan, cutting the SOFR margin from +3.25% to +2.75% (about 50 basis points), and to voluntarily prepay roughly $200 million of the outstanding balance. Expected annual cash interest savings approximate $28 million; closing targeted on or about September 17, 2026, subject to definitive documentation and customary conditions. No board recommendation, advisor, premium, or equity stake is stated; watch execution risk and deleveraging follow-through.

HPP.brief: Hudson Pacific Properties, L.P. and affiliates disclosed an Extension and Loan Modification Agreement dated September 9, 2026 with Wilmington Trust, as trustee for BXHPP Trust 2021-Film CMBS holders, amending the August 2021 $1.1 billion CMBS mortgage financing on the co-owned Hollywood Media Portfolio. The 8-K, furnished under Items 7.01 and 8.01 with a press release, extends and modifies loan terms. No price, stake, or premium terms were stated; the transaction addresses maturity/performance issues for a leveraged landlord. Watch for extension length, covenant relief, paydown or reserve requirements, and any equity cure or recapitalization implications.

PI.brief: Impinj filed an 8-K disclosing privately-negotiated exchange agreements with certain holders of its 1.125% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027. The company will exchange roughly $56.5 million in cash plus about 188,451 shares, based on the Reference Price, for $56.3 million principal of the 2027 Notes; amounts adjust over a two-day measurement period ending September 14, 2026, with closings expected on or about September 16, 2026. Cash on hand funds the exchange, leaving about $1.0 million principal outstanding. Shares issued under Section 4(a)(2) to qualified institutional buyers; watch settlement share true-up and remaining note overhang.

ETD.brief: Ethan Allen Interiors Inc., the Delaware-incorporated furniture maker, filed a definitive additional proxy statement (DEFC14A) on September 24, 2026, a revised solicitation rather than a merger document; no acquirer, stake percentage, price per share, or premium is stated. The excerpt carries only cover-page and XBRL tagging data, including executive-compensation and equity-award values for fiscal years 2022 through 2026. No board recommendation or financial advisor is named in the text. Because the filing amends a live solicitation, structural notes center on shareholder-vote mechanics and compensation disclosures, not collateral, overhang, or a regulatory clock. Watch for the underlying merger or tender terms, if any.

NG.brief: NovaGold Resources filed an 8-K updating its July 22, 2026 plan of arrangement under the BC Business Corporations Act, in which newly formed Delaware entity New NovaGold will acquire all outstanding NovaGold shares. Terms are a one-for-one share exchange, with Paulson contributing its 40% Donlin Gold LLC stake for New NovaGold voting and non-voting stock, voting capped at 19.99%, valued at a 10% discount to NovaGold's 10-day VWAP as of July 21, 2026. No price, premium, break fee, or close date was stated. Watch shareholder and court approvals plus Donlin funding milestones.

ADUS.brief: Addus HealthCare, Inc., an Illinois subsidiary of Addus HomeCare Corporation, entered into an Equity and Asset Purchase Agreement with AccentCare, Inc. to acquire the seller's personal and community care business outside New York for $275,000,000 in cash, subject to customary working capital adjustments. The transaction involves ten transferred entities plus certain assets of AccentCare Home Health of Mountain Valley. Closing is conditioned on regulatory approvals, HSR waiting period expiration, and other customary conditions, with the 8-K filed September 14, 2026 and dated September 12, 2026. Watch regulatory clearance timing and any potential divestiture requirements.

AIRJ.brief: AirJoule Technologies subsidiary acquired all equity of Bitsink LLC, a South Carolina AI data-center cooling, power distribution and racking manufacturer, under a Sept 10, 2026 Purchase Agreement. Consideration was $18,000,000 cash plus 1,859,504 Class A shares issued via a concurrent Subscription Agreement, plus up to $40,000,000 of earnouts payable in Class A stock if 2027-2029 revenue targets are met. Seller Stanislav Dyshko accepted non-compete and non-solicitation covenants. Watch earnout dilution, share overhang and revenue-target achievability as the arbitrage angle.

BWMN.brief: Nasdaq Stock Market LLC filed a Form 25-NSE on 2026-11-06 to strike Bowman Consulting Group Ltd.'s common stock from listing and registration under Section 12(b), citing 17 CFR 240.12d2-2(a)(3) — the issuer no longer meets listing standards after a corporate action extinguished the security. The filing names Katelin Rowe as the CDO analyst contact and lists the security as Common Stock (SEC File 001-40371). No deal terms, board recommendation, or financial advisor were disclosed in the excerpt; the rule basis implies a merger, consolidation, or similar transaction rather than a compliance failure. Mechanically, delisting removes the Nasdaq trading venue and triggers Section 12(b) deregistration; watch for the underlying transaction's 8-K/merger proxy, the exact consideration and closing date, and whether OTC quoting or a cash-out follows.

PURR.brief: Hyperliquid Strategies Inc filed an 8-K on September 14, 2026 disclosing Amendment No. 2 to its October 22, 2025 ChEF Purchase Agreement with Chardan Capital Markets LLC. The amendment reset the VWAP purchase price for shares the issuer may elect to sell: 98.5% of VWAP for VWAP and Intraday VWAP purchases, and 97.0% for Off-Hour VWAP purchases. This is a structured equity facility, equivalent to a US at-the-market or standby equity distribution pact, not a special situation. No board recommendation, advisor, or deal terms beyond the pricing formula were stated, leaving dilution and pricing risk as watch items.

PRDO.brief: Perdoceo Education Corp filed an 8-K on September 14, 2026, disclosing a Membership Interest Purchase Agreement to acquire 100% of South University Savannah, LLC from nonprofit seller South University Member, Inc. Initial cash consideration is $150 million at closing, subject to working-capital and debt adjustments as of April 2027, plus $18 million deferred cash over 24 months and up to $56 million in EBITDA-linked earn-outs for fiscal 2027-2029, funded from cash. South generated roughly $291 million 2025 revenue and $34 million adjusted operating income, serving about 10,500 students; no board recommendation or advisor named. Watch regulatory/accreditation approvals and earn-out thresholds.

PDM.brief: Piedmont Realty Trust filed an 8-K updating acquisition and disposition activity and capital markets plans. On September 10, 2026 it acquired 4075 Wilson Boulevard, a 189,000 sq ft Ballston, Arlington Class A office building, for a net purchase price of about $52.7 million; the asset is 83% leased with 5.5-year weighted-average lease term. It also completed the $12.0 million Royal Lane land sale in Dallas and contracted to sell office properties for roughly $80 million, expected to close in Q4 2026. Separately, the operating partnership announced a proposed $200 million private Rule 144A offering of exchangeable senior notes due 2031, fully guaranteed by the Company. Watch due diligence and closing risk on the pending disposition, plus notes pricing and exchange-premium terms.

SION.brief: Sionna Therapeutics filed an 8-K disclosing a board-approved restructuring approved September 9, 2026, cutting headcount roughly 46% to concentrate on the SION-451/SION-2222 dual combination program and extend cash runway. The company is winding down the SION-719 add-on program, terminating related clinical and manufacturing vendor pacts. Estimated charges total about $6.4 million: $5.3 million severance and post-employment benefits, $0.7 million contract close-outs, $0.4 million stock compensation, substantially complete by Q3 2026. Chief Business Officer Caroline Stark Beer's employment terminated without cause effective September 15, 2026, triggering Severance Plan benefits. Watch cash runway, execution risk, and any further charges.

TCBI.brief: Texas Capital Bancshares filed a Form 25 on 2026-10-08 voluntarily withdrawing from Nasdaq listing and Section 12(b) registration its Depositary Shares, each representing a 1/40th interest in a share of 5.75% Fixed-Rate Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock, Series B. The issuer, not an acquirer, is the actor; no stake, price, premium, board recommendation, advisor, or deal value appears. Mechanics: the filing triggers a 17 CFR 240.12d2-2(c) delisting, with deregistration becoming effective 90 days later absent Commission objection; no collateral, overhang, ownership split, or regulatory clock is disclosed. What to watch: redemption or exchange terms for the Series B depositary shares and any related capital action.

THRY.brief: Thryv Holdings, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting that its wholly-owned subsidiary Thryv, Inc. entered into an Asset Purchase Agreement on September 12, 2026 with Coldwater YP, LLC, an affiliate of Carolwood, L.P., to sell its US, Australia and New Zealand Yellow and White Pages print directories, related digital editions and Australia White Pages for a $142 million cash purchase price, subject to customary adjustments. The Purchase Agreement includes customary representations and warranties, representation and warranty insurance, and customary closing conditions and termination provisions. No board recommendation or advisor is disclosed. Watch regulatory and closing conditions, purchase-price adjustments and the press release for strategic rationale and use of proceeds.

AXON.brief: Axon filed an 8-K disclosing an incremental minority investment of roughly $1.2 billion in Skydio, lifting its ownership from about 15% (as of September 30, 2026) to approximately 37% on a fully diluted basis. Consideration is expected to be ~60% cash (~$720 million) and the remainder in Axon common stock, with final mix subject to Series G settlement. The initial closing occurred November 5, 2026: 25,000,000 non-voting Series G preferred shares at $10.19617/share, ~$254.9 million, half cash and half Axon stock. Remaining tranches expected across Q4 2026 and Q1 2027. Watch equity issuance, lock-up overhang and closing conditions.

BKE.brief: The Buckle, Inc. filed an 8-K on September 15, 2026, furnishing a press release announcing that its Board authorized a quarterly cash dividend of $0.35 per share, payable October 29, 2026 to holders of record at the close of business October 15, 2026. The declaration was made at the Board's quarterly meeting on September 14, 2026. No advisor, premium, or strategic transaction is referenced; this is an ordinary capital-return action by the Nebraska-based specialty retailer, which operates 447 stores in 42 states. The dividend was declared at the Board's quarterly meeting, with no advisor named. Watch for any future deviation in dividend policy or payout coverage.

DHI.brief: D.R. Horton filed an 8-K on September 15, 2026 disclosing that its board authorized an additional $5.0 billion share repurchase program with no expiration date, leaving approximately $53 million under the prior authorization. Management expects total fiscal 2026 repurchases of at least $3.25 billion. No price, premium, advisor, or closing date is stated. The open-ended authorization gives the builder substantial buyback capacity, signaling capital-return priority amid housing-cycle uncertainty; watch quarterly share-count reduction, cash flow versus land spend, and whether repurchases accelerate or slow with mortgage-rate-driven demand.

LIND.brief: Lindblad Expeditions filed an 8-K disclosing that on September 14, 2026 its subsidiary entered a Purchase Agreement to acquire a 60% controlling interest in White Desert Ltd, PNR Airways Ltd and Echo Charlie Ltd, Antarctic expedition and aviation-based experiential travel operators, for roughly $61 million cash plus about $6 million for balance-sheet cash, subject to working-capital, cash and debt true-ups. Two options to buy the remaining equity in equal tranches within 30 days after December 31, 2030 and 2031, priced off EBITDA, were granted; employment agreements were signed with key employees and updated guidance issued.

TYRA.brief: Tyra Biosciences filed an 8-K on September 15, 2026, disclosing an underwriting agreement dated September 14, 2026 with Jefferies, Guggenheim, Cantor Fitzgerald and Barclays for a public offering of 9,079,000 common shares at $22.03 and 9,078,529 pre-funded warrants at $22.029 (strike $0.001), gross proceeds about $400.0M; underwriting price $20.7082/$20.7072 per share/warrant. Closing expected September 15, 2026. No board recommendation or premium stated. Pre-funded warrant exercise is capped by 4.99%/9.99%/19.99% beneficial-ownership blockers, adjustable to 19.99% with 61 days' notice. Watch dilution, overhang and pricing versus market.

NVT.brief: nVent Electric plc, through Hoffman Schroff Holdings and nVent Finance S.r.l., completed an $800 million offering of 6.150% senior notes due 2036, guaranteed jointly and severally by the parent and finance subsidiary. Proceeds, alongside a $600 million term loan, a $250 million revolving facility draw and cash, fund the roughly $1.75 billion acquisition of Maverick Power, LLC. The Irish-domiciled registrant acts as acquirer. No board recommendation, advisor, premium or per-share terms appear in the excerpt. Watch closing conditions, leverage and rating-event interest-rate adjustments.

MITT.brief: TPG Mortgage Investment Trust filed an Amendment No. 1 to its Form S-4 registration statement, the US equivalent of a prospectus/proxy for a merger, in connection with a combination with Cherry Hill Mortgage Investment Corporation. The filing registers TPG shares to be issued and covers a joint proxy statement/prospectus; it remains subject to completion and SEC effectiveness. No price per share, stake percentage, implied value, or premium is stated in the excerpt. Mechanics to watch include shareholder votes, the SEC effectiveness clock, and risk-arb focus on deal terms once disclosed.

BCBP.brief: BCB Bancorp's BCB Community Bank disclosed definitive agreements with six purchasers to sell problem loan portfolios totaling ~$205.3M unpaid principal at June 30, 2026, comprising ~$180.7M commercial/multifamily real estate, ~$14.8M C&I, and ~$9.8M construction loans, largely criticized or classified. Five closings occurred; the sixth is expected before quarter-end. The estimated pre-tax loss is $43.3M, recorded in Q3 2026. Each agreement is independent, with no cross-closing conditions. Watch the capital and reserve impact, remaining problem-loan overhang, and whether further portfolio sales follow.

GSBC.brief: Great Southern Bancorp, the Maryland-incorporated holding company for Great Southern Bank, filed an 8-K on September 16, 2026 disclosing that its board declared a $0.43 per common share quarterly cash dividend, payable October 14, 2026 to holders of record September 28, 2026. This marks the 147th consecutive quarterly dividend. No advisor, premium, or structural terms apply; the release is routine shareholder-return disclosure tied to ordinary capital allocation rather than any transaction. Watch for dividend sustainability against bank earnings and any future special-dividend or buyback signals, which would shift the capital-return narrative.

ATLC.brief: Atlanticus Holdings disclosed on Form 8-K (Item 8.01) that subsidiary Mercury Financial, LLC completed the sale and assignment of the MERCURY word mark and related intellectual property to an unaffiliated third party on September 30, 2026, for $27.5 million in cash. Underlying consumer credit card receivables from the MERCURY-branded program remain with the Company. The purchaser granted a non-exclusive, royalty-free 12-month license to solicit new card consumers via the mark, plus up to five additional years for servicing legacy accounts and regulatory obligations. Watch brand-transition execution, bank-partner consent, and any further monetization or goodwill implications.

PXED.brief: Phoenix Education Partners (NYSE: PXED) disclosed on Form 8-K that on September 16, 2026 it agreed to acquire Fuel50 Inc., an AI-powered workforce transformation platform, via merger of CEG Merger Sub into Fuel50, which survives as a wholly-owned subsidiary. Aggregate cash consideration is approximately $31.5 million, subject to customary working capital, cash, debt and expense adjustments, plus up to $8.5 million of earnouts through calendar 2027 tied to performance milestones. Funded from cash on hand; closing expected within 30 days pending Fuel50 stockholder approval. No board recommendation or advisor named; deal is small and all-cash, limiting arb dynamics—watch earnout triggers and closing conditions.

DASH.brief: DoorDash filed an 8-K under Items 8.01/9.01 disclosing completion of its reincorporation from Delaware to Nevada, effective September 18, 2026 at 12:02 a.m. Pacific, following filings with both secretaries of state on September 17, 2026. Each Delaware Class A and Class B share automatically converted one-for-one into Nevada shares of identical par value $0.00001, with no certificate exchange required. New Nevada articles and bylaws govern, plus fresh indemnification agreements with officers and directors. No change to business, management, assets or liabilities; a governance redomiciliation, not a special situation, with litigation-risk/statutory-ambiguity the only watch item.

HALO.brief: Halozyme (HALO) closed a $1.5B private placement of 1.50% Convertible Senior Notes due 2033, including the $200M initial-purchaser option. Net proceeds were about $1,471.1M; roughly $187.5M funded capped-call transactions. The company expects to repurchase approximately $151.7M of 0.25% 2027 notes and $220.0M of 1.00% 2028 notes, with total repurchase costs stated for the 2027 tranche. Notes were sold to qualified institutional buyers under Rule 144A and are unregistered. Key angles: capped-call dilution mitigation, unregistered share overhang, and liability-management execution.

HYPR.brief: Hyperfine, Inc. filed an 8-K on September 18, 2026, disclosing receipt on September 17, 2026 of a Nasdaq Listing Qualifications staff notice that its Class A common stock (HYPR) closed below $1.00 for 30 consecutive business days, failing Nasdaq Global Market Listing Rule 5450(a)(1). The notice has no immediate effect on listing or operations. Hyperfine has until March 16, 2027, a 180-day compliance period, to regain the $1.00 minimum bid for at least 10 consecutive business days, subject to staff extension. A further 180-day period is available only via transfer to the Nasdaq Capital Market and satisfaction of other listing standards, potentially requiring a reverse split. No board recommendation, advisor, deal terms, or activist filer is stated. Watch for a reverse-split announcement and potential delisting appeal risk.

MRSH.brief: NYSE filed a Form 25-NSE on September 21, 2026, notifying the SEC that it intends to remove Marsh & McLennan Companies' entire class of 1.349% Senior Notes due 2026 from listing and registration, effective at the opening of business on October 2, 2026, under Rule 12d2-2(a)(2), the US equivalent of a delisting-and-deregistration notice. The filing states the entire class was redeemed, paid at maturity, or retired on September 21, 2026, and that trading in the notes was suspended the same day. No deal terms, board recommendation, advisor, or price are stated. Arbitrage angle: confirm redemption payment and final accrued interest; residual value turns on trustee disbursement mechanics.

EBF.brief: Ennis, Inc. filed an 8-K reporting quarterly results and a dividend increase. The board declared a 5.0% raise in the quarterly cash dividend from $0.25 to $0.2625 per share, payable November 6, 2026 to holders of record October 9, 2026. Revenues rose 3.3% to $102.0 million, but EPS fell to $0.37 from $0.51 on prior-year favorable and current-year adverse litigation items. The filing is a routine earnings-and-dividend release, not a structural special situation; the risk-arb angle is minimal, with the payout and record date the only dates to watch.

HE.brief: Hawaiian Electric Industries filed an 8-K disclosing it monetized 30% of its 9.9% stake in American Savings Bank (NYSE: ASBH) via ASB's IPO, selling ~2.0 million shares for $29.5 million net proceeds on September 16, 2026. Underwriters fully exercised a 30-day option for 293,904 additional shares on September 21, adding $4.4 million net. HEI's residual 6.4% stake was worth ~$73.5 million based on ASB's $17.57 September 18 close, subject to a 180-day lockup. Proceeds fund Maui wildfire settlement payments, reducing future capital raises. Watch lockup expiration and any follow-on block sale overhang.

VGZ.brief: Vista Gold Corp filed a preliminary management information and proxy circular (PREM14A) dated October 19, 2026, for a special shareholder meeting on a proposed plan of arrangement with Artemis Gold Inc., a Canadian-plan-of-arrangement structure functionally equivalent to a US merger. Vista's board, acting on the Special Committee's recommendation, urges shareholders to vote FOR the Arrangement Resolution. Consideration is stock-based (Artemis shares), though the excerpt does not state an exchange ratio, implied equity value, or premium; Georgeson acts as proxy solicitor, and financial-advisor opinions are summarized. Mechanics entail shareholder and court approvals, exchange listing and delisting steps, and other regulatory consents. Watch the vote threshold, dissent rights, and any appraisal overhang.

ACRE.brief: Ares Commercial Real Estate Corporation reported that a wholly-owned subsidiary completed the sale of a multi-building North Carolina office property to an unaffiliated buyer for $64 million cash on September 18, 2026. The company had taken legal title via deed in lieu of foreclosure on September 19, 2024, and classified the asset as held for sale beginning in Q1 2026. No board recommendation or advisor was named. Pro forma balance sheet and income statements were filed to reflect the disposition as of June 30, 2026 and January 1, 2025. Watch for the realized gain or loss versus carrying value and redeployment of proceeds.

LXEO.brief: Lexeo Therapeutics filed an 8-K on September 29, 2026, reporting completion of its previously announced merger of Mantle Therapeutics Inc. under a September 16, 2026 Agreement and Plan of Merger, with Merger Sub merging into Mantle and Mantle surviving as a wholly owned Lexeo subsidiary. Consideration: $5.3 million cash plus $3.0 million in unregistered Lexeo common stock, subject to adjustments. Mantle restricted stock vested pre-close; SAFEs converted per liquidity-event provisions and convertible notes were paid off. Watch milestone/CVR economics, share overhang from the 4(a)(2) issuance, and any earnout funding obligations.

PRGS.brief: Progress Software filed an 8-K on September 22, 2026, reporting completion of its purchase of substantially all assets and employees of Domo, Inc., excluding Domo's net operating loss carryforwards, under an Asset Purchase Agreement dated July 22, 2026. Progress paid $400 million in cash, funded via cash on hand and an existing revolving credit facility. No board recommendation or advisor was named. Progress will file audited financial statements and pro forma information by amendment under Regulation S-X. Watch integration execution, leverage impact, and purchase-price allocation, with no public deal spread remaining.

RCL.brief: Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd. filed an 8-K on September 23, 2026 announcing definitive agreements to acquire a 50% equity interest in the business comprising Sandals and Beaches Resorts for a base cash purchase price of approximately $3.0 billion, with committed debt financing from Morgan Stanley. The transaction is expected to close in early 2027, subject to customary approvals and closing conditions. The partnership expands Royal Caribbean into the all-inclusive resort space, combining Sandals and Beaches Caribbean hospitality expertise with Royal Caribbean's vacation brands and loyalty platform. No board recommendation, premium, or per-share price was disclosed.

WLDN.brief: Willdan Group filed an 8-K reporting completion on October 30, 2026 of its previously announced acquisition of 100% of Mantis Intermediate Holdings, LLC via subsidiary Willdan Energy Solutions, under a Membership Interest Purchase Agreement dated September 22, 2026 with Seller Mantis NewCo. Consideration was approximately $285.0 million cash, subject to customary post-closing adjustments, funded by $35.0 million under the existing Revolving Credit Facility and $250.0 million under an amended Credit Agreement. The filing also discloses a Second Amendment to the credit facility with BMO Harris as administrative agent. Watch leverage and integration execution.

CD.brief: Chaince Digital Holdings Inc. filed an 8-K reporting that on October 1, 2026 it entered a Subscription Agreement with Sentinel Strategic Holdings LP, subscribing for a Class A limited partnership interest and committing US$20.0 million. The subscription was accepted by Sentinel Strategic Holdings GP Ltd.; a drawdown notice for the full commitment was received and funded October 5, 2026. No price per share, premium, advisor, board recommendation, or close date is stated. The filing was incorporated into the company's Form F-3 shelf registration. Watch for follow-on drawdowns, valuation marks, and disclosure gaps on Sentinel's underlying assets.

INNV.brief: InnovAge Holding Corp. filed an 8-K disclosing a secondary offering by a selling shareholder. Under a September 22, 2026 underwriting agreement with Barclays, Goldman Sachs and Wells Fargo as representatives, the Selling Shareholder agreed to sell 10,000,000 firm shares at $9.25 per share, plus a 30-day option for up to 1,500,000 additional shares. The company receives no proceeds, and shares settled September 24, 2026. No board recommendation or advisor is named. The offering was made under an existing Form S-3 shelf registration statement. Watch for overhang, lock-up terms and the extent of the option exercise.

UTMD.brief: Utah Medical Products filed a final SC TO-I/A amendment reporting results of its issuer tender offer, which expired October 27, 2026. The company offered to buy up to 650,000 shares at $75.00 per share under an Offer to Purchase dated September 24, 2026; only 327,740 shares were tendered and purchased, for total consideration of $24,580,500. Administration fees of $107,720 to the depositary/information agent and $6,732 in SEC filing fees raised the effective cost to $75.35 per share; a 1% federal excise tax on repurchases also applies. Post-offer shares outstanding total 2,849,041. Watch the proration-free shortfall as a signal of holder reluctance and the excise-tax drag on buyback economics.

WHK.brief: WhiteHawk Minerals Corp. filed an 8-K/A confirming completion of the SJM II Acquisition on September 25, 2026, via indirect subsidiaries WhiteHawk Income Marcellus LLC and WhiteHawk Income Haynesville LLC as Buyers, purchasing mineral, fee mineral, overriding royalty and non-participating royalty interests in the Marcellus and Haynesville shales from Three Rivers Royalty II, LLC and Cypress Mineral Partners, LLC. Aggregate purchase price was $105.0 million, subject to adjustments, with approximately $96.8 million paid at closing. Funding combined Series E Preferred proceeds, a September 21, 2026 private placement of Class A Common Stock, and cash on hand. The Series E ranks senior to common and pays monthly cash dividends; terms beyond that are truncated, and no board recommendation or advisor is named. Watch integration, preferred dividend overhang, and dilution from the common placement.

GTY.brief: Getty Realty Corp., through subsidiary Getty Leasing, Inc., entered a September 22, 2026 purchase and sale agreement with Refuel Operating Company, LLC and Blue Horseshoe 2, LLC to acquire 41 convenience store properties in Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Texas for approximately $260.9 million; the acquisition closed simultaneously with signing. Getty funded the purchase with forward equity proceeds, unsecured debt, and property disposition proceeds. The properties were leased back to Refuel under four 20-year unitary triple net leases, guaranteed by FR Refuel, LLC, with five-year rent escalations. No board recommendation or advisor was named. Watch sale-leaseback tenant credit and rent coverage.

LFCR.brief: Lifecore Biomedical filed an 8-K (Item 8.01) disclosing that on November 4, 2026 the DOJ and FTC granted early termination of the HSR waiting period for its previously announced September 27, 2026 Agreement and Plan of Merger with Lifecore Inc. (Parent) and Hazel Merger Sub, Inc., under which Merger Sub merges into the company, leaving Lifecore a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent. This satisfies the antitrust condition; remaining conditions include stockholder adoption of the merger agreement at a special meeting. No price, premium, advisor or break fee is stated in the excerpt. Watch the special-meeting vote and any remaining regulatory or closing conditions.

FLWS.brief: 1-800-Flowers.com filed an 8-K disclosing a September 26, 2026 Asset Purchase Agreement to sell its Personalization Mall, Things Remembered, and Personalization Universe businesses to PlanetArt, LLC for $45.0 million cash, subject to working capital and other adjustments. The company acts as seller; no board recommendation or advisor is named in the excerpt. Closing conditions include no Business Material Adverse Effect, accuracy of reps and warranties, and specified third-party consents. Ancillary commercial and transition services agreements are contemplated. The deal terms as stated are a $45 million all-cash purchase price, with no per-share metric given.

MAA.brief: The New York Stock Exchange filed a Form 25-NSE on October 1, 2026, notifying the SEC of its intent to delist and deregister Mid-America Apartment Communities' entire class of 8.50% Series I Cumulative Redeemable Preferred Stock under Rule 12d2-2(a)(1). The full class was called for redemption on October 1, 2026, with sufficient funds deposited with an authorized paying agent and made available to holders that same day; trading was suspended immediately. Removal from listing and registration becomes effective at the opening of business on October 12, 2026. No board recommendation, advisor, stake, or per-share price is disclosed. The event is a clean redemption-driven delisting, not a merger, leaving only residual transfer and final-distribution mechanics to monitor.

HTO.brief: H2O America filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement for an offering of 6,500,000 Equity Units at $50 stated amount, raising $325M gross ($315.25M net) via Wells Fargo, J.P. Morgan, BofA and TD as joint book-runners, with a 975,000-unit over-allotment option. Each Corporate Unit pairs a purchase contract with a 1/20 interest in $1,000 principal of 5.300% Remarketable Senior Notes due 2031; 2.450% contract adjustment payments apply. Settlement is November 1, 2029, converting into shares based on a market-value formula bounded by $58.5686 and $68.8231. Common closed at $58.57 on October 29, 2026. Watch dilution and remarketing reset risk.

LQDT.brief: Liquidity Services filed an 8-K reporting entry into a merger agreement and immediate closing of its acquisition of Auction Holdings, Inc., operator of Invaluable, AuctionZip and RFC Auction Systems, online marketplaces for fine art, antiques and estate auctions. The company paid $80 million cash, funded from cash on hand, with customary working capital, cash and debt adjustments. Merger Sub merged into Auction Holdings, which survives as a wholly owned subsidiary. About $9.4 million was escrowed for indemnification and purchase-price adjustments, released at 12-month and three-year anniversaries. Key employees signed 12- or 24-month restrictive covenants; investors signed non-solicitation agreements. Arbitrage angle is limited as the deal is already closed; watch integration, escrow claims and seller earnout mechanics.

SGP.brief: SpyGlass Pharma filed an 8-K on October 1, 2026, announcing its acquisition of 100% of Advanced Vision Science, Inc. from Santen Holdings US, Inc., with Santen Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. guaranteeing the seller's obligations. Consideration was $13,000,000 cash, subject to customary post-closing adjustments. AVS previously supplied SpyGlass with intraocular lenses. Ancillary agreements include an amended supply and distribution pact granting Santen exclusive Japan sales rights to Eternity lenses and cross-licenses of intellectual property. No board recommendation or advisor was disclosed. The all-cash deal closed simultaneously with signing, eliminating financing and regulatory-approval risk.

VERI.brief: Veritone, Inc. filed an 8-K on October 1, 2026, reporting a registered direct offering of 20,000,000 common shares to named purchasers under a September 30, 2026 securities purchase agreement. The offering used the company's effective Form S-3 shelf (No. 333-280148). No price per share, premium, board recommendation, advisor, or closing date appears in the excerpt. Cooley LLP supplied the legality opinion. Mechanics involve shelf takedown and share overhang from new issuance; watch dilution and pricing terms.

INBK.brief: First Internet Bancorp filed an S-4/A amendment on October 8, 2026, registering an exchange offer of up to $20.5 million aggregate principal amount of new registered 8.00% fixed-to-floating rate subordinated notes due 2036 for any and all outstanding unregistered notes issued in a September 10, 2026 private placement. The exchange satisfies obligations under a registration rights agreement with purchasers; no cash proceeds or increased indebtedness result. The registration statement remains subject to completion and SEC effectiveness. CUSIP, pricing, and closing mechanics are unstated. Risk-arb angle: no economic trade; the event hinges solely on SEC effectiveness and the exchange deadline, not on credit terms.

IMXI.brief: International Money Express (IMXI) filed an 8-K updating its pending merger with The Western Union Company, announced August 10, 2025, under which Ivey Merger Sub, Inc. will merge into IMXI, leaving IMXI a wholly owned Western Union subsidiary. All required regulatory approvals are secured except California DFPI approval, suspended August 14, 2026 pending review, and Hart-Scott-Rodino clearance. Because the original HSR waiting period expired October 6, 2025, and clearance lapses after one year, both parties refiled Premerger Notification forms on October 2, 2026, starting a new 30-day period; early termination was requested. No price, premium, or closing date is stated.

OPK.brief: OPKO Health's wholly owned BioReference Health unit agreed to sell its clinical and anatomic pathology lab testing business—including women's health, urology, corrections and the proprietary 4Kscore prostate cancer test—to Laboratory Corporation of America Holdings (Labcorp) under an October 14, 2026 Asset Purchase Agreement. Labcorp pays $722 million cash at closing, subject to revenue-based adjustment, plus up to $150 million over ten years tied to 4Kscore sales. Closing requires HSR clearance and customary conditions, no financing condition, outside date April 14, 2027. Buyer owes a $28.88 million termination fee for antitrust-approval failure. Watch HSR review and revenue-adjustment mechanics.

IMNM.brief: Immunome filed an 8-K disclosing Amendment No. 4 to its 2017 license agreement with Bristol-Myers Squibb, terminating all milestone and royalty obligations and assigning patent rights for varegacestat (AL102) and AL101 to Immunome. Consideration was $20.0 million cash plus 4,425,487 newly issued common shares, issued under a concurrent stock issuance agreement. Immunome must file a resale registration statement by November 16, 2026, with effectiveness within 60 days. The structure removes a royalty overhang but adds BMS share overhang; watch registration timing, dilution, and any BMS resale pressure.

PTC.brief: PTC Inc. filed a preliminary proxy statement (PREM14A) on November 3, 2026, for a special shareholder meeting to approve its merger with Schneider Electric SE. Under the October 4, 2026 merger agreement, Schneider's Grand Slam Merger Sub, Inc. will merge into PTC, which survives as a wholly owned Schneider subsidiary; PTC holders receive $205 in cash per share, without interest. The PTC board unanimously determined the deal fair and in shareholders' best interests, approved the agreement and recommends voting FOR the merger proposal and FOR the advisory merger-related compensation proposal. Mechanics: virtual special meeting at a date to be set; no premium, implied value, advisor, break fee or regulatory clock terms appear in the excerpt. Risk-arb angle: watch the unset meeting date and proxy supplement disclosures for financing, antitrust timing and any go-shop or fiduciary-out pressure.

RXO.brief: RXO, Inc. filed an 8-K on October 5, 2026, disclosing an Agreement and Plan of Merger dated October 4, 2026, under which C.H. Robinson Worldwide, Inc. will acquire RXO through a two-step merger via Merger Sub Inc. and Viking Logistics LLC. RXO will become a wholly owned C.H. Robinson subsidiary. The RXO board unanimously approved the deal and recommends stockholders adopt the merger agreement. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027. Consideration terms, including any election mechanics, remain partially disclosed in the filing excerpt. Watch regulatory approvals and shareholder vote timing.

HPK.brief: HighPeak Energy filed an 8-K on October 6, 2026 disclosing two Securities Purchase Agreements for a newly created Series A 6.0% Perpetual Convertible Preferred Stock: 250,000 shares to PT Danantara Energy International and 200,000 shares to PT Tunas Harapan Perkasa, each at a $1,000 stated value, implying roughly $450 million gross. Terms include quarterly cash dividends starting at 6.0% cash/7.5% PIK, stepping to 7.5%/9.0% in year two, then 10.0%; conversion at $9.50; issuer redemption after year three at a 10% IRR; mandatory conversion if shares exceed 150% of the conversion price for thirty of forty trading days.

OPCH.brief: Option Care Health filed a preliminary proxy (PREM14A) on October 28, 2026, seeking stockholder adoption of its October 5, 2026 Agreement and Plan of Merger with Onyx Bidco LLC and Onyx Merger Sub, Inc., entities formed by investment funds managed by Clayton, Dubilier & Rice, LLC. Merger Sub will merge into Option Care, which survives as a wholly owned subsidiary of Parent, with holders receiving $32.05 per share in cash. The board unanimously recommends the deal, along with advisory say-on-golden-parachute and adjournment proposals. The special meeting will be virtual; the record date and meeting date remain bracketed. Watch appraisal-rights dissent levels, the shareholder vote timeline, and any competing indications of interest before the proxy is finalized.

HCSG.brief: Healthcare Services Group filed an 8-K on October 6, 2026, disclosing a Membership Interest Purchase Agreement to acquire all equity interests of NexDine, LLC and Xendella, LLC, collectively NEXDINE Hospitality, from Real Artisan Brands, LLC and other seller parties. Aggregate purchase price is approximately $93.5 million, subject to customary adjustments, plus contingent consideration tied to post-closing performance conditions, funded with cash on hand. The filing includes customary representations, warranties, covenants and termination provisions, with the purchase agreement and October 7 press release attached as exhibits.

TENX.brief: Tenax Therapeutics filed an 8-K on October 8, 2026, disclosing a temporary pause in enrollment for its Phase 3 LEVEL-2 trial of oral levosimendan (TNX-103) in PH-HFpEF to amend enrollment criteria based on completed LEVEL trial learnings; enrollment may resume per site as the amended protocol takes effect. The company also requested a Type C FDA meeting on levosimendan development and updated its investor presentation (Exhibit 99.1). No financial terms, stake, price, premium, board recommendation, advisor, or deal mechanics are stated. Watch regulatory feedback, protocol amendment timing, and any resulting financing needs.
