PINE.brief: Alpine Income Property Trust, via a wholly owned subsidiary of its operating partnership, filed an 8-K disclosing an October 5, 2026 Purchase and Sale Agreement with an unaffiliated institutional seller to acquire a 13-property industrial portfolio spanning 11 states for $117.3 million, subject to closing prorations. The $1.0 million earnest money became non-refundable on October 9, 2026, and the company now deems closing probable though conditions remain unsatisfied. No board recommendation or advisor is named, and no financing terms are disclosed. Watch closing conditions, financing and cap-rate disclosure on the pro formas.

STE.brief: STERIS plc disclosed that its wholly owned subsidiary, STERIS Corporation, signed an October 11, 2026 Purchase and Sale Agreement to acquire all equity interests of Xodus Medical, Inc., a Pennsylvania specialty surgical products business, plus related affiliates, for $2.1 billion cash at closing, subject to customary adjustments, with up to $150 million additional earnout tied to calendar 2028 performance targets. Sellers are Craig E. Kaforey and Mark A. Kaforey and their legacy trusts. Financing is primarily debt, supported by a $2.0 billion senior unsecured bridge facility committed by JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs. Closing is anticipated by December 31, 2026, subject to regulatory approvals; outside date July 12, 2027, extendable to January 11, 2028. Watch antitrust/regulatory timing, bridge syndication, and earnout mechanics.

THO.brief: THOR Industries filed an 8-K on October 13, 2026, announcing that its board declared an increased regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.54 per share, a 3.8% rise from the prior $0.52, payable November 10, 2026 to holders of record October 27, 2026. The filing includes the press release as Exhibit 99.1; no advisor or board recommendation beyond approval is disclosed. Mechanics are routine: a NYSE-listed common stock dividend with no overhang, collateral, or regulatory clock. Watch for future payout sustainability given RV demand cyclicality and tariff/input cost pressures.

LQDA.brief: Liquidia Technologies, a wholly owned unit of Liquidia Corporation, and United Therapeutics executed an October 13, 2026 settlement ending all patent, trade secret and contract litigation, including matters relating to U.S. Patent Nos. 11,824,327, 11,357,782 and 10,989,494 and the North Carolina Business Court case. Liquidia keeps marketing YUTREPIA for PAH but must delete the PH-ILD indication, halt PH-ILD promotion, and pay UTC $175.0 million net within 30 business days plus $145.4 million in two installments by January 31 and April 30, 2027. Releases vest only on payment, dismissals with prejudice and FDA label approval. Watch label-approval timing and installment funding.

ALXO.brief: ALX Oncology filed an 8-K disclosing privately negotiated exchange agreements dated October 14, 2026 with existing holders, under which 13,353,384 common shares were surrendered in return for pre-funded warrants on the same share count, settling about October 15, 2026. Participants included Blackstone Annex Master Fund (12,885,891 shares), RA Capital (213,667), and venBio Global Strategic Fund (253,826). Warrants carry a $0.001 exercise price, cashless exercise, and 4.99%/9.99% beneficial ownership blockers, increasable up to 19.99% only after 61 days' notice. Issued under Section 3(a)(9) exemption; the exchange is a balance-sheet/structural recapitalization maneuver that preserves economic exposure while recasting the register; watch for exercise-driven share overhang, registration rights, and future monetization or strategic alternatives.

CWCO.brief: Consolidated Water Co. Ltd. reported that its U.S. subsidiary PERC Water Corporation executed the Central Coast Blue AWPF Design-Build Agreement with the City of Pismo Beach, California, for an advanced water purification facility in Grover Beach. The fixed design-build price is approximately $39.8 million, awarded after a public two-step competitive procurement, covering design, construction, commissioning, warranties and 600 training hours. Initial capacity targets roughly 500 acre-feet per year, with optional Phase 2 expansion to 750 acre-feet not in current scope. This is an ordinary commercial contract, not a special situation; watch execution, change orders and cost-overrun risk.

DJCO.brief: Daily Journal Corporation filed an 8-K on October 15, 2026, reporting completion on October 13, 2026 of its acquisition of Austin, Texas-based Revir Technologies, Inc., whose AI-driven Scout platform helps law enforcement, prosecutors and corrections agencies manage, search and analyze large digital evidence collections. The deal was structured as a merger of a wholly owned Daily Journal subsidiary into Revir, funded with cash on hand; Revir will operate independently within Daily Journal's Courts, Justice, and Government Technology division alongside Journal Technologies, Inc. No price, share count or premium was disclosed, and the company stated the acquisition is not material to it.

RAIL.brief: FreightCar America filed an 8-K on October 14, 2026 disclosing a Stockholder Agreement with OC III LVS XII LP, OC III LVS XXVIII LP, and OC III LFE II LP, which collectively hold roughly 48.8% of common stock including warrants, per a July 2, 2026 Schedule 13D/A. The Company terminated its August 5, 2026 Rights Agreement, capped future poison-pill acquirer thresholds at no less than 20%, and imposed board review before transfers to any person exceeding 20% fully diluted. The 10-day review window and following 60-day completion period are structural mechanics to watch, given the 48.8% overhang and no advisor named.

LUCD.brief: Lucid Diagnostics filed an 8-K on October 16, 2026 disclosing receipt, on October 12, 2026, of a Nasdaq Listing Qualifications notice that its common stock closed below the $1.00 minimum bid price under Listing Rule 5550(a)(2) for 30 consecutive business days through October 9, 2026. Nasdaq grants a 180-calendar-day cure period ending April 12, 2027, requiring a $1.00 closing bid for at least ten consecutive business days; a further 180-day period may be available. Shares continue trading uninterrupted as LUCD; no board recommendation, advisor, or transaction terms are stated. The company says it will consider all options to regain compliance, including a potential reverse split. Watch for a compliance plan, any reverse-split announcement, and the risk of accelerated delisting if the bid stays sub-$1.

HLT.brief: Hilton Worldwide Holdings Inc. filed a Form 25 on 2026-11-04 to remove its common stock, $0.01 par value, from listing on the New York Stock Exchange and to withdraw registration under Section 12(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. The filing invokes Rule 12d2-2 and, per the document, reflects exchange compliance with its rules to strike the class; it is signed by EVP, General Counsel and Secretary Caroline Krass. No deal terms, board recommendation, advisor, price, premium or regulatory clock are disclosed. Form 25 is the US equivalent of a delisting notification; it is typically a precursor to deregistration and often follows a completed take-private or merger. Watch for the corresponding Form 15 and any merger proxy detailing consideration and closing conditions.

LNZA.brief: LanzaTech Global filed an 8-K reporting an October 14, 2026 Tranche 1 closing of a series of related recapitalization and deleveraging transactions at LanzaJet, a sustainable aviation fuel affiliate in which the Company holds a significant equity stake. LanzaJet issued $10 million of senior secured notes to Future Solution Investments, an entity affiliated with a large existing LanzaTech stockholder, under a facility permitting up to $25 million total; FPF guarantees. Investors exchanged FPF indebtedness, LanzaJet convertible notes, preferred stock and offtake rights for warrants to purchase senior-ranking LanzaJet preferred. LanzaTech also issued FSI-designated warrants on its own common stock. No board recommendation or advisor is named. Watch dilution from the LanzaTech warrant overhang, LanzaJet ownership reshuffling, and further tranche drawings against the $25 million cap.

MMS.brief: Maximus, Inc. filed an 8-K on October 20, 2026 disclosing that its wholly owned subsidiary Maximus Federal Services entered a definitive Equity Purchase Agreement on October 19, 2026 to acquire all outstanding equity of Agile Defense, LLC and certain affiliates from Arclight Equity Holdings, LLC. Consideration is $660 million cash, reduced by Agile indebtedness and transaction expenses, plus up to $50 million of contingent earnout payments tied to revenue milestones over the twelve months post-closing. Expected close is the first quarter of fiscal 2027, subject to HSR clearance and customary conditions; no shareholder vote is required. Watch regulatory timing and purchase-price working-capital adjustments.

SLGN.brief: Silgan Holdings filed an 8-K disclosing a November 6, 2026 Consent to Amended and Restated Credit Agreement with Wells Fargo as Administrative Agent, tied to the previously announced October 17, 2026 Transaction Agreement with A-VL Holdco, LP. Silgan will contribute its metal food/general line containers, metal and plastic vacuum closures, non-dispensing plastic dairy and aluminum roll-on closures businesses to newly formed Silgan Metal Packaging LLC. Lenders consented to MetalCo's Unrestricted Subsidiary designation, guarantor and equity-pledge releases, and limited-condition-acquisition covenant testing. Watch closing conditions and proceeds use for debt redemption.

VZ.brief: Verizon Communications filed a Form S-4 registration statement on October 20, 2026, covering offers to exchange newly registered notes for any and all of its outstanding original notes across eight series maturing 2028 through 2031, including 6.860% 2028s, 6.730% 2028s, 6.800% 2029s, 8.375%/8.000%/7.850%/7.875% 2029s and 8.300% 2031s. The filing registers exchange notes identical in terms to the originals, a routine registered-exchange mechanics step rather than a capital raise. No board recommendation, advisor, price per share, premium, collateral, ownership split or regulatory clock is stated. Watch for effectiveness and settlement timing; risk-arb relevance is minimal as this is a liability-management registration, not a change-of-control event.

AKBA.brief: Akebia Therapeutics filed an 8-K on October 23, 2026, disclosing receipt on October 21, 2026, of a Nasdaq Listing Qualifications staff deficiency letter under Listing Rule 5550(a)(2); the company's common stock closed below $1.00 for 30 consecutive business days, breaching the minimum bid price requirement. The notice has no immediate listing effect. Akebia has an initial 180-calendar-day period, through April 19, 2027, to regain compliance via a $1.00 bid for at least 10 consecutive business days. A possible second 180-day period requires meeting market-value and other initial listing standards and notifying Nasdaq of intent to cure, potentially via reverse split. No board recommendation, advisor or deal terms; no price, premium or ownership terms stated. Watch for reverse-split authorization and bid-price recovery.

EVEX.brief: Eve Holding, Inc. filed an 8-K under Item 3.01 on October 26, 2026, disclosing that on October 21, 2026 the NYSE notified and on October 22 publicly announced its determination to commence delisting proceedings for the company's public warrants (EVEXW) and to immediately suspend trading in them, citing abnormally low selling price levels under Section 802.01D of the Listed Company Manual. Each warrant remains exercisable for one share of common stock at $11.50. The NYSE will apply to the SEC to delist the warrants after applicable procedures. Common stock (EVEX) trading is unaffected. Watch warrant liquidity, exercise economics versus the $11.50 strike, and any acceleration or redemption mechanics.

PRG.brief: PROG Holdings filed an 8-K (Items 8.01/9.01) disclosing a board-declared quarterly cash dividend of $0.14 per share, payable December 1, 2026 to holders of record November 17, 2026, with a press release attached as Exhibit 99.1. No advisor or board recommendation language beyond the declaration; no buyback authorization, special dividend, or structural terms were disclosed. This is a routine recurring quarterly capital return, not a tender or special distribution. What to watch: any future increase, special dividend, or repurchase authorization signaling a shift in capital allocation.

CFR.brief: Cullen/Frost Bankers, Inc. filed an 8-K on October 29, 2026, disclosing that, with Board authorization, it notified the NYSE of its intention to voluntarily delist its common stock (CFR) and its 4.450% non-cumulative perpetual preferred depositary shares (CFR.PrB) and transfer both listings to the Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE). Trading on the NYSE is expected to end at market close on November 11, 2026, with TXSE trading beginning at market open on November 12, 2026, under the same symbols. No price, stake, premium, advisor, or break fee is stated. The move is an exchange transfer rather than a transaction; watch index-inclusion effects, liquidity migration, and any spread dislocation around the November 11-12 transition.

ABOS.brief: Acumen Pharmaceuticals filed an 8-K on two items tied to a pipeline wind-down. On November 3, 2026 it noticed voluntary full prepayment of its K2 HealthVentures term loan, paying roughly $23.3 million cash on hand on November 5 covering principal, accrued interest, a $1.6 million final fee and lender expenses; all liens and the lender's conversion right were released. Separately, following its October 30, 2026 announcement to cease sabirnetug development (including the ALTITUDE-AD open-label extension) and evaluate strategic options, the board approved exit/disposal costs. Watch remaining cash runway and strategic-review outcome.

IBM.brief: New York Stock Exchange LLC filed Form 25-NSE on 2026-11-02 notifying the SEC of its intention to delist and deregister International Business Machines Corp's 0.30% Notes Due 2026, a $42.0 billion principal class. The removal proceeds under 17 CFR 240.12d2-2(a)(2) because the entire class was redeemed, paid at maturity, or retired on 2026-11-02; trading was suspended the same day, with delisting effective at the opening of business on November 13, 2026. No price, premium, board recommendation, or advisor applies — this is a routine debt-listing termination, not a change-of-control event. Watch for confirmation the notes were fully retired and any residual registered debt overhang.

CVI.brief: CVR Energy filed a 424B5 prospectus supplement for a 10,515,248-share common stock offering priced at $47.55 per share, raising roughly $500 million ($490 million net before expenses), with a 1,577,287-share greenshoe. Proceeds, plus cash and other financing, fund an unspecified Acquisition, redemption of the 2028 Notes, and fees. The offering is not contingent on the acquisition closing; absent a deal, proceeds go to general corporate purposes. Barclays and Jefferies are joint book-running managers. Watch acquisition terms and financing closing risk.

DDD.brief: 3D Systems filed an 8-K disclosing privately negotiated exchange agreements with all holders of its 5.875% convertible senior secured notes due 2030. It will exchange $92.03M principal for $20M cash plus accrued interest, 13,471,138 common shares, and $85M of new 3.30% convertible senior unsecured notes due 2031, converting at ~$3.43/share, a ~30% premium to the $2.64 NYSE close on November 4, 2026. No advisor or board recommendation disclosed. Closing is targeted around December 2026; watch deleveraging, dilution and noteholder conversion overhang.

ANIP.brief: ANI Pharmaceuticals filed an 8-K on November 5, 2026, disclosing a 364-day senior bridge facility of up to $676 million with JPMorgan Chase as administrative agent, entered November 4, 2026, to fund its recommended public cash offer for all outstanding shares, the 2023:1 convertible loan and 2023/2033:1 warrants of Sweden's Egetis Therapeutics AB (a Swedish public cash tender offer, the US-equivalent of a tender offer/acquisition). The facility is initially unsecured, becoming guaranteed and secured by substantially all assets upon funding, priced at ABR+1.75% or SOFR+2.75%. Watch funding conditions and Egetis acceptance levels.

FIX.brief: Comfort Systems USA filed an 8-K on November 5, 2026, disclosing that its board approved an amendment increasing its stock repurchase authorization to top off the program at up to 1,000,000 shares, adding 994,606 shares to the previously authorized 11,757,964. Through November 4, 2026, the company had repurchased 11,752,570 shares for an aggregate $1,711,769,315, exclusive of excise tax. Repurchases may occur in the open market or privately negotiated transactions, funded from available cash, at management's discretion; the board may modify, suspend, extend, or terminate the program at any time. No price, premium, or advisor was specified; watch execution pace against cash generation and buyback's support for per-share metrics.

DTE.brief: DTE Energy filed an 8-K disclosing a November 1, 2026 Purchase and Sale Agreement to sell all equity interests in wholly owned subsidiary DTE Energy Resources, LLC (d/b/a DTE Vantage) to Velocity BidCo LLC, a Delaware vehicle owned by institutional investors advised by J.P. Morgan Asset Management's Global Infrastructure group. Consideration is $2,970,672,573, subject to cash, debt, working capital, capex and transaction-expense adjustments. DTE's board unanimously approved on October 30, 2026. Closing requires HSR clearance, FERC Section 203 authorization and Canadian Competition Act clearance (advance ruling certificate or waiting-period expiry/non-objection). Watch regulatory timing and purchase-price adjustments.

FCAP.brief: First Capital, Inc. filed an 8-K on November 4, 2026 disclosing a definitive Agreement and Plan of Merger under which First Bancorp of Indiana, Inc. will merge into First Capital, with First Federal Savings Bank merging into First Harrison Bank. Consideration is 0.3075 First Capital shares per First Bancorp share, a fixed exchange ratio, valuing the deal at approximately $33.2 million based on First Capital's 20-day VWAP of $63.05 as of November 4, 2026. Cash is paid in lieu of fractional shares. First Bancorp's board will recommend approval and solicit proxies; no advisor is named. What to watch: shareholder and regulatory approvals, plus arbitrage sensitivity to First Capital's share price given the fixed ratio.

LPTH.brief: LightPath Technologies filed an 8-K announcing the October 30, 2026 closing of the previously announced sale of 100% of its wholly owned Chinese subsidiary, LightPath (Zhenjiang) Optical Instrumentation Co., Ltd. (LPOIZ), including its manufacturing facility, to an entity owned by LPOIZ's incumbent management team. No purchase price, premium, or advisor was disclosed in the excerpt. Post-closing, LightPath has no China-based facilities or operations, reinforcing its NDAA-compliant, Western-aligned manufacturing footprint across the U.S. and Europe. LPOIZ will continue supplying LightPath as a third-party vendor for continuity; China third-party revenue averaged roughly $4.5 million annually across fiscal 2025-2026 and drops out of consolidated results. Watch supply-continuity and revenue-dis-synergy risk on the now-smaller base.

LNN.brief: Lindsay Corporation, a Delaware-incorporated NYSE-listed farm equipment maker, filed an 8-K disclosing a cooperation agreement dated November 4, 2026 with the Vision One fund entities, settling a previously noticed activist campaign. Lindsay will nominate Marvin E. Washington as an independent director at the fiscal 2027 annual meeting for a term expiring at the fiscal 2030 meeting, recommend and solicit proxies for him, and appoint him to the Audit Committee. Board size is capped at nine; Vision One gains replacement rights while meeting a minimum ownership threshold. Vision One irrevocably withdrew its October 5, 2026 nomination and proposal notice and ceased solicitation. Management also agreed to submit binding proposals to declassify the board. Watch for the ownership threshold and standstill terms in the full agreement, and whether declassification passes.

RHLD.brief: Resolute Holdings Management filed an 8-K reporting third-quarter 2026 results and disclosing that its board authorized an increase of its share repurchase program to $100.0 million, with no expiration date. Repurchases may occur via open market, privately negotiated transactions, tender offers, or other methods at management's discretion, sized by market conditions, liquidity and alternatives. No price, share count or premium is stated; the program is non-binding and may be modified, suspended or discontinued anytime. Watch execution pace, buyback-driven EPS accretion and any signal of undervaluation.

XMTR.brief: Xometry filed an 8-K (Item 8.01) disclosing a notice of redemption for all approximately $85.0 million outstanding principal of its 1.00% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027, issued under a February 4, 2022 indenture with U.S. Bank Trust. The redemption date is November 20, 2026, at 100% of principal plus accrued interest from August 1, 2026; holders may convert until 5:00 p.m. New York time on November 19, 2026, at 17.8213 shares per $1,000 (plus 0.0018 make-whole shares), settled physically. Watch conversion-driven share dilution and noteholder election dynamics.

ANDE.brief: The Andersons, Inc. disclosed an 8-K on November 3, 2026 that its wholly owned subsidiary, Andersons Renewables, LLC, entered a Merger and Equity Purchase Agreement to acquire all outstanding limited partner interests in Harvestone Low Carbon Partners, LP via blocker-entity purchases and a merger of Heartland Merger Sub into HLCP, which survives as a wholly owned subsidiary. Total purchase price is $915 million, including normalized working capital, subject to adjustments. HLCP operates three low-carbon ethanol facilities in North Dakota and Indiana with roughly 215 million gallons annual capacity. Financing blends long-term debt and revolver borrowings, backed by a commitment letter from U.S. Bank and Farm Credit Mid-America. Closing is targeted Q4 2026 or early Q1 2027, subject to regulatory approvals; the Company guarantees subsidiary obligations. Watch regulatory timing, definitive debt documentation, and purchase-price adjustments.

ATMU.brief: Atmus Filtration Technologies filed an 8-K on 2026-11-06 reporting third-quarter 2026 results and disclosing that its board approved a new share repurchase authorization of up to $300 million of common stock, effective immediately. The new program replaces the prior authorization, which had $28.9 million remaining. Repurchases may occur in the open market or privately negotiated transactions, including Rule 10b5-1 plans, funded from operating cash and cash on hand; no expiration date, no obligation to buy, suspendable at any time. The prior buyback's unused capacity was effectively retired. Watch pace of execution versus prior residual authorization and any signal on share-price view.
